Property developer Andreas Christopheros, 29, was severely injured in a December acid attack outside his Truro home, leaving him with life-changing injuries. His husband David Phillips, 48, is charged with grievous bodily harm with intent, while Nicole Phillips, 45, faces charges of perverting the course of justice.

In Lastres, a Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route, signs depicting a squatting figure with a "no entry" symbol have been placed to discourage pilgrims from defecating along the path. The signs, which have become a tourist attraction, are in response to complaints from residents about pilgrims defecating near their homes. The municipality lacks adequate public facilities for pilgrims, leading to this unconventional solution.

A fire consumed a building in Flint, Michigan, that previously housed a strip club called The Body Shop. The blaze started around 1pm and produced thick smoke and large flames, affecting only the building and nearby power lines. Local officials are investigating the cause, and this is not the first fire at the site.

Shoshana Hebshi, a woman of Arab and Jewish descent, received $40,000 in compensation after being strip-searched at Detroit Metropolitan Airport on the 10th anniversary of 9/11. The federal government and Frontier Airlines settled a lawsuit filed by the American Civil Liberties Union, addressing Hebshi's claim of ethnic profiling.

A plane making an Asiana Airlines flight from Seoul to Hiroshima experienced a tailstrike and skidded off the runway, injuring 20 people. The Airbus A320 overran the runway after missing the landing point, causing a hard landing and deploying evacuation slides. The airport was closed, and emergency services responded to the crash, which is being treated as a crash landing.

Mark-Francis Vandelli, a 26-year-old from Made In Chelsea, boasts an impressive collection of 16 expensive watches, including a £32,000 Cartier white gold Moonphase and a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42, valued at £6,500. His collection, which he updates annually, reflects his wealthy background and taste in luxury timepieces.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy, 89, is auctioning over 200 antiques, including a 3D diorama of the Battle of Agincourt and a medieval longbow, to downsize his home. The collection, valued at £100,000, includes furniture, paintings, and historical items reflecting his interests in literature and military history. The auction, organized by Dominic Winter, takes place this Saturday in Gloucestershire.

Brazilian commuter Nelson Felippe posted a photo on Facebook of two women hugging on a train platform, initially expressing disapproval and concern about public behavior, but the post was later revealed to be a clever commentary on public safety, specifically about following rules, rather than homophobia.

A 16-year-old English cricket fan named Jonathan Stevenson received a detailed letter of advice from legendary spinner Richie Benaud about left-handed leg spin almost 20 years ago. Stevenson shared the letter on Twitter as a tribute after Benaud's death, highlighting Benaud's expertise and the lasting impact of his guidance.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg envisions a future where virtual reality will revolutionize travel, allowing users to experience the world's most breathtaking locales without leaving home. This vision, supported by Facebook's acquisition of Oculus and plans to integrate VR into its newsfeed, could make long-haul flights a thing of the past, with users able to explore destinations in immersive 3D environments.

A boyfriend, Guo Kai, arranged for professional wedding photographs to be taken for his girlfriend, Dong Hui, on her 22nd birthday, despite her being bedridden in hospital due to bone cancer. The photos served as a romantic gesture and a dream come true for the couple, who met a year ago and planned to get married soon.

A 34-year-old man, Blaine Boudreaux, killed two people and injured others in three separate drunk driving collisions in Houston within three hours, including the death of a 6-year-old boy, Joshua Medrano. Boudreaux, with a history of DUIs, has been charged with intoxication manslaughter and other offenses.

Microsoft has launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions at its Redmond campus, partnering with Specialisterne. The initiative, announced by Mary Ellen Smith, aims to expand opportunity and create a diverse workforce. This move follows Microsoft's efforts to address past criticisms, including CEO Satya Nadella's controversial comments about women's pay.

Two deputies involved in the fatal arrest of Eric Harris in Tulsa, Oklahoma, have been reassigned due to safety concerns after threats were made against them and their families. The deputies, who pinned Harris' head to the ground as he said he was losing breath, are not charged but face criticism. The sheriff's office has suspended its drug unit and is reviewing the shooting, pending the outcome of the case against Reserve Deputy Robert Bates, who is charged with second-degree manslaughter.

Katie Prager, 24, with cystic fibrosis and an infection, needs a lung transplant but Kentucky Medicaid won't cover the out-of-state treatment. Her husband, Dalton, 23, who has already received new lungs, is pleading for help to save her, as doctors predict she won't live a year without a transplant.

Using data from the Sleep Cycle app, researchers found that people wake up earliest on Mondays in South Africa, while the worst mood occurs on Tuesdays in the US. Wednesday nights show the best sleep quality globally, with China leading. Thursdays see the latest wake-up times in the Middle East, and Americans report the happiest wake-up moods on Fridays.

Auction house Doyle New York is set to sell a collection of 25 unpublished love letters from Frida Kahlo to her lover Jose Bartoli, expected to fetch over $120,000. Written between 1946 and 1949, the passionate letters reveal Kahlo's adoration for Bartoli and insights into her personal life, including her relationship with Diego Rivera.

Len McCluskey, Unite's fiery leader, campaigns warmly for Labour but his union remains a potent, sinister force in British politics, seeking to impose 1970s-style socialism. With significant influence over Labour candidates and a history of militant strikes, Unite's grip on the party is concerning, especially given McCluskey's admiration for that era. This union-Labour link, often overlooked, poses a threat to modern governance with its push for expanded public sector, higher taxes, and less workplace flexibility.

Zookeeper Elad Hershkowitz filmed animals drinking from water troughs using a GoPro camera for 30 hours, capturing unique and humorous drinking behaviors from various species, including a rhino that almost kisses the water and a lemur that delicately licks it.

A poll shows that only 25% of voters believe David Cameron is most eager to win the election, compared to 43% for Ed Miliband. Despite Cameron's efforts to appear more passionate, Miliband is seen as more enthusiastic by voters. Nicola Sturgeon and Nigel Farage are also perceived as more engaged in the campaign.

Zaur Dadaev, one of five Chechen men accused of assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov, retracted his confession in court, claiming he was beaten and pressured into confessing. Human rights activists have documented signs of torture on Dadaev. Nemstov, a Putin critic, was shot near the Kremlin in February, sparking protests.

A photo of four-month-old Sonit Awal being rescued from the rubble after a 7.8-magnitude earthquake in Nepal became a symbol of the disaster, which killed over 5,000 people. Sonit was trapped for 22 hours before being found by soldiers who lifted him to safety, finding him uninjured despite the ordeal.

A Church of Scientology-backed organization, Narcocon, is trying to turn a 40-acre wooded property near Camp David into a drug rehab center, despite current zoning laws prohibiting medical use. They aim to have the land designated as historic to circumvent these laws, but opponents view this as a trick and cite past legal issues with Narcocon. The rehab program uses sauna therapy and vitamin Niacin, costing over $30,000 per month.

In post-American presence Kabul, five Afghans who spoke English, a valuable skill during NATO's time, now face unemployment and fear, sleeping in market stalls and avoiding family visits due to potential reprisals. Meanwhile, Kabul's landscape has changed dramatically, with empty streets and abandoned foreign enclaves, reflecting the city's new reality post-NATO.

Two US Navy SEALs died and one was critically injured while swimming in a pool at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story in Virginia. The incident occurred during regular training, with one SEAL pronounced dead at a hospital and the other in critical condition. An investigation is underway, and the base commander expressed condolences to the families and teammates.

NBC, with the live rights to the Premier League in the USA, expects to have more live viewers in the US than in Britain soon. This season, they have transported their entire production to England to enhance coverage, with anchor Rebecca Lowe and other experts providing analysis at key matches. Lowe, a Crystal Palace fan, has helped increase US interest in the Premier League, with replica shirts now common across the country.

Boris Johnson verbally attacked Ed Miliband on the Andrew Marr Show, claiming Miliband would do "more damage to the country than he did to his brother." The encounter turned into a heated exchange, with Miliband laughing it off. Johnson also criticized Labour's potential coalition with the SNP, saying Miliband would have to take help from the Scottish party, making it impossible for him to govern in the UK's interests.

Dustin Irons, a prisoner in Oregon, was sentenced to an extra 30 days in jail for flashing a judge during a video court hearing, despite being handcuffed. The incident occurred when Irons became disgruntled with the proceedings. Captain Stewart Harp praised Irons' creativity in the act.

Jenson Button believes McLaren has made significant progress, now competing with midfield teams like Force India, Sauber, and Lotus, after a strong performance in Malaysia despite retirements. Button hopes further improvements will allow them to challenge these teams in this weekend's Chinese Grand Prix, though cooler temperatures in Shanghai may affect their performance.

The Fiona Stanley Hospital in Perth faced severe scrutiny after blood and bone fragments were discovered on supposedly sterilised medical instruments, leading to the removal of its medical service provider and a fine. The hospital's reputation is further damaged by ongoing issues despite previous problems and a recent patient death.

Becca Litchfield and Dale, from Nottingham, sacrificed their dream wedding to fund one last IVF attempt, which led to them winning a wedding competition and eventually giving birth to twins. This unexpected turn of events allowed them to achieve both their dreams of having children and getting married.

A family coffee shop in Omaha, Scooter's Coffee, had its Facebook page hacked for 24 hours, displaying pornography after an employee clicked a malicious link. The hack, similar to breaches of other major brands, was only resolved after contacting other businesses to intervene with Facebook. Scooter's issued an apology to its customers.

A Shibu Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club center attempted to bark but mostly squeaked and squawked, creating a humorous scene with a young husky. The video shows the playful, high-pitched vocalizations and laughter from onlookers, highlighting the puppy's efforts to communicate. Canine vocalization typically develops from grunts and whines to barks over several weeks.

Liam Plunkett, a 29-year-old England seamer, aims to challenge the West Indies batsmen with his pace in the upcoming Test series, seeking to earn a spot in the team by outperforming Chris Jordan and Mark Wood. Recovered from an ankle injury, Plunkett trains hard to be the fastest bowler and plans to "rough up" batsmen when needed.

Paul Smith is set for a third fight against a reigning super-middleweight champion, Andre Ward, who is using Smith as a warm-up before potentially facing Carl Froch. The WBA has ordered a unification fight between Ward and Froch, but Ward prefers to box in London rather than Nottingham. Froch is also considering a fight against Julio Cesar Chavez Jr. in Las Vegas.

In Parma, Missouri, the election of the city's first black mayor, Tyrus Byrd, was overshadowed by the sudden resignations of most of the police force, the city attorney, clerk, and water treatment supervisor, all citing safety concerns. The outgoing mayor and Byrd's father deny any issues with the police, and residents question the need for such a large police force for a town of 713 people.

Manchester City will make Yaya Toure available this summer but are open to him staying, despite interest from Inter Milan and his high wages. Toure, a key player for City's recent successes, remains committed to the club but a potential contract extension is being discussed. Meanwhile, City will not allow Valencia to pull out of the deal for Alvaro Negredo to fund a move for Radamel Falcao.

A new study finds that over two-thirds of people taking antidepressants do not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder, suggesting widespread overprescription. The research, published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, indicates that antidepressants are commonly used without clear evidence-based indications.

Doris Fuller's daughter, Natalie, who suffered from bipolar disorder and psychosis, took her own life at 28. Fuller, in a Washington Post article, detailed how Natalie's condition went undiagnosed until her early 20s and worsened, despite treatment. Natalie, described by her mother as the bravest person she knew, struggled with terrifying voices that urged self-harm.

A 10-year-old boy named Koby Hodder suffered a cardiac arrest during a game of British Bulldog at school, collapsing and losing consciousness for 12 minutes. Teachers performed CPR until paramedics arrived and saved his life using a defibrillator. The incident has led to calls for the game to be banned due to its perceived danger, and Koby was later diagnosed with a heart condition similar to that of footballer Fabrice Muamba.

Britain's most senior female judge, Baroness Hale of Richmond, calls for divorce laws in England and Wales to be overhauled, removing the need for allegations of blame and encouraging couples to resolve child and financial arrangements before divorce. This would involve a one-year cooling-off period and aims to reduce bitterness in matrimonial disputes.

Tottenham Hotspur are planning a £400 million stadium with a retractable pitch to accommodate an NFL franchise, potentially giving the league a permanent London base. The new 65,000-capacity stadium could better suit American football needs than Wembley's 90,000 seats, though Wembley retains its iconic status.

A group of U.S. senators has urged FIFA to move the 2018 World Cup away from Russia, citing its role in the Ukraine crisis. The senators argue that hosting the event would bolster President Putin's regime and contradict international sanctions. England is considering a bid for the 2028 European Championship but is unlikely to participate in the 2026 World Cup while Sepp Blatter remains FIFA president.

Universal has set "Fifty Shades Darker" for release on February 10, 2017, and "Fifty Shades Freed" for February 9, 2018. EL James's husband, Niall Leonard, will write the second film's script. Dakota Johnson and Jamie Dornan are negotiating for higher pay following the first film's massive success.

Tony Pulis, despite his reputation for keeping teams in the Premier League, has never managed to finish in the top half of the table in his seven seasons, currently leading West Bromwich Albion in another relegation battle. His record includes notable successes like promotion with Stoke and turning around Crystal Palace, but he faces tough fixtures that could jeopardize their position.

Fenerbahce has called for the suspension of the Turkish championship after their team bus was attacked by gunfire, wounding the driver. The bus was on its way from Rize to Trabzon airport following an away match. The club demands justice and a suspension until the culprits are found and punished.

A massive avalanche hit Everest Base Camp, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens more. The video captures climbers scrambling for safety as a snow cloud engulfs the camp. Rescue efforts are complicated by aftershocks and impassable icefall routes, leaving hundreds of climbers stranded. Helicopters are bringing stranded climbers down, but the situation remains critical.

At 87, Gregory Margolin, a WWII veteran who survived the Nazi invasion, found himself surrounded by war again in Ukraine. His family, including his granddaughter Liora, fled to Israel after a missile hit their home, killing his daughter. This wave of Ukrainian Jewish immigration to Israel coincides with ongoing conflict in Eastern Ukraine.

John Carver, Newcastle's assistant manager, recalls how Ruud Gullit's controversial decision to bench key players in a 1999 Tyne-Wear derby led to Gullit's resignation after a loss. Carver, vying for the head coach position, is aware of the significant impact a victory over Sunderland could have on his prospects.

Reverend Al Sharpton addressed a North Charleston church congregation about the Walter Scott case and called for policing reform, meeting with local officials including Mayor Keith Summey. Sharpton is also attending a vigil near where Scott was shot. He denied allegations that he was barred from Scott's funeral, stating he was not invited due to his scheduled convention.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers will speak to Raheem Sterling about his recent controversial behavior, including inhaling nitrous oxide and smoking a shisha pipe, and remind him of his responsibilities as a professional after Sterling scored the opening goal in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United.

Labour received over £1 million in union donations during the second week of the election campaign, more than doubling the Conservatives' £492,512. Union contributions, including over £700,000 to Labour, far exceeded donations to other parties, highlighting the significant financial support Labour is receiving from trade unions.

Passengers on a Qatar Airways flight from Doha to Manchester revolted after being stranded for five hours on the tarmac in Birmingham due to severe winds. Police were called twice as passengers became frustrated. The plane eventually took off for Manchester, but passengers faced further delays and some waited up to 24 hours. Qatar Airways apologized for the delay, citing weather conditions and crew limitations.

Canadian pop star Justin Bieber will accompany Floyd Mayweather into the ring for his high-stakes fight against Manny Pacquiao, following their long-standing friendship. Bieber has previously joined Mayweather on stage and into the ring for other fights, and will now lead the fighter's entourage at the MGM Grand. This fight is being billed as the biggest in boxing history, with Mayweather aiming for a 48th win.

Corinthian Colleges, a notorious for-profit college chain, is shutting down all 28 of its campuses, marking a significant step in holding such institutions accountable. These colleges, which rely heavily on federal student aid, often exploit low-income students with dubious degrees and high debt. With student loan defaults at alarming rates, there's a push to close down these schools and forgive debts for affected students.

Pep Guardiola denied a dispute with former Bayern Munich doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit after blaming the medical staff for the team's Champions League defeat by Porto. Guardiola took responsibility for the loss but maintained there was no personal feud, while Muller-Wohlfahrt cited damage to trust.

Wladimir Klitschko, 39, prepares for his world title defense against Bryant Jennings at Madison Square Garden, reflecting on his Olympic gold win in 1996 that transformed his life. Klitschko, who has reigned as heavyweight champion for 15 years, believes age is an advantage and is confident in his performance despite being close to 40.

Jeremy Clarkson, fired from Top Gear for attacking a producer, admitted he would miss hosting the show. Former presenter Angela Rippon expressed interest in returning to the motoring show. The future of Top Gear remains uncertain as BBC tries to retain co-presenters James May and Richard Hammond.

In Barcelona's 1-0 La Liga win over Celta Vigo, Celta striker Fabian Orellana was sent off after throwing a lump of grass at Sergio Busquets, hitting him in the neck. The incident occurred as tempers flared in the closing stages of the match, with Orellana also remonstrating with the referee. Barcelona secured crucial points, with Jeremy Mathieu scoring the only goal.

Federal Judge George A. O'Toole warned jurors in the Dzhokhar Tsarnaev bombing case to avoid the Boston Marathon and related events during the sentencing phase, which begins April 21. Tsarnaev was convicted on all 30 counts, including using weapons of mass destruction, and faces the possibility of the death penalty. The sentencing phase is expected to last four weeks.

Tens of millions of Chinese people honored their ancestors during the Tomb Sweeping Festival (Qingming Festival), cleaning graves, burning paper money, and offering food. The festival, marking the start of spring, also includes celebrations like a grand ceremony in honor of the Yellow Emperor in Shaanxi Province, involving dancers and symbolic acts. This three-day holiday, one of 24 Chinese solar terms, sees extensive travel and outdoor activities.

Paul Simon, 73, has topped the UK album charts with "The Ultimate Collection," outselling albums by younger artists like Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. This marks his first UK number one album since 1990. The success is attributed to his recent tour with Sting, which received positive reviews.

Iker Casillas, despite potential competition from David de Gea, insists he will stay and fight for his spot as Real Madrid's first-choice goalkeeper. Casillas, who has been with Real Madrid since 1996, is focused on helping the team defend their Champions League title, emphasizing his commitment to the club until the end of his contract.

Britain's employment reached a historical high of over 31 million, with the number of jobs increasing by 557,000 in a year. The International Monetary Fund and German finance minister praised Chancellor George Osborne's economic strategy, crediting it for reducing the deficit and boosting employment. Prime Minister David Cameron hailed this as a 'jobs miracle,' while warnings were issued about Greece's potential impact on the global economy.

SsangYong, known as 'two dragons' in Korean, is launching the Tivoli SUV in the UK starting from £12,950, aiming to compete with the Nissan Juke. The Tivoli offers various trim levels and features, including a five-year warranty and a 'My Tivoli' personalization program. Citroen's Aircross model features protective alloy bumps front and side, inspired by indestructible toy cars, to enhance its rugged appearance.

Chef Sam Longhurst at Splendid Kitchen in Manchester created a massive burger called "The Whole Damn Farm," weighing 1 kg and standing 10 inches tall, featuring six types of meat and 2,000 calories, priced at £13.50. Inspired by a customer's challenge, the burger includes two beef patties, bacon jam, ham, chicken, pulled pork, and bacon, making it a spectacle for diners.

Yeo Valley's staff canteen, overseen by a Michelin-trained chef, offers high-quality, organic, and locally sourced meals to dairy workers for as little as £2. The menu changes daily and includes gourmet dishes like soft-poached quail egg and confit tomato. Now open to the public, it has been praised as the world's best staff canteen.

B.B. King, the legendary blues guitarist, was hospitalized for dehydration caused by his Type II diabetes but has since been discharged and is resting at home with his grandchildren. He thanked fans for their concern and remains optimistic about his health. King, 89, is known for his hits like "The Thrill Is Gone" and his custom-made Gibson guitar named Lucille.

On Easter Sunday, New York's Fifth Avenue hosted an Easter parade featuring a wide array of bizarre and colorful hats, from bunny ears and floral bonnets to elaborate dioramas and ship-shaped headpieces, reflecting a mix of religious and secular participation in the annual tradition.

The East of England Ambulance Service received numerous prank and inappropriate calls, including reports of a squirrel hit by a car, a bleeding burger, and excessive food consumption, among others. These calls, totaling 1,248 in two years, potentially diverted emergency resources away from genuine medical emergencies.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake won an Audi football challenge against Loic Remy and Willian, despite Willian accidentally breaking a car's wing mirror during the long-range shooting competition.

Brendan Rodgers criticizes Raheem Sterling's advisor for potentially manipulating the player, suggesting Sterling would prefer to stay at Liverpool if left to decide on his own. Rodgers has spoken to Sterling about his contract situation and believes staying at Liverpool is in the player's best interest for now, despite Arsenal's interest.

Rachel Riley was embarrassed on Countdown when contestants provided the double entendre "erection" as an answer, causing Nick Hewer to struggle to contain his laughter. This incident is part of a recurring pattern where rude words have caused similar reactions from the hosts, including previous instances with Carol Vorderman.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, UK, was spared jail time after attempting to buy deadly poison online to commit suicide. Covert counter-terrorism officers, tracking his dark web activity, arrested him before he could obtain the poison. He received a 12-month referral order, with officers hoping he can get the support needed to turn his life around.

Lianne Hindle, 37, died from a cardiac arrest three hours after giving birth to her daughter Poppy at North Manchester General Hospital in December, prompting calls for action to prevent further tragedies. This incident, along with nine other deaths at the hospital and two at Royal Oldham Hospital, led to an investigation. Lianne's partner, Chris Barnes, expresses concern over the care she received and advocates for improved safety measures in maternity units.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after training while eight months pregnant. Pittman, a two-time world champion hurdler, continued rigorous training throughout her pregnancy, planning to compete in the Beijing World Championships and the 2016 Rio Olympics. She used an IVF donor to conceive Emily and has been praised for her dedication and careful management of her training.

A powerful storm capsized several sailboats during the Dauphin Island regatta in Alabama, resulting in at least one death and four people missing. The storm scattered boats across Mobile Bay, and rescue efforts continued through the night. Participants described near-capsizing and the severity of the unexpected gale-force winds.

Roseanne Barr revealed she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma, which are worsening her vision. These conditions, often affecting those over 60, can be genetic and are progressive. While there is no cure, treatments can delay progression and reduce risks. Protecting eyes from UV exposure is recommended to prevent these diseases.

A 17-year-old, Chancey Allen Luna, was convicted of first-degree murder in the 2013 shooting death of Australian college baseball player Christopher Lane while Lane was jogging. The jury recommended a life sentence without parole, though the defense argued Luna only intended to scare Lane.

Arsene Wenger insists Arsenal's upcoming match against Jose Mourinho's Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium will focus on performance rather than their history of poor results against each other. Despite Arsenal being 10 points behind Chelsea, Wenger sees this as a chance to close the gap. The game also marks the return of former Arsenal player Cesc Fabregas to the Emirates Stadium.

Manny Pacquiao, a Filipino boxer who rose from poverty to become a global icon, is set to face Floyd Mayweather in a highly anticipated fight. Pacquiao's journey began in Manila at age 14, where he trained in a local gym and won his first 10 professional bouts. Now 36, he has faced some of the biggest names in boxing and is poised for what could be his biggest win yet.

Jack Grealish, an outstanding Aston Villa player, was photographed using nitrous oxide, joining other top-tier athletes who have engaged in this behavior. Despite his talent, his use of the drug could hinder his career. Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger emphasized the importance of professional athletes making healthy choices to maintain peak performance.

Sam Barton, who spent £55,000 on cosmetic surgery to resemble Joey Essex, was attacked by a group who pelted him with eggs after he checked into a pub on Facebook. Barton believes the attackers tracked him down using his social media posts. He has also faced online bullying and had to move house due to his appearance.

Manchester University in Indiana was placed on lockdown late Friday night due to a "likely prank call" about an armed individual near the administration building. Police, a bomb squad, and Indiana State Police responded but concluded it was a prank. Students were advised to shelter in place, and no injuries were reported.

Edinson Cavani, known as "El Matador," faces the challenge of leading Paris Saint-Germain past Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals, with key PSG players out and Barcelona's star-studded attack. Cavani, despite his reputation, has struggled recently, going seven matches without a goal before scoring twice in a recent match.

Derry Mathews won the interim WBA lightweight title with a unanimous points decision over Tony Luis in Liverpool. The fight was filled with Luis's aggressive style, but Mathews controlled the early rounds and maintained a tight victory, despite both fighters being deducted a point in the eighth round for infractions.

Hull secured a surprising 28-20 victory over St Helens, ending the home team's three-game winning streak. Early tries by Hull, including one from Jamie Shaul, were crucial, while St Helens struggled with injuries and substitutions, ultimately falling behind despite a strong second-half performance.

The U.S. immigrant population, both documented and undocumented, is projected to reach a record high of 51 million by 2023, accounting for 14.8% of the population. By 2060, it could grow to 78 million, making up 82% of total population growth and reaching 18.8% of the population. This surge is expected to significantly alter demographic trends, with immigrants and their descendants projected to account for most of the U.S. population growth over the next few decades.

Jack Wilshere led Arsenal Under 21s in a 1-0 loss to Reading, with Niall Keown scoring the winning goal for Reading in the 8th minute. Despite Wilshere's and Abou Diaby's returns from injury, neither team could find an equalizer.

Justin Rose, who has been in the world's top five for the past three years, fell outside the top 10 after a poor performance in Florida. However, he showed encouraging signs at the Shell Houston Open, hitting 17 out of 18 greens and scoring a 69. Rose attributes his recent struggles to technique issues and is optimistic about his performance heading into the Masters.

A mansion in Mayfair, once a milking parlour, is now on the market for £25 million. The 8,139 square foot property, built in 2011, features modern luxuries like an indoor pool, gym, and cinema room. Its unique history as a dairy site in central London adds to its appeal.

Bayern Munich, despite several key injuries, remains confident and united, according to Thomas Muller. The team, chasing a treble, is focused on the strength gained from recent tough matches and aims to score against Porto in the Champions League. Coach Pep Guardiola acknowledges Porto's quality but remains optimistic about Bayern's chances.

Mercedes drivers Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited the team's Brackley base to strategize against Ferrari after Vettel's victory in Malaysia. The visit followed a surprising performance where Ferrari's Vettel outperformed both Mercedes drivers, highlighting the need for a new strategy for the upcoming Chinese Grand Prix.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to use nitrogen gas for executions, should lethal injection become unavailable. This method, which causes unconsciousness within 8-10 seconds and death from oxygen deprivation, has never been used in U.S. executions. The move comes as Oklahoma's executions have faced scrutiny, with the latest taking 43 minutes.

Bafetimbi Gomis led Swansea to a 3-1 win over Hull with two goals, including an overhead kick, and topped this week's EA Sports Performance Index with a score of 52.9. Other top performers include Charlie Austin (52.2), Eden Hazard (51.7), and Ander Herrera (51.5), as Premier League action continued with exciting goals and performances.

A Russian freezer trawler, the Dalny Vostok, sank in the Sea of Okhotsk, killing at least 56 of its 132 crew members and leaving 13 missing. A massive rescue operation involving over 1,300 people is underway, with 63 survivors rescued and 56 bodies recovered. The ship sank quickly after a heavy fishing net was pulled in, flooding the engine compartment.

Clinical trials show that olaparib, a drug originally for women with BRCA gene mutations, can benefit men with advanced prostate cancer, delaying disease progression in up to 30% of cases with specific genetic defects. This PARP inhibitor targets cancer cells with DNA repair mutations, offering a more precise treatment with reduced side effects.

Rhiannon Taylor, a 29-year-old travel photographer from Australia, turned her passion for globetrotting into a successful business called 'In Bed With', where she reviews and photographs luxurious accommodations worldwide. With over 12,000 Instagram followers, she documents the best beds, pools, and room service, generating income from hotel stays, photo sales, and partnerships with travel product companies.

A five-day-old hippopotamus was killed during a fight between two adult hippos in South Africa's iSimangaliso Wetland Park. The calf's mother watched helplessly as the baby was thrown into the air and dragged through the water. The mother likely stayed with her herd, believing it was safer, but her decision proved fatal for the calf when one of the adults grabbed and killed it.

The Football Association is investigating an incident at QPR's home game against Chelsea, where Chelsea players were hit by objects thrown from the crowd. QPR is reviewing CCTV footage and appealing for witnesses to help identify the culprits, who could face bans.

A young mother, LaTasha Gosling, and her three children were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. The suspect, known to the family, was found dead hours later, not from homicide. The family has started a GoFundMe page to raise money for funeral services, having already exceeded their initial goal.

Labour politician Emily Thornberry faced criticism for opposing the right to buy policy while renting out a property she bought from a housing association, now worth nearly £1 million. Her hypocrisy was highlighted by opponents, who accused her party of being out-of-touch. Thornberry defended her stance, arguing that the policy should ensure like-for-like replacements.

Mike Lane, joint master of the Tedworth Hunt, was severely beaten by masked protesters during a fox hunt in Wiltshire. Despite a wealth of evidence and a video of the attacker, police have dropped the investigation, citing insufficient evidence. This decision has angered hunt supporters and the victim, who feels let down by the police.

Valencia's Andre Gomes insists he will stay at the club, despite links to Manchester United and Chelsea. The 21-year-old midfielder, who has scored four goals in 25 La Liga appearances, says he is happy at Valencia and focused on the upcoming season. He denies being contacted by Chelsea and states his agent is unaware of any transfer offers.

An Australian teenager, Audrey Pekin, was raped twice by a man named Henry Alafu during a Christmas holiday in Bali. Alafu lured her to his home and then followed her in a taxi, despite her attempts to escape. Indonesian police failed to detain Alafu, who later returned to Nigeria.

Ashley James, a former Made In Chelsea star, is part of a PETA campaign against Harvey Nichols for reintroducing fur products, using a fake mutilated fox in the campaign to highlight animal cruelty. Harvey Nichols previously had a ten-year anti-fur policy but recently changed its stance. James advocates for informed consumer choices and ethical practices.

Chile has enacted a new law recognizing same-sex civil unions, which will take effect in six months and provide legal rights to cohabiting same-sex couples, similar to those of heterosexual couples. The law, signed by President Michelle Bachelet, aims to end discrimination and will benefit an estimated 2 million people, though marriage equality remains illegal in Chile.

Chelsea is on track to become the most dominant Premier League title winner in a single season, having led the table for 230 days, just 12 short of Manchester United's record of 262 days set in 1993/94. They currently lead by seven points with a game in hand, facing key matches against QPR, Manchester United, and Arsenal.

Cape Verde, a small island nation with a rich musical heritage, is leveraging its cultural assets to boost its economy. Despite lacking natural resources, the country is promoting music and the arts as key sectors for development. The Kriol Jazz Festival, among other initiatives, aims to attract international artists and visitors, potentially turning Cape Verde into a cultural hub and driving economic growth.

An old hoax video of a wave rider surfing near Sydney's Opera House resurfaced and went viral again after recent storms. The video, originally posted in 2012, was debunked by wave experts who said it's impossible for waves to reach that area.

Birmingham defeated Reading 1-0 in a Championship match, with Clayton Donaldson scoring the winning goal in the 89th minute. Reading, despite dominating much of the match, wasted several chances, while Birmingham defended stubbornly. This loss comes after Reading's FA Cup semi-final defeat to Arsenal, with Reading now focused on avoiding relegation.

Paris Saint-Germain's David Luiz suffered a hamstring injury during a match against Marseille and will miss at least four weeks, including both legs of the Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona. The injury could also impact PSG's Ligue One title defense, as Luiz is set to miss up to eight crucial matches.

The return of Game of Thrones has led to a significant surge in internet piracy, with over 100,000 illegal downloads per day and seven million episodes illegally downloaded between February and April. This marks a 45% year-on-year increase, with Brazil leading in illegal downloads. HBO has responded by launching a new streaming service, HBO Now, in an attempt to curb piracy.

Leicester City, fighting for survival, will face West Ham United at King Power Stadium. Key absences include Matt Upson for Leicester and Andy Carroll for West Ham. West Ham's Winston Reid returns from injury, while Leicester's Jeff Schlupp might be rested. West Ham is favored to win, with odds of 2/1, while the match has a long history with West Ham having won the last seven league meetings against Leicester.

Residents of Celoron, NY, are highly critical of a statue of Lucille Ball unveiled in 2009, deeming it an unflattering and "monstrous" depiction. The statue, based on Ball's intoxicated pitch from "I Love Lucy," has sparked a Facebook campaign for its removal, despite the artist's refusal to comment. The estimated cost to recast the statue is between $8,000 to $10,000.

Sharon Smith, who weighed nearly 20 stone and struggled to fit in airplane seats, lost 4.5 stone after standing for 11 hours during a flight to Hong Kong. This experience prompted her to join a slimming club and start running, eventually dropping to 9 stone 9 pounds and running a 10k race.

Nicola Bonn, a London-based mother of 14-month-old Poppy, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences and reduce new mothers' feelings of cluelessness and self-doubt. Her viral post highlights the overwhelming opinions and judgments new mothers face, emphasizing the need to stop justifying every decision.

Two 17-year-old boys from Dewsbury, Yorkshire, believed to have traveled to Syria to join ISIS, have gone missing, causing shock and concern for their families. The boys, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, left for Turkey during Easter holidays under false pretenses. Their families, including a relative of one boy who was previously convicted for terrorism, are urging the public for information and praying for their safe return.

Stephanie Scott, a school teacher from Leeton, was found murdered days before her wedding. Her father, Robert, describes her as joyful and thoughtful, with plans for a perfect wedding that now serve only as reminders of her loss. The couple had been preparing for their wedding, including taking dance lessons together. The high school where she taught has become a memorial site.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is interested in signing Feyenoord players Tonny Vilhena and Jordy Clasie, with Vilhena ready to leave Feyenoord after one year, while Koeman also aims to make Eljero Elia's loan move permanent, as the club looks to strengthen ahead of potential European qualification.

The National Trust has replaced antique furniture with beanbags at Ickworth House in Suffolk as part of an experiment to engage visitors, sparking controversy among heritage experts. Similar experiments will be conducted at nine other sites. The Trust aims to enhance visitor experience by encouraging interaction, though critics argue it is patronizing.

Former Prime Minister John Howard was photographed helping his driver change a flat tire in Sydney, with Howard standing on the footpath while the driver worked. Howard chatted with a passerby who recognized him and offered assistance, and even agreed to a selfie. This incident contrasts with a recent challenge faced by Liberal MP Christopher Pyne, who was asked to change a tire on national television.

Tony Pulis acknowledges Joey Barton's criticism of West Brom's mental fortitude after a 2012 match where they lost a 2-0 lead. Pulis, who has improved the team's performance, recalls his own experience of losing a match despite a two-goal lead. The teams face off again at the Hawthorns, with West Brom showing improved results and solid performances.

In the Democratic Republic of Congo, researchers have captured the first photo of the Bouvier's red colobus monkey, thought extinct for over 50 years, in Ntokou-Pikounda National Park. This discovery, along with the recent identification of the white-cheeked macaque in Tibet, highlights the ongoing efforts to rediscover and document rare primate species.

Kim Kardashian, Kanye West, and their family are on an eight-day visit to Armenia, the country of Kim's father's birth, where they are receiving a star treatment and exploring local landmarks. They are staying at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan in Yerevan, a city known for its cultural richness and Soviet-era architecture. The visit includes stops at the Yerevan Opera House and the historic Geghard Monastery.

British expats Patrick and Valerie Jubb are facing the demolition of their property in Jimena de la Frontera, Spain, due to illegal alterations made by a previous owner, despite obtaining a certificate stating no infractions. This dispute is complicating their plans to move back to the UK and sell the property, which they purchased in 2008.

Apple reported record-breaking first-quarter results, with over 61 million iPhones sold, generating $58 billion in revenue and $13.6 billion in profit, up 40% from the previous year. Sales in China surpassed those in the US, and while iPad and Mac sales declined, the iPhone remains the company's primary driver of success.

A 3-year-old girl, Elisa Tyler, has been having nightmares about a white van since her mother's fatal car accident. Her father suspects the van may be connected to hit-and-run incidents involving a white box truck in the area, raising doubts about the official accident report.

Researchers at New York University found that the brain can better remember neutral events when they are linked to emotions, a process that enhances memory through emotional arousal and affects brain regions like the amygdala and hippocampus. This study highlights how emotions strengthen both positive and negative mundane memories over time, pointing to the adaptive nature of human memory.

Jahnae Jackson, girlfriend of 18-year-old Jackson Byrnes, has put her studies on hold to care for him after he was diagnosed with a stage four brain tumour. The tumour has left Jackson paralysed and unable to dress himself. With community support, they have raised over $80,000 for surgery by renowned neurosurgeon Dr. Charlie Teo, though they still need additional funds for rehabilitation.

Nedum Onuoha, a QPR centre-back, is attracting interest from Hull City, Everton, and West Ham United, with Hull also showing interest in West Bromwich Albion striker Victor Anichebe, who is likely to be sold this summer. QPR is considering squad streamlining due to potential relegation.

The Yale University researchers have mapped out unique sentence structures and phrases across the United States, revealing regional variations such as "I ain't never had no trouble with none of 'em" in Florida and "All of my clothes needs washed" in Idaho. This project highlights how different regions have their own grammatical systems and sentence structures, which can be quite different from standard English.

A Canadian man, Kalman Kallai, traveled from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia for work by dragging a green rocking chair behind him in a trailer, capturing scenic views and amusing moments along the 2,796-mile journey.

Manager Tim Sherwood joked about a letter from six-year-old Aston Villa fan Charlie Pye, who applied for the job after Paul Lambert's dismissal. Sherwood revealed he had received a Twix multi-pack as a "win bonus" in reference to Pye's request for sweets and chocolate, playfully thanking the young fan.

Kell Brook attended the Premier League Darts in Sheffield, where Dave Chisnall won two matches to move to second place in the table. Chisnall defeated Gary Anderson and James Wade, while Michael van Gerwen maintained his lead with an 8-2 win record.

Marco Verratti praises Zlatan Ibrahimovic's crucial off-field support for Paris Saint-Germain, highlighting his role in helping teammates and young players, despite scoring 17 goals in Ligue 1. Ibrahimovic was suspended for the first leg of the Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona but will play in the return match.

A secret RAF Aerodrome Manual for the Falklands Islands, containing vital GPS coordinates and technical details, was mistakenly published online by the Ministry of Defence, potentially aiding Argentina in any military action. The document could serve as an "invasion handbook" and was accessed by the public before being removed. Tensions have risen due to Argentina's leasing of Russian SU-24 bombers, capable of attacking the Falklands without refueling.

Huddersfield Giants coach Paul Anderson aims to improve his team's offensive play to boost their Super League standing, following a poor run of results. Despite their strong defense, the Giants have dropped from third to ninth place. Anderson takes responsibility for the team's offensive struggles and hopes a win against Catalans Dragons can turn their season around.

Planners in Windsor have approved the opening of a second Costa cafe within a short walking distance of an existing one, bringing the total to three within a mile. The new location replaces a former bank, and a Costa Express is also nearby. While some residents are concerned about the proliferation of coffee shops, others see it as a sign of the area's growth.

The British Veterinary Association has withdrawn support for shooting free-running badgers in controversial culls, instead advocating for trapping and shooting. This decision comes as the Environment Secretary promises more culls if the Conservatives win the election, despite criticism from wildlife groups. The culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire have had mixed results, with only sufficient badgers culled in Somerset to potentially reduce TB in cattle, while the number in Gloucestershire fell far short.

Geoff Barrow, Portishead's founder, criticizes streaming services for low royalty payments, despite his band's songs receiving 34 million plays. He supports streaming but advocates for better compensation for musicians, especially for younger artists. Jay-Z's Tidal service offers higher payouts to artists but comes at a higher cost to consumers.

The first four episodes of Game of Thrones' fifth season have been leaked online, appearing on torrent sites before the official premiere. This follows the show's history of heavy piracy, with episodes from its first four seasons being illegally downloaded over seven million times. HBO is investigating the leak, which originated from a press group, while the company attempts to combat international piracy through simultaneous global premieres and new streaming services.

Daniel Buccheri, a Melbourne singer, composed an emotional song for his brother Adrian's wedding, touching on their childhood and Adrian's new marriage to Sarah. The speech, performed at Poet's Lane in Sherbrooke, Melbourne, went viral with over 100,000 views, and moved guests to tears.

Zara Phillips, after giving birth to her daughter Mia, surprised by the difficulty in regaining her fitness, has committed to a strict morning exercise routine on an exercise bike and a healthy diet to prepare for the 2016 Rio Olympics. She aims to be part of the eventing team, balancing training with time around horses for her young daughter.

Raheem Sterling's interview about not signing a new contract at Liverpool upset many fans, who feel he is ungrateful given the club's support. Sterling's performance has been inconsistent, and while he has potential, fans are divided on whether he should stay or go, with some welcoming his departure.

A photograph from the early 2000s shows Jose Mourinho and Pep Guardiola, both assistants at Barcelona under Bobby Robson, in deep conversation with other future managers like Laurent Blanc and Julen Lopetegui. This image highlights the rich history of Barcelona nurturing future football managers, with many from the 1996-97 team going on to coach in the Champions League.

Former Manchester United star Eric Cantona claims Paris Saint-Germain's Javier Pastore is the best player in the world, praising his creativity over Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. Pastore, who cost PSG £29 million, has impressed Cantona with his passing and ability to surprise opponents, despite lower goal-scoring figures compared to Messi and Ronaldo.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murder after dismembering his tenant Michael Spalding and dumping the body parts in a canal. Simon, with his girlfriend Michelle Bird, 35, helped in the disposal. Bird was cleared of murder but admitted to assisting an offender.

Health experts are using "loneliness maps" to identify areas where elderly and others are at risk of social isolation, a condition as harmful as smoking 15 cigarettes a day. Two UK counties, Essex and Gloucestershire, have implemented these maps, which combine data on demographics, health factors, and resident surveys to pinpoint vulnerable zones. The Campaign to End Loneliness recommends this approach to tackle loneliness nationwide, citing its potential to reduce healthcare burdens.

Judy Eddingfield, 65, celebrated 50 years of working as a waitress at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, a job she calls her "home away from home." She started at 15 and has seen the restaurant through half a century, meeting her husband there and serving iconic figures like 'Leave It to Beaver' actors. Winstead's, open since 1940, has been a constant in Eddingfield's life.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not return to the national team immediately, even if he performs well for Surrey, as other players are playing well and Gatting questions Pietersen's ability to rebuild trust. Gatting also comments on Alastair Cook's poor performances and suggests that more questions will be asked of the captain if he fails to score runs against West Indies.

A 17-year-old student developed an app called 'Uploader for Instagram' that allows users to upload photos to Instagram from their computers, potentially violating Instagram's terms of service. Instagram has demanded the app be changed, but the student argues this would render the app useless. The incident highlights the challenges of using APIs while maintaining platform integrity.

Hoesik, a common Korean practice of company dinners often involving alcohol, is a significant part of workplace culture. It is seen as a way to build relationships and understand colleagues better. Foreigners must navigate this tradition, which can be challenging but is crucial for professional success. Etiquette includes deferring to seniors, never leaving a glass empty, and pouring for others before drinking.

The Duke of Kent, 79, was discharged from Aberdeen Royal Infirmary after being treated for a dislocated hip sustained at Balmoral estate. He was seen leaving with a walking stick alongside his daughter. The injury occurred just two years after he had a mild stroke.

The Surfers Paradise Meter Maids, a 50-year tradition in Queensland, faces potential end due to local business leaders arguing they are outdated and no longer provide a public service. However, Meter Maids defend their role as an integral part of the Gold Coast's tourism experience.

Greece denies it will fail to pay a £330 million loan to the IMF, stating it will make the payment on time. Reports suggested the country was considering a parallel drachma currency, but this has been denied. The government is prioritizing wages and pensions, and may face a furore in markets if it defaults to the IMF. Germany's finance minister warns that Greece must pay on time to avoid eurozone exit concerns.

A Turkish court has blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after the social media platforms refused to remove images of a prosecutor killed during a hostage siege by a terrorist group. The images upset the victim's family, and the court ordered the blocks to prevent further sharing of the graphic content.

A 7-year-old Star Wars fan, Colin Gilpatric, wrote to George Lucas about the Jedi rule against marriage, fearing it might lead to the "dark side." Lucas responded, affirming that selfless connections are key to staying on the path of the light and allowing marriage. Colin was thrilled to receive a package from Lucasfilm with Star Wars merchandise and the heartfelt letter.

Wisconsin defeated Kentucky 71-64 in a tense semi-final to reach the NCAA Tournament final, ending Kentucky's undefeated season. Duke also advanced with an 81-61 win over Michigan State. Both teams will compete for the national championship at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis.

The article discusses the varied and often controversial performances of the American national anthem by famous artists, highlighting instances where performances were praised or criticized, from Vince Neil's recent rendition to Whitney Houston's iconic Super Bowl performance, Roseanne Barr's booed version, Jimi Hendrix's psychedelic take, and Michael Bolton's word-for-word recitation.

Security footage has been released showing Barry Lyttle delivering a single punch to his brother Patrick, causing Patrick to fall unconscious and nearly lose his life outside a Sydney bar. Barry, from Belfast, pleaded guilty to grievous bodily harm and faces up to two years in jail. The brothers, who had only recently reunited for a holiday, are now facing the consequences of their violent altercation.

The parents of conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, who died 19 days after birth, were devastated to find their gravesite at Pinegrove Memorial Park in Sydney cleared of all mementos and flowers, with items thrown in the rubbish. The family had built a small shrine over 11 months, but everything was removed without notice, leaving them heartbroken and mortified.

Britain's Supreme Court President, Lord Neuberger, suggests courts should allow full-face veils for Muslim women, advocating for sensitivity towards cultural differences and respect. This comes amid debates over the place of traditional Muslim dress in legal settings, following a 2003 case where a woman was jailed for refusing to remove her veil. Neuberger also calls for judges to understand and address the intimidating nature of court proceedings for ordinary people.

Andre Cole, 52, was executed by lethal injection in Missouri for killing Anthony Curtis in 1998 over child support disputes. The execution proceeded despite Cole's claims of mental illness, and he declined a last meal. Cole's all-white jury convicted him, and Governor Nixon denied a clemency petition.

Prince Harry will depart the UK for Australia without meeting his new niece or nephew, who is overdue in birth. He had hoped to meet the royal baby before returning to his duties, but will now see the new arrival in May. Meanwhile, excitement builds over the expected birth of the second child to Prince William and Kate, with bets placed on various details of the baby's arrival.

Florida man Justin Jackson has been accused of an eight-year fraud scheme, posing as celebrities including Oprah Winfrey, Reggie Love, and Madonna's manager to obtain free items and job recommendations, totaling over $2.4 million in value. Jackson and co-conspirator Angel Agarrat are facing lawsuits from Oprah's network and others.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini is asking €50 million for Paulo Dybala, likening him to Lionel Messi and attracting interest from top clubs including Paris Saint-Germain, Manchester United, and Chelsea. Inter Milan's Roberto Mancini was seen scouting Dybala, but PSG is seen as the frontrunner, with Zamparini setting a high price to ensure Dybala's future in Serie A.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians are protesting against President Dilma Rousseff due to an economic downturn and a corruption scandal at Petrobras, the country's state-run oil company. The protests, which have grown in size and diversity, call for Rousseff's impeachment, while her supporters defend her and argue the opposition is elite-driven. Rousseff has acknowledged the need for reform but denies personal involvement in the corruption.

Former Manchester United player Eric Cantona has defended his involvement in the film "You and the Night," insisting it is an artistic piece rather than pornographic, and praising its aesthetic value. The film includes racy scenes, one of which shows Cantona on his hands and knees in just his underwear, alongside actress Beatrice Dalle.

Psychologists have found that listening to certain music can enhance the flavors of food and drink. For instance, The Beatles' music complements fish and chips, while specific classical pieces can heighten the taste of wine and desserts. Behavioral psychologist Charles Spence explains that our ears can influence our taste perception, a phenomenon he calls "digital seasoning."

Raheem Sterling has postponed contract talks with Liverpool until the summer, despite a £100,000-a-week offer, to focus on the season. PFA chief Gordon Taylor supports Sterling's decision, noting it's not disloyal and could be wise to wait until the end of the season. Sterling is linked with moves to Arsenal and Spanish clubs, and has recently scored for England.

An Ohio woman, La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, discovered her birth mother, Francine Simmons, worked at the same call-center and lived just six minutes away after accessing her birth records. They eventually met and learned Mitchell-Clark has three younger sisters.

Oscar 'Papoo' Hernandez Jr, a gun trafficker, pleaded guilty to weapons charges related to sending weapons to Aaron Hernandez, who was convicted of murdering Odin Lloyd. Papoo, awed by Hernandez's fame, shipped the guns in April 2013, a month before Lloyd's killing. Papoo faces up to 30 months in prison and claims he was beaten by fellow inmates after being incorrectly listed as a government witness.

A Florida man, Joel Parker, was arrested for throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head after threatening and disrupting the ride. Parker asked the driver if he wanted a Snickers but when declined, he threw the candy at the driver. He was arrested for battery, posted $250 bond, and received a trespass warning, barred from using the bus again.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has discussed pre-season plans with striker Saido Berahino, indicating the club plans to retain him beyond the summer transfer window. Berahino, 21, has expressed a desire to play in the Champions League and was linked with a move in January, though West Brom were open to a £20 million bid. Pulis praises Berahino's attitude and performance, suggesting he sees a future for the player at the club.

Giovanni Lo Porto, an Italian aid worker, was abducted and later killed in a U.S. drone strike in Pakistan in 2012 while working on reconstruction efforts post-flooding. A project manager for Welthungerlife, Lo Porto was remembered for his passion and commitment to humanitarian work. His colleagues and family expressed pride in his efforts and mourned his loss.

A photographer in Florida captured images of hundreds of sharks, believed to be Blacktips and Spinners, swarming just offshore, prompting concerns among beachgoers. The sharks were migrating north to breed in shallower waters, with sightings continuing for several days.

An 11-year-old German Shepherd named Zeus, a retired K-9 officer from the Ridgefield Police Department, was honored with a grand procession before being euthanized due to severe health issues. The tribute, attended by fellow officers and residents, celebrated Zeus's eight years of service, during which he assisted in over 250 narcotics arrests and helped locate 50 missing or wanted individuals.

Reports of child sex abuse have surged by over 60% since 2011, with nearly 9,000 cases reported in 2014, particularly in South Yorkshire where there was a 577% increase. However, the number of arrests has decreased by 9%, prompting criticism of the government's handling of child abuse cases.

Iceland has become a popular filming location, hosting scenes from hit TV series and movies like Game of Thrones, Interstellar, and Prometheus. Notable filming spots include Thingvellir National Park, Svartalfheim, and the Svinafellsjokull glacier, each providing unique and stunning natural settings. Directors appreciate Iceland's diverse landscapes, from dramatic cliffs to powerful waterfalls and vast glaciers, which enhance the visual appeal of their productions.

In Australia, unique historic properties are fetching high prices. A 19th-century bathing box sold for $276,000 in Melbourne, breaking records. A heritage-listed mechanic’s garage in Sydney sold for $1.2 million to be converted into a home. And a 19th-century maximum security prison in Victoria is on the market for $2 million after being renovated into a residence.

Samantha Rawcliffe, 40, lost control of her body and crashed her car after a rare brain disorder, functional neurological disorder, was diagnosed. She now struggles with severe symptoms, including loss of bladder control, inability to walk, and reliance on medication, severely impacting her life and job.

The controversial "Scary Lucy" statue in Celoron, New York, which depicts Lucille Ball in a frightening manner, has prompted the sculptor, Dave Poulin, to offer to create a new, more flattering statue for free. The original statue, based on a moment from "I Love Lucy," has been criticized by residents and fans alike. Poulin admits to being disappointed in his work and taking ownership of the poor decision to cast and display it.

David Alaba, Bayern Munich's left-back, is ruled out for around seven weeks due to a torn knee ligament, missing crucial games including the Champions League quarter-finals. The 22-year-old, who had earlier recovered from a similar injury, expressed disappointment but aims to return for the season finale. Alaba, known for his excellent form, will start rehabilitation in about a month.

Beatrice Nokes, 21, and 37-year-old Daniel Williams, a suspended police officer, face charges related to running a prostitution ring in London. Nokes, daughter of respected solicitors, is accused of grooming women for sex work, while Williams is charged with voyeurism and hiding profits. Both appeared in court, facing multiple charges including causing or inciting prostitution and misconduct in public office.

A firm called Sequester is offering to sell personal and medical data, including details of eating disorder sufferers and plastic surgery patients, for as little as 12p per record. This data, obtained from a business partner of Alchemy Direct Media, has prompted investigations by multiple regulatory bodies. Concerns are raised about the potential misuse of such sensitive information by unscrupulous firms and criminals.

Jordan Spieth won the Masters at Augusta, becoming the second-youngest champion and the fifth to lead from start to finish. Despite the victory, he missed his sister Ellie, who has autism and couldn't attend. Spieth credits her with providing him perspective and shaping his upbringing, emphasizing her support and impact on his life.

Dick Advocaat, learning from his past mistake of downplaying the Old Firm derby, emphasizes the importance of the upcoming Wear-Tyne Derby for Sunderland, who are struggling to avoid relegation. Despite the pressure, Advocaat focuses on securing three points, acknowledging the significance of fan support in boosting team performance.

A dispute erupted in Sydney when Belinda Bartholomew, girlfriend of rugby player Aidan Guerra, claimed she was racially abused at a Bondi butcher. She says she was sworn at and told to leave; the butcher denies this, citing eftpos issues and claiming she was rude.

Cadbury has reduced the size of its Freddo Frog from 15g to 12g while keeping the price the same, citing increased manufacturing costs. This move follows a previous reduction in the size of their Dairy Milk family blocks. Customers have expressed anger and disappointment on Cadbury's Facebook page, questioning the company's motives.

Hillary Clinton's campaign is set to launch with a values statement emphasizing humility, discipline, and a focus on prosperity, aiming to avoid past mistakes. The campaign will officially announce on Sunday via social media, with plans to visit Iowa and New Hampshire.

Kyli Wilfson, 29, battled chronic pancreatitis for over a year and a half, unable to eat despite feeling perpetually hungry. Initially misdiagnosed, she finally received the correct diagnosis at 28. The condition, affecting less than 0.01% of people, led to her dropping to 80lbs and requiring a feeding tube. Support from a Facebook group helped her cope with the lifelong condition.

Memes from the leaders' debate featured Labour leader Ed Miliband in various humorous contexts, including being superimposed over a rapper and posing like Titanic's Jack. The images also showed David Cameron and Nick Clegg on a Gogglebox sofa, while Scottish National Party leader Nicola Sturgeon appeared with a skeptical face. These memes reflected the tense and sometimes confrontational tone of the debate.

Amir Khan, a British boxer, is set to potentially face Manny Pacquiao in a fight in Abu Dhabi, after initially being close to fighting Floyd Mayweather. Khan, who recently received a presidential award, sees this as a dream fight and Arum, Pacquiao's promoter, views it as an outstanding opportunity. The fight could happen if there's no rematch between Mayweather and Pacquiao.

A 5ft wide, two-bedroom home in Islington, London, has sold for £750,000, despite its narrow dimensions. The property, described as "well proportioned" by the estate agency, features a maximum width of 8ft 8in and includes two bedrooms, a kitchen, and a garden. The high price reflects significant interest in small, characterful homes in the area.

Nicola Sturgeon is launching a SNP manifesto with policies aimed at forming a power-sharing deal with Labour, including tuition fee cuts, NHS changes, and recognition of Palestine. The SNP's proposals, totaling £180 billion over five years, could give them significant influence in a hung parliament, potentially leading to constitutional changes similar to those in early 20th-century UK politics.

Celtic won the Glasgow Cup 2-0 against Rangers in a match played at Hampden Park, with goals from Josh Kerr and Mark Hill. Rangers' goalkeeper Robby McCrorie made two costly errors, allowing Celtic to take the lead and secure the victory. The match was played behind closed doors due to recent fan troubles, with no major off-field incidents reported.

Tony Pulis, manager of West Bromwich Albion, led his team to a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace while maintaining his distinctive pre-game attire of cap, track suit, and white trainers, despite the high-profile nature of the match. Pulis insists on this look, stating it keeps him close to the action, and believes in his unique style, which has also helped secure the team's safety in the Premier League.

Television presenter Jameela Jamil, 29, spent £3,000 replacing her amalgam fillings with white ones after experiencing health issues for seven years, which were linked to high mercury levels from the fillings. Despite concerns, dental experts argue that the amount of mercury released is minimal and there is no significant risk from amalgam fillings.

Suge Knight, facing murder charges, appeared confident in court but was later wheeled out in a wheelchair. He hopes Floyd Mayweather will bail him out after Mayweather's upcoming fight. Knight's attorney believes Mayweather, a close friend, will help. The trial is set to begin on July 7.

TV chef Gizzi Erskine's British shorthair, Kimchi, has a discerning palate, loving human foods like taramasalata and poppadoms. For a cat magazine shoot, Gizzi set up a lavish feast including caviar and seafood sculptures, though Kimchi is on a diet due to her love for such treats. Her new cat, Ponzu, also enjoys unusual human foods, like green curry from a Thai takeaway.

Martin Springall, father of the girl in a viral photograph featuring mysterious black boots, says he has no idea what the boots are and insists the image was not Photoshopped. The photograph sparked debate on Reddit, with some doubting its authenticity. Springall, living in Tokyo, took the photo of his shy daughter in Zushi, Japan, in 2014.

Under Tory plans, foreign workers will pay £22,000 in tax before accessing UK benefits, and unemployed EU migrants will be banned from claiming benefits for four years, with a six-month job search requirement. These measures aim to curb EU migration and will be part of negotiations with the EU, with a referendum on the deal scheduled for 2017.

Eight-year-old Cody Neatis, who has multiple disabilities, has been forced to sleep on the floor for seven nights in Royal Preston Hospital due to a lack of suitable specialized bed. His mother, Lynne, has slept with him to watch over him, fearing he might injure himself or pull out his oxygen. The hospital has been criticized for not having the necessary equipment, despite previous promises to provide one.

The Masters golf tournament is set to begin, with highlights including Ian Poulter forgetting his golf clubs, Henrik Stenson recovering from flu, Tiger Woods playing with his children, and the anniversary of Gene Sarazen's famous albatross shot. Other traditions like the ball-skipping contest at the 16th hole add to the excitement.

Juventus has ruled out signing Manchester United's loan player Radamel Falcao due to his high wages. The club remains interested in Palermo's Paulo Dybala and Paris Saint-Germain's Edinson Cavani as forward reinforcements.

If re-elected, David Cameron plans to sell £4 billion worth of Lloyds Bank shares to the public at a discount, aiming to pay down national debt, in the largest UK privatisation since the Thatcher era. This move follows other Conservative policies inspired by the 1980s and aims to remind voters of the economic challenges under the previous government.

Living near congested roads increases the risk of 'silent strokes,' which can lead to brain shrinkage and raise the risk of dementia, according to a study of over 900 people. The research links exposure to fine particulate matter from traffic and factories to a 46% higher risk of silent strokes, underscoring the need for better air quality regulation.

Jessica Ainscough, 30, died in February from epithelioid sarcoma, after choosing unconventional Gerson Therapy over conventional treatments. Her fiancé, Tallon Pamenter, revealed she underwent radiation in her final weeks, a risky but brave decision. Despite the treatment's success in shrinking her tumor, complications led to her death. Pamenter praised her partner's courage and grace throughout her battle.

A multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway near Fernvale involved ten people, including four children. Three individuals were airlifted to Princess Alexandra Hospital with serious injuries, while six others were taken to Ipswich Hospital with minor injuries. Emergency crews freed one trapped person using hydraulic tools, and the highway remains closed with diversions in place.

Jason McDonald, a gator handler at Colorado Gator Farm, walked a slackline over a pool containing over 50 alligators, some up to 10 feet long, as a daring new way to interact with the creatures. Despite initial reservations, the alligators showed little concern. McDonald plans to walk over larger gators and even albino ones, though he acknowledges the danger and his mother's concerns.

The son of a Syrian imam, Abdul Hadi Arwani, who was shot dead in London, may have met his killer days before the murder while seeking a building quote. The imam, an opponent of Syrian President Assad, was targeted due to his links with the Muslim Brotherhood and activism against the regime.

In Hong Kong, there's a craze for Jenny's butter cookies, with people lining up for hours to buy them at $9 a tin. The popularity has led to knockoffs and reselling at high mark-ups, while the original store warns against fake products. This cookie frenzy is part of a global trend where foods like cronuts and ramen burgers have sparked similar manias, though often short-lived.

Kira Hollis, a 27-year-old mother from Tamworth, overcame anorexia and depression through bodybuilding after being diagnosed with borderline personality disorder. Now a healthy 9.5st and a personal trainer, she credits the sport with giving her confidence and purpose. Her six-year-old daughter Olivia and boyfriend Michael Dennis also played crucial roles in her recovery.

Jockey Lewis Ferguson, 18, survived a spectacular double somersault fall during a race, which went viral online. Despite the fall, Ferguson returned to mucking out stables and remains undeterred from his racing career, aiming to compete in major events like Cheltenham and Aintree.

Hillary Clinton launched her 2016 campaign with a video and road trip aimed at rebranding herself and reframing her image as more empathetic and relatable. Critics dismissed her launch as vapid, but her campaign may be successfully projecting a more confident and forward-looking image, akin to successful product launches by companies like Nike and Apple.

More than 1,700 Chinese high school students in Yichuan, Shaanxi province, took their exam in the school playground due to lack of indoor space, organizing the unusual outdoor test themselves. To prevent dizziness from sunlight, students rotated their chairs and desks. This novel approach aims to test their organizational skills and broaden their horizons.

A reader can win a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Joe Hart, England and Manchester City goalkeeper, along with a Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor and shaving gel in a competition ending April 19.

Kecil, a baby orangutan rejected by two mothers, found a loving surrogate in Maggie at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. After a tense period, Kecil and Maggie formed an inseparable bond, with Kecil relying on Maggie for comfort. Kecil will make his first public appearance this weekend, following a 10-month period under Maggie's care.

Noelle Baynham, a 61-year-old woman from Winchester, Hampshire, died after an accidental overdose of medication and was partially eaten by her pet dogs, which became desperate for food after she was undiscovered for days. Her friend Grant Donovan made the horrific discovery when he entered her home and found her body. The cause of death was likely an accidental overdose, but this was difficult to determine due to the dogs eating parts of her body.

French handball star Nikola Karabatic, along with his brother and 15 others, is set to stand trial for fraud in an illegal betting case involving a match-fixing incident during his time with Montpellier. Karabatic's lawyer aims for a not-guilty verdict, stating even a suspended sentence would be too harsh. The trial is expected to take place within months.

A gang of six men have been sentenced to a total of 31 years in jail for sexually abusing teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire, from 2009 to 2014. The men lured victims to parties and then sexually abused them, targeting emotionally immature girls at under-18s events. The judge rejected the defense's argument that the girls were motivated by a desire to be victims rather than out of their own volition.

Aaron Hernandez, convicted of murder, faces three more trials, including another murder case for killing two men and wounding another near a Boston nightclub in 2012. He also faces civil suits and a grievance over unpaid NFL bonus money, requiring him to maintain legal representation.

Emirates is set to rebrand the FA Cup as the Emirates FA Cup in a £30 million three-year deal. This adds to their extensive portfolio of sporting sponsorships, including Arsenal (Emirates Stadium, £150 million deal), AC Milan (£80 million deal), and Hamburg (£17 million deal).
