Juventus have ruled out signing Manchester United's loan player Radamel Falcao due to his high wages, despite interest in other strikers like Paulo Dybala and Edinson Cavani. Falcao, 29, has struggled at Manchester United since joining on loan last summer and is expected to leave in the summer.
If re-elected, David Cameron plans to sell £4 billion worth of Lloyds Bank shares to the public at a discount, aiming to pay down national debt, in the largest privatisation since the Thatcher era.

Living near congested roads with high air pollution increases the risk of 'silent strokes' and dementia, according to a study of over 900 people. The research links exposure to fine particulate matter, PM2.5, to brain shrinkage and a 46% higher risk of silent strokes, raising concerns about the long-term impacts of air pollution on brain health.

Jessica Ainscough, 30, died in February from epithelioid sarcoma, after choosing unconventional Gerson Therapy over conventional treatments. Her fiancé, Tallon Pamenter, revealed she underwent radiation in her final weeks, which successfully shrunk her tumor but led to complications. Jessica's story highlights the tension between alternative and conventional medical approaches.

A multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway near Fernvale, involving ten people including four children, resulted in several injuries; three were airlifted to Princess Alexandra Hospital with serious injuries, while six others were taken to Ipswich Hospital with minor injuries. Emergency crews freed one trapped person using hydraulic tools, and the highway remains closed with diversions in place.

Jason McDonald, a gator farm volunteer from Colorado, walked a slackline over a pool containing over 50 alligators, some up to ten feet long, as a daring new way to interact with the creatures. McDonald, who has been involved with alligators for over a decade, plans to walk over the farm's largest gators and even albino ones.

Abdul Hadi Arwani, a Syrian imam and activist, was shot dead in London, and sources suggest he may have met his killer during a building quote visit days before his murder. The counter-terrorism unit is investigating whether the man who requested the quote was a hired assassin, considering Arwani's links to the Muslim Brotherhood and his opposition to Syrian President Assad.

In Hong Kong, there's a craze for Jenny's butter cookies, with people lining up for hours to buy them at $9 a tin. The popularity has led to knockoff bakeries and resellers, while the original store warns against fake products. This cookie frenzy is part of a global trend where foods like cronuts and ramen burgers have sparked similar manias.

Kira Hollis, a 27-year-old from Tamworth, Staffordshire, overcame anorexia and depression by turning to bodybuilding after being diagnosed with borderline personality disorder. Now a personal trainer and healthy 9.5st, she credits the sport with giving her confidence and purpose, while her daughter Olivia and medication also played crucial roles in her recovery.

Jockey Lewis Ferguson, 18, survived a spectacular double somersault fall from his horse Merrion Square during a race at Wincanton, an incident viewed by hundreds of thousands online. Ferguson, who only had a minor cut on his nose, returned to mucking out stables and expressed no intention to quit racing, aiming for major races like Cheltenham and Aintree.

Hillary Clinton launched her 2016 campaign with a video and road trip aimed at rebranding herself and reframing her image as more empathetic and relatable. Critics were harsh, but her campaign may be successfully projecting a more confident and forward-looking persona, akin to marketing strategies by successful brands like Nike and Apple.

More than 1,700 Chinese high school students in Yichuan, Shaanxi province, took an exam in their school's playground due to lack of indoor space, organizing the unusual outdoor test themselves. They rotated their chairs and desks to avoid sun dazzle, finding the experience novel and relaxing.

A reader can win a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Joe Hart, England and Manchester City goalkeeper, along with a Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor and shaving gel in a competition run by Sportsmail and Gillette, closing on April 19.

Kecil, a baby orangutan rejected by his natural and surrogate mothers, found a loving home with 53-year-old Maggie at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. After a tense wait, Kecil and Maggie formed an inseparable bond, with Kecil now set to make his first public appearance this weekend.

Noelle Baynham, a 61-year-old woman from Winchester, Hampshire, died after an accidental overdose of medication and was partially eaten by her two dogs, which became desperate for food when she was undiscovered for days. Her friend Grant Donovan made the horrific discovery after entering her home, finding her body in her dressing gown and a bath run.

French handball star Nikola Karabatic, along with his brother and 15 others, is set to stand trial for fraud in an illegal betting case involving a match-fixing incident during his time with Montpellier. The trial, likely within months, could result in severe penalties, though his lawyer aims for a not-guilty verdict.

A gang of six men from Banbury, Oxfordshire, have been sentenced to a total of 31 years in jail for sexually abusing teenage girls between 2009 and 2014. The abuse occurred at parties organized by the group, who targeted emotionally immature girls at under-18s events. The victims, aged 13 to 16, were lured to these parties and then sexually abused.

Aaron Hernandez, convicted of murdering Odin Lloyd, faces three additional trials, including a murder case for killing two men and wounding another near a Boston nightclub in 2012. The case involves multiple civil suits and a potential NFL grievance over unpaid bonus money.

Emirates is set to rebrand the FA Cup as the Emirates FA Cup in a £30 million three-year deal. This adds to Emirates' extensive portfolio of sporting sponsorships, including Arsenal (Emirates Stadium and shirt sponsorship worth £150 million), AC Milan (worth £80 million), and Hamburg (worth £17 million).

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic champion, plans to compete in his fifth Olympics in Rio next year, despite a recent DUI arrest and suspension from the U.S. team. He will not compete in the upcoming world championships but hopes to join the team for the Olympics. Phelps is undergoing alcohol rehabilitation and has taken steps to address his past mistakes.

Gareth Bale is a major injury concern for Real Madrid's Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid due to a calf injury. Luka Modric is also out for six weeks with a knee ligament strain. Real Madrid seek a win to progress, having drawn 0-0 in the first leg.

A study by scientists at Texas Tech University found that older people are more prone to emotional decision-making about retirement investments, leading to significant financial losses during the 2007-2008 crisis. This comes as new UK pension reforms allow retirees to access their savings flexibly, highlighting the need for better emotional regulation in financial decisions.

Stuart Pearce advocates for Manchester City to retain Manuel Pellegrini, despite the team's recent poor performance and struggle for a top-four finish in the Premier League. Pearce attributes the team's issues partly to Yaya Toure's declining form and suggests the club needs a significant squad overhaul.

Manchester United trained in preparation for their upcoming Premier League match against Manchester City, with key players like Wayne Rooney and Robin van Persie returning to action. The game, to be played at Old Trafford, is crucial as United aims to move four points ahead of City in the league standings.

Fiorentina lost 1-0 to Hellas Verona at home, conceding in the 90th minute after missing a penalty, leaving them nine points behind third-place AS Roma in Serie A and in sixth place for Europa League qualification.

Miley Cyrus, at the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony, showed her unshaven armpits in a social media snap, sparking a debate on body hair among fans and social media users. While some criticized her appearance, others defended her right to choose.

Barcelona's Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez have scored 102 goals between them this season, with a 6-0 win over Getafe, taking them five points clear in La Liga. Messi leads with 49 goals, Neymar has 32, and Suarez has 21. Their performance adds pressure on Real Madrid ahead of their match.

Andrea McVeigh, 44, was seriously injured and left scarred for life after being knocked down by a cyclist on the pavement in Bermondsey, south London. The cyclist fled the scene, despite seeing the impact and blood. Police are seeking the cyclist and have released CCTV footage.

Paul Gregory, 51, of Bedford, was fined £795 and ordered to do 150 hours of unpaid work after admitting to dishonestly obtaining a blue badge by claiming he could only walk 200 metres, when he was actually a keen walker and mountaineer. Council officials discovered his fraud through a newspaper article detailing his 191-mile hike.

Apple has been awarded a patent for a facial recognition system that could automatically unlock iPhones when the device is moved into a specific position, matching the user's face to a stored image. This feature, which doesn't require the screen to be enabled, contrasts with current methods like PINs, passwords, and fingerprint scanning.

Elizabeth Sedway, a cancer patient from California, was forcibly removed from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California because she lacked a doctor's note, despite her family's efforts to board. The incident, caught on video and shared widely, sparked controversy over the airline's handling of her situation.

A head-on collision between a 1973 E-Type Jaguar worth over $120,000 and a Toyota Kluger on Warringah Road in Frenchs Forest, Sydney, resulted in the complete write-off of the vintage car. All three adults involved were taken to hospital as a precaution, though no one was hurt. The crash occurred on Easter Sunday night and is under investigation by NSW police.

Google has established a team to enhance battery technology for various devices, including phones, tablets, and electric cars, since 2012. The team, led by a former Apple battery expert, tests innovative technologies like flexible and wearable batteries, crucial for projects like Google's Project Loon.

The 223ft Explorer, a superyacht designed by Tony Castro, features a helipad, infinity pool, and extensive storage for luxury vehicles and water toys, catering to the ultra-wealthy. At approximately €40 million to build, it offers 12 guest suites and 15 crew members, ensuring a luxurious and comfortable sailing experience.

Labour leader Ed Miliband is pushing ahead with plans to cap rents, despite warnings from experts and critics that the measure will reduce housing investment and potentially worsen the housing crisis. The proposals include three-year fixed tenancies and rent increases capped at inflation, but critics argue these plans have significant loopholes that could harm tenants.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town supporter who hoped Arsenal would win was removed as a Reading mascot for their FA Cup semi-final due to fan outrage. The Football Association moved him to an England mascot spot instead.

Astronomers propose a giant supervoid, 1.8 billion light-years across, as the cause of a mysterious 'Cold Spot' in the universe's cosmic microwave background radiation. This supervoid, the largest known structure, could explain a 20% less dense region with about 10,000 fewer galaxies than surrounding areas.

The chair where Abraham Lincoln was shot will be displayed open to the public at The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, on April 15 to mark the 150th anniversary of his assassination. The chair, part of the 'With Liberty and Justice for All' exhibit, will be removed from its enclosure for this special occasion.

A UK couple planned a surprise One Direction concert trip to Cardiff, but the boyfriend mistakenly booked flights to Dublin, Ireland, due to confusion over the location. The mix-up was discovered by the girlfriend, who is a vlogger, and the boyfriend, also a vlogger, is now arranging train tickets to correct the error.

Romanian company MB Telecom has developed the Roboscan 2M Aeria, a mobile X-ray scanner that can inspect planes for contraband and weapons, aiming to fill security gaps at small airports. The device, costing €3 million, uses a cone of radiation to scan planes, though it currently requires the plane to be empty during operation. It has already seized 76,000 packs of illegal cigarettes at European borders.

Stephen Munden, a 54-year-old convicted paedophile with an obsession for young girls, has gone missing after vanishing from a psychiatric unit in Hampshire. Last seen leaving a hospital, Munden, who was detained under the Mental Health Act, is described as having a fanatical obsession with small children and is being sought by police.

Middlesbrough leads the Championship with a point buffer over second-place Bournemouth and a favorable match schedule, putting them in a strong position for promotion. Watford's Odion Ighalo aims to help his team secure a Premier League spot, while Bournemouth's recent struggles could see the division's top two change on the final weekend.

The #grannyhair trend, featuring silver and grey hair, is gaining popularity on social media, with models and everyday women embracing natural grays. This trend, inspired by fashion shows and feminist statements, is seen as a defiant move against traditional beauty norms, offering a feel-good alternative to hair dye.

A couple from Ohio, Randy and Jodi Speidel, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning in their bedroom, less than two months after creating online fundraisers for help due to their chronic conditions and financial struggles. Despite their desperate pleas, they received no donations and were found with their two cats outside the house.

Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg vows to remain as party leader despite potential electoral losses, emphasizing the risk of Labour and Conservative parties vacating the center ground. He hopes to lead the party into the next Parliament and seeks credit for forming the current coalition, with Business Secretary Vince Cable expressing hope to become Chancellor in a potential future coalition.

A 79-year-old pensioner in Somerset, UK, was saved from a large, aggressive badger by his Jack Russell dog. The badger, with six-inch teeth, burst into the pensioner's garden with cubs, but his dog dragged him indoors, preventing an attack. The National Farmers' Union has since advised on protecting properties from badger invasions.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose 3-0 to Porto U21s at Motspur Park, while his side progressed in the Champions League. Despite the loss, Mourinho remained upbeat, with Chelsea closing in on their first Premier League title since 2010.

Property developer Andreas Christopheros, 29, was severely injured in a December acid attack outside his Truro home, leaving him with life-changing injuries. Nicole Phillips, 45, and her husband David Phillips, 48, have been charged; David Phillips pleaded not guilty at Truro Crown Court. Mr. Christopheros, a businessman and event organizer, faces a long recovery and has lost vision and suffered facial scars.

In the Spanish town of Lastres, on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route, residents have posted humorous signs warning pilgrims not to defecate along the path, attracting amusement and photos from visitors. The pilgrimage, which can be nearly 500 miles long, lacks regular public facilities, leading locals to complain about unsanitary conditions.

A fire consumed a building in Flint, Michigan, where a strip club named The Body Shop used to be located. The blaze started around 1pm and was not at a vacant facility. Only the building and nearby power lines were affected, and an investigation is ongoing.

On the 10th anniversary of 9/11, Shoshana Hebshi, a woman of Arab and Jewish descent, was strip-searched at Detroit Metropolitan Airport and held for hours after being ethnically profiled. She settled a lawsuit with the federal government for $40,000, and Frontier Airlines will amend its policies to address discrimination.

An Asiana Airlines flight from Seoul to Hiroshima experienced a tailstrike and skidded off the runway, injuring 20 people and closing the airport. The Airbus A320 overran the runway at 8pm local time, with no sign of landing gear and evidence of a hard landing. This incident follows a previous crash in San Francisco two years ago.

Mark-Francis Vandelli, a 26-year-old Made In Chelsea star, revealed his extensive collection of expensive watches, including a Cartier white gold Moonphase worth £32,000 and a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42, in a recent interview with the Evening Standard. His collection, which he has been building since his teens, includes 16 watches valued at several thousand pounds each.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy, 89, is auctioning over 200 antiques, including a £4,000 to £6,000 3D diorama of the Battle of Agincourt, at Dominic Winter auctioneers in Gloucestershire, after deciding to downsize his home. The collection, valued at £100,000, includes historical items, furniture, and books, reflecting his interests in military history and literature.

Brazilian commuter Nelson Felippe posted a photo on Facebook of two women hugging on a train platform in Rio de Janeiro, initially expressing disapproval and concern about public behavior, but the post went viral as it was interpreted as a witty critique of homophobia and public safety.

A 16-year-old English cricket fan named Jonathan Stevenson received a detailed letter of advice from Richie Benaud about spin bowling nearly 20 years ago, which was shared on Twitter after Benaud's death. The letter, dated September 27, 1996, included tips on various deliveries and was signed by Benaud.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg envisions a future where virtual reality will replace traditional travel, allowing users to experience global destinations through VR headsets like Oculus Rift. Facebook plans to integrate VR into its newsfeed, enabling users to explore locations in 3D with multiple viewpoints.

Guo Kai and Dong Hui, who met a year ago, had to postpone their wedding due to Dong's serious bone cancer diagnosis. Instead, friends helped Dong dress in a wedding gown, and professional photographers took wedding photos at the hospital for their 22nd birthday. Guo, now a firefighter, has been at Dong's bedside every hour to help with her treatment and support her.

A 34-year-old man, Blaine Boudreaux, got behind the wheel while intoxicated in Houston, causing three separate crashes within three hours that killed two people, including a 6-year-old boy, and injured others. Boudreaux, with a history of DUIs, was charged with intoxication manslaughter and other offenses.

Microsoft launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions at its Redmond campus, partnering with Specialisterne. The initiative was announced by Mary Ellen Smith, who has a son with autism. This move follows Microsoft's previous controversy regarding gender pay equity.

Two deputies involved in the fatal arrest of Eric Harris in Tulsa, Oklahoma, were reassigned due to safety concerns after Harris' family and others criticized their actions. Reserve Deputy Robert Bates, 73, shot Harris, who was black, during a weapons sting operation; Bates is charged with second-degree manslaughter. The sheriff's office suspended its drug unit and is reviewing the deputies' actions, pending the outcome of Bates' trial.

Katie Prager, 24, and her husband Dalton, 24, are fighting to save Katie's life as she awaits a lung transplant for her cystic fibrosis and related infection. Kentucky Medicaid will not cover the out-of-state treatment needed at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center, leaving the couple desperate for help. Dalton has already received new lungs.

Using data from the Sleep Cycle app, researchers found that the world wakes up earliest on Mondays in South Africa, while Americans are grumpiest on Tuesdays at 7am. The best sleep quality occurs on Wednesdays, particularly in China, and Americans sleep in the latest and report the best moods on Fridays.

Mexican artist Frida Kahlo wrote 25 passionate love letters to her lover Jose Bartoli, which are expected to fetch up to $120,000 at auction in New York on April 15. The letters, penned between 1946 and 1949, reveal details about Kahlo's relationship with Diego Rivera and her secret romance with Bartoli.

Len McCluskey, leader of the Unite union, campaigned for Labour in South Wales, expressing traditional socialist views and anti-Conservative sentiment. Despite his genial manner, Unite's influence on Labour is significant, with claims of financial and organizational muscle being used to push for policies reminiscent of the 1970s. Unite, with 1.42 million claimed members, is deeply intertwined with Labour's structure and finances, raising concerns about the potential for a return to socialist policies.

Zookeeper Elad Hershkowitz at the Zoological Center in Tel Aviv filmed animals drinking from water troughs using a GoPro camera for 30 hours, capturing unique perspectives of 26-year-old lions, rhinos, zebras, and lemurs. The footage, reduced to four minutes, shows animals like a rhino almost kissing the water surface and a lemur delicately licking it, highlighting the differences in their drinking methods.

A poll found that only 25% of voters think David Cameron is most eager to win the election, compared to 43% for Ed Miliband. This comes as Cameron tried to boost his campaign's energy, while Miliband focused on immigration. Nicola Sturgeon of the SNP was seen as most enthusiastic by 34% of voters.

Zaur Dadaev, one of five Chechen men accused of assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov, retracted his confession after claiming he was beaten and pressured into confessing. Dadaev appeared via video link from prison, where he reportedly had signs of torture. Nemstov, an outspoken critic of President Putin, was shot four times on a Moscow bridge in February.

A photo of a four-month-old baby boy, Sonit Awal, being rescued from the rubble after the 2015 Nepal earthquake became a defining image of the disaster. The 7.8-magnitude quake on April 25, 2015, killed over 5,000 people and injured thousands more. Sonit was found alive after being trapped for 22 hours, and was taken to Bhaktapur Hospital where he was found to be uninjured.

A Church of Scientology-backed organization, Narcocon, attempted to rezone a 40-acre property near Camp David for a drug rehab center, despite current zoning laws prohibiting medical use. Narcocon, which uses sauna sessions and vitamin therapy, aims to prove the site's historic significance to bypass regulations, but faces opposition and legal challenges.

In Kabul, Afghanistan, five men who spoke English for NATO have been fired and blacklisted, leaving them jobless and fearing for their safety. The city's population has grown significantly, and many areas once frequented by foreigners are now deserted due to security warnings and the end of the U.S. presence.

Two US Navy SEALs died and one was critically injured after drowning while swimming in a pool at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story in Virginia on Friday. Both were assigned to Naval Special Warfare Group Two. An investigation is ongoing.

NBC, which holds the rights to show Premier League matches in the USA, has seen a significant increase in US viewership, from 13 million in 2012-13 to over 32 million last season. To enhance coverage, NBC has brought their entire production team to England for the first time, with anchor Rebecca Lowe, a Crystal Palace fan, leading the team for matches including Burnley vs. Arsenal, Manchester derby, and Liverpool-Newcastle.

Boris Johnson verbally attacked Ed Miliband on the Andrew Marr Show, calling him a potential threat to the country, while Miliband laughed off the criticism. The exchange followed accusations that the Conservatives were "descending into the gutter" for suggesting Miliband might "stab the country in the back." Miliband won the Labour leadership in 2010 by defeating his elder brother David, a fact Johnson used to criticize Ed's leadership abilities.

Dustin Irons, a prisoner in Oregon, was sentenced to an extra 30 days in jail for flashing a judge during a court hearing via video-link, despite being in handcuffs. The incident occurred at the Umatilla County Corrections Center, and Irons, known for his difficult behavior, faces further disciplinary action.

Jenson Button believes McLaren has made significant progress in Formula One, improving their car's competitiveness after a poor start to the season. McLaren and Honda showed promise in Malaysia, outpacing Force India, Sauber, and Lotus, but still have work to do on downforce and the power unit. Button hopes this trend continues for the upcoming Chinese Grand Prix in Shanghai.

The Fiona Stanley Hospital in Perth faced criticism after blood and bone fragments were found on medical instruments, leading to the removal of its medical service provider Serco and a fine of $60,000. The hospital has been operating with poorly sanitized instruments despite previous issues, causing concern among medical professionals and potentially damaging the hospital's reputation.

Becca Litchfield and Dale, from Gotham, Nottingham, sacrificed their dream wedding to fund IVF, which led to them winning a wedding competition and eventually giving birth to twins, Darci-Mai and Stanley, after two failed IVF attempts.

Scooter's Coffee in Omaha had its Facebook page hacked and used to post pornography for nearly 24 hours after an employee clicked a malicious link. The page was locked out and taken over by an unknown third party starting at 5pm on March 29, 2015. Scooter's managed to regain control with help from other businesses after Facebook initially did not respond to their reports.

At an American Kennel Club centre, a Shibu Inu puppy struggled to bark, instead making high-pitched squeaking and whining sounds, while a husky dog barked normally, causing amusement among onlookers. The video, filmed at the centre, shows the Shibu Inu attempting to bark and the husky barking, with both dogs conversing in their unique vocalizations. Staff and handlers attempted to pacify the excited puppy. Canine vocalization typically develops from grunts and whines to barks over several weeks.

Liam Plunkett, a 29-year-old England seamer, aims to challenge West Indies' batting lineup with his pace in the upcoming Test series, after recovering from an ankle injury. He is competing with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood for a spot, with James Anderson and Stuart Broad likely to retain new ball duties. Plunkett seeks to prove his worth through practice and warm-up games, aiming to be the best bowler.

Paul Smith is set to face reigning world super-middleweight champion Andre Ward in a non-title fight, possibly as a warm-up for a potential rematch with Carl Froch. The WBA has ordered Ward and Froch to unify their titles, but Ward prefers to fight in London rather than Nottingham. Meanwhile, Froch aims for his first Las Vegas fight against Julio Cesar Chavez Jr.

In Parma, Missouri, five of six police officers and several other top officials resigned shortly after the election of the city's first black mayor, Tyrus Byrd, citing safety concerns, leaving the small community of 713 people without key city employees. The outgoing mayor, Randall Ramsey, and Byrd's father Simon Wofford, deny any issues with the police force, and residents question the timing and necessity of the resignations.

Manchester City will make Yaya Toure available this summer but will not force him out, despite his high wages and interest from Inter Milan. Toure, 31, remains committed to City and has played crucial roles in recent titles. City will resist Valencia's attempts to pull out of the £24 million deal for Alvaro Negredo, who has struggled at Valencia.

A study found that more than two-thirds of people taking antidepressants in the U.S. did not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. Researchers examined selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), commonly prescribed for various psychiatric conditions. Official guidelines require five or more depressive symptoms over two weeks for a clinical depression diagnosis. Prescriptions for antidepressants have significantly increased in wealthy countries since 1998.

Doris Fuller's daughter, Natalie, 28, with bipolar disorder and psychosis, killed herself by stepping in front of a train in Baltimore. Fuller, who wrote about Natalie's struggles in a Washington Post article, revealed the illness went undiagnosed until Natalie was 22 and worsened despite treatment. Natalie, known for her art and poetry, described terrifying voices that influenced her actions.

A 10-year-old boy named Koby Hodder suffered a cardiac arrest during a game of British Bulldog in the school playground and was revived by teachers and paramedics. The incident, which lasted 12 minutes, led to a call for the game's ban due to its perceived danger. Koby was diagnosed with a heart condition similar to that of footballer Fabrice Muamba, who survived a cardiac arrest in 2012.

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain’s most senior female judge, called for divorce laws in England and Wales to be overhauled, removing the need for allegations of adultery or blame, and encouraging couples to resolve child and financial arrangements before obtaining a divorce. This change, supported by campaigners and lawyers, aims to reduce bitterness in matrimonial disputes and aligns with her 20-year-old proposal.

Tottenham are considering a £400 million stadium with a retractable pitch for a potential NFL franchise, due to open in 2018. The stadium, with a capacity of 65,000, could be more suitable for NFL than Wembley's 90,000 seats. The NFL is testing logistics for upcoming games at Wembley, with plans to have a permanent London franchise within five years.

U.S. senators, including Robert Menendez and Ron Johnson, wrote to FIFA, urging the organization to reconsider Russia's hosting of the 2018 World Cup due to Russia's involvement in the Ukraine crisis. FIFA had previously announced Russia as the host. England is considering a bid for Euro 2028 but is unlikely to bid for the 2026 World Cup while Sepp Blatter remains FIFA president.

Universal announced that the sequel to "Fifty Shades of Grey" will be released on February 10, 2017, with the third film set for February 9, 2018. EL James' husband, Niall Leonard, will write the script for the second film. The first movie earned $568.8 million worldwide.

Tony Pulis, manager of West Brom, faces another relegation battle despite his past successes in keeping teams in the Premier League. His record is one of the worst among long-serving managers, with never finishing in the top half of the table in seven seasons. West Brom's upcoming fixtures against top teams could determine their fate, while Pulis continues to be a beloved figure among Palace fans for his previous achievements.

Fenerbahce called for the suspension of the Turkish championship after their team bus was attacked by gunfire on Saturday, resulting in the driver being wounded. The attack occurred as the bus traveled from Rize to Trabzon airport following an away match against Caykur Rizespor. Fenerbahce stated that the championship should be suspended until the attackers are found and punished.

A massive avalanche hit Everest Base Camp, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens more on Saturday. The snowstorm, triggered by an earthquake, forced climbers to scatter and take refuge. Rescue efforts were hampered by aftershocks and the dangerous Khumbu Icefall, leaving hundreds of climbers stranded. Helicopters rescued some climbers but many remain trapped above Camp 1.

Gregory Margolin, an 87-year-old Jewish war veteran who fought in World War II, survived another war in Ukraine when a missile hit his house, killing his daughter. He immigrated to Israel with his granddaughter, joining 600 other Ukrainian Jews brought there by the International Fellowship of Christians and Jews since December.

John Carver, former assistant to Ruud Gullit at Newcastle, recalls Gullit's controversial decision to bench key players Alan Shearer and Duncan Ferguson before a 1999 Tyne-Wear derby, which Newcastle lost 2-1, leading to Gullit's resignation. Carver, now fighting for the head coach position, knows the impact a derby win could have on his chances.

Reverend Al Sharpton preached at Charity Missionary Baptist Church in North Charleston and addressed the Walter Scott case, meeting with local officials including Mayor Keith Summey and Police Chief Eddie Driggers, who had fired the officer involved in Scott's death. Sharpton is also attending a vigil near the shooting site and denied allegations that he was barred from Scott's funeral.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers will speak to Raheem Sterling about his recent controversial behavior, including inhaling nitrous oxide and smoking a shisha pipe, after Sterling scored the opening goal in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United. Rodgers emphasized the importance of being a top-class professional both on and off the field.

Labour received over £1 million in union donations during the second week of the election campaign, more than twice the amount received by the Conservatives (£492,512). Unions such as Unison, USDAW, and Unite contributed significantly, while the Liberal Democrats and UKIP received much less. This influx of union funding was seen as a potential political liability for Labour, with critics suggesting it would lead to higher taxes and spending.

Passengers on a Qatar Airways flight from Doha to Manchester became disruptive after being stranded for five hours on the tarmac in Birmingham due to severe winds. Police were called twice to the Birmingham airport. The passengers were eventually allowed off the aircraft and transported to Manchester, where they faced further delays. Qatar Airways apologized for the incident, citing crew fatigue as a reason for the diversion.

Justin Bieber will lead Floyd Mayweather's entourage into the ring for his $300 million fight against Manny Pacquiao in Las Vegas on May 2, 2015. The 21-year-old pop star has accompanied Mayweather to previous fights and has been a close friend for years.

Corinthian Colleges Inc., which once enrolled over 70,000 students, announced the closure of its 28 campuses, marking a significant step in holding for-profit colleges accountable. The U.S. Department of Education had previously curtailed Corinthian's access to federal student aid. With high student loan default rates and questionable educational value, many advocate for closing for-profit colleges, suggesting loan forgiveness for affected students.

Pep Guardiola denied a dispute with former Bayern Munich doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit after blaming the medical staff for the 3-1 Champions League loss to Porto. Guardiola took responsibility for the defeat and said injuries were not the medical staff's fault. Muller-Wohlfahrt, who had worked at the club for nearly 40 years, cited damage to trust as his reason for leaving.

Wladimir Klitschko, 39, prepares for his world title defense against Bryant Jennings at Madison Square Garden, recalling his Olympic gold win in 1996 that changed his life. Klitschko, who has been dominant since 2000, believes age is an advantage and is confident in his performance.

Jeremy Clarkson, 54, admitted he would miss fronting Top Gear after being fired in March for attacking a producer. Former presenter Angela Rippon, 70, expressed interest in returning to the show. Clarkson's contract was terminated after he physically assaulted a producer during filming. BBC bosses are trying to retain co-presenters James May and Richard Hammond.

In a La Liga match, Barcelona defeated Celta Vigo 1-0. During the final minutes, Celta Vigo's Fabian Orellana was sent off after throwing a lump of grass at Sergio Busquets, striking him in the neck. The incident occurred after Busquets tried to waste time, leading to heightened tensions.

In 2013, a bombing at the Boston Marathon killed three and injured over 200. In 2015, federal Judge George A. O'Toole warned jurors in Dzhokhar Tsarnaev's sentencing trial not to attend the marathon or related events, as the trial begins on April 21. Tsarnaev was convicted on all 30 counts, including using weapons of mass destruction, and the sentencing phase is set to last four weeks.

Tens of millions of Chinese people marked the Tomb Sweeping Festival by traveling to ancestral villages to clean tombs, burn paper money, and offer food. A grand ceremony honoring the Yellow Emperor Huangdi was held in Shaanxi Province, with thousands attending. The festival, a three-day holiday, sees traditional dances and parades, and is one of 24 Chinese solar terms marking the start of spring.

Paul Simon, 73, reached the top of the UK album chart with his "Ultimate Collection" for the first time in 25 years, outselling albums by younger artists like Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. This success is attributed to his recent tour with Sting, which has been well-received. Simon's last chart-topping album was in 1990.

Iker Casillas stated he will stay at Real Madrid and fight for the starting goalkeeper position despite potential competition from Manchester United's David de Gea. Casillas, who has been at Real Madrid since 1996, expressed his commitment to the club and plans to help defend their Champions League title.

Britain's employment reached a record 31 million, with 557,000 more jobs in the three months to February compared to the same period the previous year. The International Monetary Fund and German finance minister praised Chancellor George Osborne's economic strategy, reducing the deficit from £153 billion to £90 billion. Prime Minister David Cameron hailed this as a 'jobs miracle,' and the Chancellor said the UK is one of the brightest spots in the world economy.

SsangYong, a Korean automaker, launched the Tivoli SUV in the UK at under £13,000, targeting budget-conscious consumers. The vehicle, priced from £12,950 to £19,000, comes in three trim levels and offers a five-year warranty. SsangYong expects the Tivoli to boost its UK sales from 2,000 to 4,000 annually.

Chef Sam Longhurst at Splendid Kitchen in Manchester created a 10-inch, 2,000-calorie burger called "The Whole Damn Farm" containing six forms of three different meats, weighing half a kilogram and priced at £13.50. The burger, inspired by a customer's challenge, features two beef patties, bacon jam, ham, chicken, pulled pork, and bacon, and was designed to be a show-stopping meal.

Yeo Valley's staff canteen, located in Blagdon, North Somerset, offers Michelin-starred quality meals made from organic and locally sourced ingredients to dairy workers for as little as £2. The canteen, praised as the world's best staff canteen, has expanded to serve the public at higher prices.

B.B. King, the legendary blues musician, was hospitalized for dehydration caused by his Type II diabetes but has since been discharged and is resting at home. He thanked fans for their concern and has been a "trouper," as his daughter and publicist described. King, 89, is known for his hits like "The Thrill Is Gone" and his custom-made Gibson guitar named Lucille.

On Easter Sunday, New York's Fifth Avenue hosted an Easter parade featuring colorful and bizarre hats, with participants ranging from churchgoers to hatmakers and passersby, creating a unique spectacle. Highlights included a ship-shaped hat, a butterfly bonnet, and a diorama inspired by Mayor Bill de Blasio. The event, a modern twist on the 1880s tradition, showcased a mix of conservative and elaborate headwear in a sunny Manhattan setting.

The East of England ambulance service received 1,248 inappropriate calls in two years, including prank calls about a squirrel being hit by a car, a bleeding burger, and a woman feeling ill after eating too much takeaway. Front-line crews attended nearly half of these calls, potentially delaying responses to genuine emergencies.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake won a series of challenges against Loic Remy and Willian in an Audi football challenge, except for the final long-range shot where Willian accidentally broke a car's wing mirror, though Remy and Willian ultimately won the final challenge.

Brendan Rodgers criticizes Raheem Sterling's advisor, suggesting Sterling would stay at Liverpool if left to decide alone. Sterling rejected a £100,000-a-week contract and has two years left on his deal. Rodgers met with Sterling to advise him to stay, citing his best interest and Liverpool's benefits for his development.

On a recent episode of Countdown, co-presenter Rachel Riley was embarrassed when contestants offered the word 'erection' as their answer, causing host Nick Hewer to struggle to contain his laughter. This incident is part of a recurring pattern where rude words have caused hosts to react awkwardly, including previous instances with Carol Vorderman.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, was spared jail after attempting to buy deadly poison online to commit suicide. He was caught in an anti-terror operation by North West Counter Terrorism Unit officers who had been tracking his online activity since January. The boy, who pleaded guilty, was sentenced to a 12-month referral order.

Lianne Hindle, 37, died of a cardiac arrest three hours after giving birth to her daughter Poppy at North Manchester General Hospital in December, prompting calls for action from her partner Chris Barnes. The hospital, along with Royal Oldham, is under investigation following 10 deaths at their maternity units between December 2013 and July 2014. Ms Hindle's family is concerned about the care she received, particularly the presence of a student midwife after the birth.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after training while eight months pregnant. Pittman, a two-time world champion hurdler, continued training throughout her pregnancy and plans to compete in the Beijing World Championships and the 2016 Rio Olympics. Her coach confirmed she trained carefully, monitoring her core temperature.

A powerful storm capsized several sailboats during the Dauphin Island regatta in Mobile Bay, Alabama, on April 25, 2015, resulting in at least one death and leaving four people missing. Over 100 sailboats and about 200 participants were involved in the event. Richard Mather rescued three people from a sinking boat.

Roseanne Barr revealed she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma, conditions that worsen over time and have stolen her central and peripheral vision. Her doctors have not provided a timeline, but Barr uses marijuana to relieve eye pressure. Ophthalmologist Steven A. Shanbom explains that while it's unusual for Barr to have both conditions, it's not unheard of, and there are treatments that may delay progression or halt further vision loss.

A 17-year-old named Chancey Allen Luna was convicted of first-degree murder in the 2013 shooting death of Australian college baseball player Christopher Lane in Duncan, Oklahoma. The jury recommended a life sentence without parole. Luna's defense argued he only meant to scare Lane, but the jury found him guilty.

Arsene Wenger, Arsenal's manager, insists his poor record against Jose Mourinho will not affect the upcoming match between Arsenal and Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium. Wenger has lost 7 out of 12 games against Mourinho, but believes the result will depend on the day's performance. The match is significant as it could help Arsenal close the 10-point gap to Chelsea in the Premier League standings.

Manny Pacquiao, a Filipino boxer, is set to face Floyd Mayweather in a high-profile fight at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Pacquiao's career began in poverty and involved moving to Manila at 14 to pursue boxing, eventually becoming one of the world's biggest sports stars. The fight, dubbed the "Fight of the Century," is scheduled for Saturday and is expected to generate $300 million in revenue.

Jack Grealish, an outstanding Aston Villa player who starred in their FA Cup semi-final win over Liverpool, was photographed inhaling nitrous oxide, a drug that can affect athletic performance. This incident, along with similar cases among other young players, highlights the need for athletes to make responsible choices to maintain their professional standards.

Sam Barton, who spent £55,000 on cosmetic surgery to resemble Joey Essex, was attacked on Easter Monday by a group who pelted him with eggs after he checked into a pub on Facebook. Barton, who has debts of £100,000 and has been bankrupt, believes the attackers targeted him due to online abuse about his appearance.

Manchester University in Indiana was placed on lockdown late on Friday night after receiving a 'likely prank call' about an armed person near the administration building. Police, a bomb squad, and Indiana State Police responded but decided it was a prank. The university advised students to shelter in place and wait for police, with no injuries confirmed.

Edinson Cavani, known as "El Matador," faces Luis Suarez in a crucial Champions League match between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona at Parc des Princes. Cavani, without key players Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Marco Veratti, must perform to help PSG advance, despite a recent goal drought.

Derry Mathews won the interim WBA lightweight title with a unanimous points decision over Tony Luis in Liverpool. Richar Abril and Ismael Barroso had previously pulled out due to illness and visa issues, respectively. Luis, drafted in at the last minute, showed aggression but Mathews secured the win with scores of 114-112, 114-112, 115-112.

Hull shocked St Helens with a 28-20 victory at Langtree Park, ending St Helens' three-game winning streak. Jamie Shaul's try proved decisive, while St Helens struggled with injuries and substitutions.

The U.S. immigrant population, including both documented and undocumented, could reach a record high of 51 million by 2023, accounting for 14.8% of the total population, and grow to 78 million by 2060, making up 82% of future population growth. This trend, driven by current immigration policies, has prompted discussions among political candidates and raised concerns about workforce, infrastructure, and integration.

Jack Wilshere captained Arsenal Under 21s in a 1-0 loss to Reading's U21s at the Emirates Stadium. Martin Keown's son Niall scored the winning goal in the 8th minute. Wilshere and Abou Diaby, both returning from injuries, lasted the full match without issue.

Justin Rose, who fell outside the world's top 10 after a poor performance in Florida, showed signs of improvement at the Shell Houston Open, hitting 17 out of 18 greens and scoring a 69. Rose attributed his recent struggles to getting ahead of the ball at impact and issues with his irons and putter, which he has since corrected. He remains focused on his game ahead of the Masters, aiming to maintain his top-five ranking.

A mansion in Mayfair, London, built on the site of a former milking parlour, has been listed for £25 million. The 8,139 square foot property, constructed in 2011, features modern amenities like an indoor pool, gym, and cinema room. The site was originally a dairy hub dating back to the 1800s.

Bayern Munich, without several key players due to injuries, is relying on team unity to overcome Porto in the Champions League quarter-final, with coach Pep Guardiola emphasizing the importance of the remaining squad members. Arjen Robben, Franck Ribery, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and David Alaba are among the injured. Bayern has shown resilience in recent matches, winning against Borussia Dortmund, Bayer Leverkusen, and Eintracht Frankfurt.

Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited Mercedes' Brackley base to strategize against Ferrari after Sebastian Vettel's victory in the Malaysian Grand Prix. Hamilton and Rosberg finished behind Vettel, with Hamilton needing three pit stops compared to Vettel's two. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff expressed concern, acknowledging Ferrari's superior performance and the need for analysis.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to use nitrogen gas for executions if lethal injection becomes unavailable, aiming for a humane method. The bill, which has never been used in U.S. executions, was passed amid concerns over lethal injection and Oklahoma's controversial execution practices.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice, including an overhead kick, helping Swansea to a 3-1 win over Hull and topping EA Sports' Performance Index with a score of 52.9. Other top performers include Charlie Austin (52.2) and Eden Hazard (51.7).

A Russian freezer trawler called the Dalny Vostok sank in the Sea of Okhotsk, killing at least 56 of its 132 crew members. The ship, with an international crew, sank in 15 minutes after pulling in an 80-ton fishing net, and a massive rescue operation involving over 1,300 people is underway. At least 56 bodies have been recovered, and 63 survivors have been rescued, with 13 still missing.

A clinical trial found that olaparib, a drug originally for women with breast cancer, can benefit men with advanced prostate cancer, delaying disease progression in up to 30% of cases with specific genetic mutations. The trial, led by researchers at the Institute of Cancer Research and the Royal Marsden hospital, showed olaparib can control prostate cancer growth and improve scan responses. This makes olaparib the first cancer drug targeting inherited genetic mutations, with potential to reduce side effects from traditional treatments.

Rhiannon Taylor, a 29-year-old travel photographer from Australia, turned her passion into a business by reviewing and photographing luxury accommodations worldwide. With over 12,000 Instagram followers, she documents the best beds, pools, and room service in hotels from places like Indonesia, the U.S., and Mexico, generating income from hotel stays, photo sales, and partnerships with travel product companies.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was killed after getting caught in a fight between two adult hippos in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park, South Africa. The calf's mother watched helplessly as the baby was thrown into the air and dragged through the water. A tour operator, Stacey Farrell, described how the mother likely believed it safer to stay with her herd, but her decision proved fatal for the calf when one of the males grabbed and killed it.

During Chelsea's 1-0 victory over QPR at Loftus Road, QPR fans threw objects onto the pitch, hitting Branislav Ivanovic on the head. The Football Association will observe the situation, with QPR reviewing CCTV and appealing for witnesses to help identify the culprits, who could face bans.

A young mother, LaTasha Gosling, and her three children were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. The suspect, known to the family, was found dead hours later without signs of homicide. The family has started a GoFundMe page to raise money for funeral services, having already exceeded their initial goal.

Emily Thornberry, a Labour politician, faced criticism for opposing the right to buy policy while renting out a housing association property worth nearly £1 million. Her husband and she bought the property eight years ago for much less. Critics accused her of hypocrisy, while housing association leaders were also criticized for living in mansions while opposing the right to buy. Thornberry previously lost her frontbench job after tweeting a picture of a house with English flags and a white van, highlighting her own expensive properties.

Police dropped an investigation into a violent assault on Mike Lane, the joint master of the Tedworth Hunt, despite having evidence and a video of the attack by masked protesters on January 24 near Amesbury. Wiltshire Police cited insufficient evidence and have not identified, charged, or prosecuted anyone involved, angering hunt supporters.
Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes insists he will stay at the club, rejecting links to Manchester United and Chelsea, and stating he is happy with his current form and position in La Liga.

An Australian teenager, Audrey Pekin, was raped twice on Christmas Eve in Bali by a man named Henry Alafu, who lured her to his home and then followed her in a taxi. Pekin, who has type 1 diabetes, was unable to resist her attacker. Despite seeking help, Alafu escaped and was later seen waiting at a hotel lobby. Indonesian police failed to apprehend him, and he returned to Nigeria.

Ashley James, a former Made In Chelsea star, posed with a fake skinned fox to launch an anti-fur campaign against Harvey Nichols, which recently reintroduced fur products after a decade-long ban. PETA is supporting the campaign, and Harvey Nichols defended its decision by stating its commitment to ethical trading and responsible sourcing.

Chile enacted a new law on Monday allowing civil unions between same-sex couples, which will take effect in six months. The law, supported by President Michelle Bachelet, aims to provide legal rights to cohabiting couples, including property, health care, pensions, and inheritance rights, and will benefit an estimated 2 million people. This move aligns Chile with other South American countries like Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay that have allowed same-sex civil unions, though full marriage equality is only recognized in Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay.

Chelsea have led the Premier League for 230 days, on course to break Manchester United's record of 262 days set in 1993/94. Chelsea currently lead by seven points with a game in hand, and could beat the record by 12 days if they stay top until the end of the season.

Cape Verde, a small island nation in the Atlantic, is leveraging its rich musical heritage to boost its economy, lacking conventional natural resources. The government, including Prime Minister Jose Maria Neves, is promoting music and culture as key sectors. The Kriol Jazz Festival, celebrating its seventh edition, has attracted international artists and boosted tourism, indicating potential for the music industry to drive economic growth.

A hoax video of a wave rider surfing in front of Sydney's Opera House resurfaced on social media, going viral again after heavy storms. The video, originally posted in 2012, was shared by radio hosts Fitzy and Wippa and quickly spread. Wave experts dismissed the video as impossible due to the physical constraints of Sydney Harbour.

Reading lost 1-0 to Birmingham in a Championship match at the Madejski Stadium, despite dominating much of the game. Clayton Donaldson scored Birmingham's winning goal, his 16th of the season. Reading, who had lost in the FA Cup semi-finals to Arsenal, wasted several chances and were held firm by Birmingham.

David Luiz, a key defender for Paris Saint-Germain, injured his hamstring during a match against Marseille and will miss at least four weeks, including both legs of the Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona.

The return of Game of Thrones has led to a significant surge in internet piracy, with over 100,000 illegal downloads per day and seven million episodes illegally downloaded between February and April. Brazil was the top country for illegal downloads, followed by France, the US, Canada, and the UK. HBO announced it will air the new season simultaneously in 170 countries and launched a new streaming service, HBO Now, to combat piracy.

Leicester City and West Ham United will face off at King Power Stadium in a Premier League match. Matt Upson is out for Leicester, while Winston Reid returns for West Ham. West Ham is favored with odds of 2/1, while Leicester is at 7/5. West Ham has not lost to Leicester in their last seven league meetings but Leicester has won just one of their last ten home matches.

In 2009, Celoron, N.Y., unveiled a statue of Lucile Ball that residents found unrecognizable and unflattering, leading to a Facebook page with over 600 likes calling for its removal. The statue, based on Ball's intoxicated pitch for a health tonic, was created by artist Dave Poulin, who declined to comment. Estimated to cost $8,000 to $10,000 to recast, the statue has sparked controversy for six years.

Sharon Smith, 43, from Halesowen, lost nearly half her body weight, going from over 20st to 9st 9lb, after standing for 11 hours on a flight in December 2012 due to concerns about crushing the passenger next to her. She joined Weight Watchers and started running, which helped her maintain her weight loss.

Nicola Bonn, 34, from London, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences as a first-time mother of 14-month-old Poppy, addressing the overwhelming opinions and judgments she faced, and encouraging other mothers to stop justifying their decisions.

Two 17-year-old boys from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, named Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, traveled to Turkey on March 31 and are believed to have crossed into Syria, raising concerns among their families. The boys' families, in shock and worry, are urging the public for information to help bring them back home. Hassan is related to Hammaad Munshi, who was arrested in 2006 for planning to murder non-Muslims. The boys reportedly used the Easter holidays as a "window of opportunity" to leave the UK.

Stephanie Scott, a school teacher from Leeton, was murdered just days before her wedding, leaving her fiancé Aaron Leeson-Woolley devastated. Her body was found in bushland on Easter Friday after she went missing on Easter Sunday. The couple had planned a wedding at Eat Your Greens venue, with a guest list of 120 people. Scott's father described her as bubbly and thoughtful, with many wedding preparations left unfinished.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is pursuing Feyenoord players Tonny Vilhena and Jordy Clasie for potential transfers, while also looking to make Eljero Elia's loan move permanent, as the club aims to strengthen its squad for possible European qualification. Vilhena, a 20-year-old Dutch winger, wants to leave Feyenoord, while Clasie, a £10m-rated midfielder, is also a target.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in Ickworth House's library in Suffolk, sparking controversy among heritage experts. The experiment, aimed at encouraging visitors to engage more deeply, will also be tested at nine other National Trust venues. The Trust's director defended the move, stating it aims to enhance visitor experience rather than merely display objects.

Former Prime Minister John Howard and his driver stopped at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music to change a flat tyre, with Howard chatting to passerby Felicity Waterford, who recognized him. The incident occurred just weeks after Liberal MP Christopher Pyne faced a similar challenge on national television.

Tony Pulis acknowledges Joey Barton's criticism of West Brom's mental fortitude after they lost a 2-0 lead to QPR in December. Barton claimed the team "s***ed themselves" during the match. Pulis, who has improved West Brom's performance, compares his own experience of losing a 2-0 lead as a manager. The teams face each other again at the Hawthorns, with West Brom aiming to maintain their strong performance.

In the Democratic Republic of Congo, researchers have captured the first-ever photograph of the Bouvier's red colobus monkey, proving it is not extinct after being thought lost for over 50 years. The monkeys, found in Ntokou-Pikounda National Park, are vulnerable to hunters in the area. Meanwhile, a new species of white-cheeked macaque, Macaca leucogenys, was discovered in southeast Tibet using camera traps, distinguishing it by its rounded penis.

Kim Kardashian, Kanye West, and their family visited Armenia, the country of Kim's father's birth, for eight days, receiving a star-studded welcome in Yerevan. They stayed at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan and visited landmarks like the Yerevan Opera House and Geghard Monastery. Their visit, documented extensively, highlighted the city's cultural attractions and its blend of Soviet and modern architecture.

Patrick and Valerie Jubb, British expats in Jimena de la Frontera, Spain, face losing their four-bedroom bed and breakfast due to illegal alterations made by a previous owner, despite obtaining a certificate stating no infractions. The town hall ruled the additions illegal, and the couple, who want to return to the UK, are trying to sell the property for €680,000 but are unable to due to the demolition threat.

Apple reported record iPhone sales of over 61 million units in the first quarter, generating $58 billion in revenue and $13.6 billion in profit, up 40% from the previous year. Sales in China surpassed those in the US, and the company's cash reserves grew to $200 billion. iPad and Mac sales declined, but CEO Tim Cook expressed optimism about the new Apple Watch and continued iPhone success.

A 3-year-old girl named Elisa, whose mother Natali Castellanos-Tyler died in a car crash, has been having nightmares about a white van. Her father, Craig Tyler, believes this may be connected to the crash, as there have been multiple hit-and-run incidents involving white box trucks in the area recently.

Researchers at New York University found that emotionally neutral events can be better remembered when tied to an emotion, as seen in studies on the September 11 attacks' impact on memory. Emotion strengthens memory by affecting brain regions like the amygdala, striatum, and hippocampus. A power nap of 45 minutes can significantly boost memory retention, according to scientists from Saarland University.

Jahnae Jackson, girlfriend of 18-year-old Jackson Byrnes from northern NSW, has cared for him after he was diagnosed with a stage four brain tumour. They raised over $80,000 for surgery by Dr. Charlie Teo, which is scheduled for Wednesday. Jackson will be paralysed post-surgery and needs additional funds for chemotherapy. The community's support has been overwhelming for the couple.

Nedum Onuoha, a 28-year-old QPR centre-back, is being pursued by Hull City, among other clubs, as QPR considers squad reductions if they are relegated. Onuoha, with 15 months left on his contract, started in QPR's 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion. Hull is also interested in West Brom striker Victor Anichebe, who is likely to be sold this summer.

Researchers at Yale University mapped regional variations in sentence structure across the US and UK through an online survey, revealing unique phrases like "Here's you a water bottle" in the South and "This glass needs washed" in Idaho. The project highlights how sentence patterns vary by region, age, and social group, offering insights into linguistic diversity.

A Canadian man, Kalman Kallai, took a nine-day journey from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia, dragging a green rocking chair behind him for scenic views. He documented his adventure, featuring stops by cornfields, cafes, and water bodies, and even bonding with his father for part of the trip.

Manager Tim Sherwood joked about his 'win bonus' during a press conference, revealing a Twix multi-pack after a six-year-old fan named Charlie Pye had applied for the Aston Villa job and requested sweets as a win bonus.

Kell Brook, the world boxing champion, attended the Premier League Darts in Sheffield, where Dave Chisnall won two matches to move to second place in the table with 17 points. Chisnall defeated Gary Anderson 7-3 and James Wade 7-1, while Michael van Gerwen maintained his lead with an 8-5 win over Stephen Bunting.

Marco Verratti praises Zlatan Ibrahimovic's off-field contributions for Paris Saint-Germain, where Ibrahimovic has scored 17 Ligue 1 goals. Ibrahimovic was suspended for the first leg of PSG's Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona but will play in the return match.

The Ministry of Defence accidentally published a secret RAF Aerodrome Manual for the Falklands Islands on their website, revealing GPS coordinates and technical details that could aid Argentina in an invasion. The document, which included information on the runway and facilities, was accessible to anyone online, including potential Argentine attackers. The MoD has since disabled the link, but the incident highlights increased tensions between Britain and Argentina over the Falklands' sovereignty.

Huddersfield Giants coach Paul Anderson aims to improve his team's offensive play to boost their Super League standing after a poor start to the season, with a home game against Catalans Dragons offering a chance to climb the ladder. The Giants, currently ninth, have the league's best defensive record but have lost three consecutive games. A win could see them leapfrog their French opponents.

Planners in Windsor approved the opening of a second Costa cafe less than 500 yards from an existing one, bringing the total to three within a short walking distance. The new Costa will open on the site of a former bank, while a Costa Express is located between the two. Residents are divided, with some concerned about the proliferation of coffee shops and fast-food businesses, while others see it as a sign of the area's growth.

The British Veterinary Association has withdrawn its support for shooting free-running badgers in controversial pilot culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire, instead advocating for trapping and shooting. The Environment Secretary, Liz Truss, promised to expand culls if the Conservatives win the election, despite criticism from wildlife groups. In Somerset, 341 badgers were culled, meeting the required number, but in Gloucestershire, only 274 were killed due to protest and intimidation.

Geoff Barrow, Portishead's founder, criticized streaming services for low royalty payments, citing £1,700 for 34 million plays. He and other artists, including Jay-Z, are pushing for better deals, while streaming companies defend their practices. Jay-Z's Tidal service offers higher artist payouts but at a higher cost to users.

The first four episodes of Game of Thrones season five were leaked online before the official premiere, with over 550,000 downloads by early Sunday morning. HBO stated that the leak likely came from press copies, and they are investigating. The show is known for being heavily pirated, with episodes from the first four seasons illegally downloaded over seven million times between February and April 2015.

Daniel Buccheri, a 25-year-old singer from Melbourne, composed an emotional song for his brother Adrian's wedding, which went viral with over 100,000 views. The speech, performed at Poet's Lane in Sherbrooke on March 29, included tributes to Adrian and his new wife Sarah, touching on their relationship and Daniel's childhood.

Zara Phillips, 33, regained her fitness after giving birth to Mia by exercising daily before her daughter woke up, aiming to qualify for the 2016 Rio Olympics. She follows a strict routine including morning exercise, a healthy diet, and additional workouts, having previously won team silver at the 2012 London Olympics.

Raheem Sterling's interview where he said he was not ready to sign a new contract at Liverpool upset fans and could affect his relationship with the club. Sterling has been linked with a move to Arsenal, and while some fans are willing to offer him a high salary, there is growing frustration among supporters who believe no player should be bigger than the club.

In the 1996-97 season, Barcelona's squad, which included future managers like Jose Mourinho, Pep Guardiola, and Laurent Blanc, won the Spanish Super Cup. This team, under Bobby Robson, is now producing managers for the current Champions League, with four of the last eight coaches coming from Barcelona.

Former Manchester United star Eric Cantona named Paris Saint-Germain's Javier Pastore the best player in the world, praising his creativity over Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, at the Laureus World Sports Awards in Shanghai. Pastore, who cost PSG £29 million, has three goals and five assists this season, compared to Messi's 45 and Ronaldo's 51.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murdering his tenant Michael Spalding, 39, by hacking his body into pieces and dumping the remains in a canal. Simon, with his girlfriend Michelle Bird, 35, was arrested after the bodies were discovered in two suitcases. The trial lasted four weeks, and Bird was cleared of murder but admitted to assisting an offender.

Health experts and campaigners in Essex and Gloucestershire are using 'loneliness maps' to identify areas where elderly and other residents are at risk of social isolation. These maps, based on factors like age, living alone, mental illness, and low income, help councils target support. A new report recommends this approach to tackle loneliness nationwide, which can lead to health issues like dementia.

Dedicated waitress Judy Eddingfield celebrated 50 years of working at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, where she started at age 15. The restaurant, open since 1940, has been a family tradition for Eddingfield, with her mother and siblings also working there. Eddingfield met her husband at the restaurant and has seen many memorable moments, including when actors from 'Leave It to Beaver' visited in the 1970s.

Former England captain Mike Gatting suggests Kevin Pietersen should not return to the national team immediately despite his potential to score runs for Surrey, as Gary Ballance, Ian Bell, and Joe Root are performing well. Alastair Cook, England's captain, is facing pressure to perform in the upcoming Tests against West Indies, with Gatting stating that questions will be asked if Cook fails to score runs.

A 17-year-old Californian student, Caleb Benn, developed an app called 'Uploader for Instagram' that allows users to upload photos to Instagram from their computer, violating Instagram's terms of service. The app, priced at $4.99, has been generating $1,000 a day for Benn, but Instagram has demanded he 'fix' it by Monday, threatening legal action.

In South Korea, "hoesik" involves frequent group drinking sessions at work, often with soju, to build relationships. Foreign business travelers face pressure to participate, as drinking is seen as a way to reveal someone's true character. Traffic patterns in Seoul reflect this culture, with evenings after work being the busiest times. Etiquette includes deferring to seniors, never leaving a glass empty, and pouring for others before drinking.

The Duke of Kent, 79, was discharged from Aberdeen Royal Infirmary after being treated for a dislocated hip he suffered at Balmoral estate. He used a walking stick and was driven away by his daughter. Buckingham Palace confirmed he was successfully treated. This injury comes two years after he had a mild stroke.

The Surfers Paradise Meter Maids, a 50-year tradition of young women in bikinis patrolling the beachside area to manage parking meters, faces potential end due to local business leaders' calls for modernization. The group, started in 1965, is seen as outdated and a violation of anti-touting laws, with the Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce president arguing they no longer provide a public service. However, Meter Maids' general manager disputes this, claiming they are an integral part of the Gold Coast experience.

Greece denied it would fail to pay a £330 million loan to the IMF, stating it would make the payment on time. Deputy finance minister Dimitris Mardas said Greece is prioritizing wages and pensions. Sources suggested Greece might enter a 'silent arrears process' with the IMF, while Germany's finance minister warned against default, as it could lead to Greece leaving the eurozone.

A Turkish court blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after the social media platforms refused to remove images of prosecutor Mehmet Selim Kiraz, who was killed during a siege by the DHKP-C terrorist group. The blocks were imposed due to the images upsetting the family of the deceased prosecutor. Kiraz died after being taken hostage during an investigation into the death of Berkin Elvan, a 15-year-old who died in 2013 following a police incident.

A seven-year-old Star Wars fan named Colin Gilpatric wrote to George Lucas, asking to change the rule that bans Jedi Knights from marrying. Lucas responded, affirming that compassion and loyalty are values important in marriage and that the Force is strong with Colin. Colin received a package from Lucasfilm containing Star Wars merchandise and a letter addressing his question.

Wisconsin beat Kentucky 71-64 in the NCAA Tournament semi-finals, ending Kentucky's undefeated season and advancing to the final. Duke defeated Michigan State 81-61, securing a spot in the final against Wisconsin. The finals will be held at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis.

Vince Neil of Mötley Crüe performed a poor rendition of the American national anthem at a Las Vegas football game, joining a list of notable performers including Whitney Houston, Roseanne Barr, Jimi Hendrix, and Michael Bolton, who have all been criticized for their versions of the anthem.

In January, Barry Lyttle from Belfast punched his brother Patrick outside a Sydney bar, causing Patrick to fall unconscious and nearly lose his life. Security footage shown at Downing Centre Local Court revealed the incident, with Barry pleading guilty to grievous bodily harm. He faces up to two years in jail, though a possible suspended sentence is under consideration.

The gravesite of conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, buried at Pinegrove Memorial Park in Sydney's west, was found stripped of memorabilia by their parents, who confronted cemetery staff about the unauthorized removal of their daughters' mementos, which were found in nearby rubbish bins. The twins, born with a rare condition, died 19 days after birth.

Lord Neuberger, President of the UK Supreme Court, suggested Muslim women should be allowed to wear full-face veils in court to show respect for different customs. He addressed the need for judges to be sensitive to cultural differences and subconscious biases when dealing with less privileged individuals. This comes amid uncertainty over the place of traditional Muslim dress in the legal system, following a 2003 case where a woman was sentenced for refusing to remove her veil.

Andre Cole, 52, was executed by lethal injection in Missouri on Tuesday for killing Anthony Curtis in 1998 over child support disputes. The execution was carried out at the Eastern Reception, Diagnostic and Correctional Center in Bonne Terre, Missouri. Cole, who was black, was convicted by an all-white jury and faced several appeals, including one disputing his mental fitness for execution.

Prince Harry will fly to Australia without seeing his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is overdue with the birth of her second child. Harry, who had hoped to meet the new royal baby, will return in mid-May. He recently returned from Turkey to hand out prizes at the London Marathon. Bookmakers are taking bets on the baby's details, including name and appearance.

Florida man Justin Jackson, accused of posing as celebrities including Oprah Winfrey and Reggie Love, defrauded businesses of $2.4 million worth of goods and services over eight years, including posing as Oprah's nephew and sending forged letters to hotels for job recommendations. He is also accused of working with Angel Agarrat in these schemes.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini has set a €50 million price tag on Paulo Dybala, attracting interest from Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus, and Paris Saint-Germain. Inter Milan's Roberto Mancini was seen scouting Dybala, but PSG is considered the strongest bidder. Zamparini wants €50 million for Dybala, comparing him to Lionel Messi and stating Dybala could be sold to PSG if they meet his asking price.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians protested against President Dilma Rousseff, demanding her impeachment due to an economic downturn and a bribery scandal at state-run oil company Petrobras. Rousseff's approval rating dropped sharply after protests last month, and her supporters argue she was not involved in the corruption. The scandal, involving construction companies paying bribes to Petrobras executives and politicians, has grown, complicating the political landscape.

Former Manchester United player Eric Cantona refuted claims that he starred in a soft porn film, insisting You and the Night is an artistic piece. The film includes racy scenes, such as Cantona on his hands and knees in just his underwear, and stars alongside Beatrice Dalle. Cantona defended the film, stating it is "a work of art" and not pornographic.

Psychologists found that listening to certain music can enhance food flavors, with The Beatles' music enhancing fish and chips at a Shanghai restaurant. Researchers also discovered that paired music can increase wine enjoyment by up to 15%, and different musical tones can highlight specific tastes like sweetness, bitterness, and sourness.

Raheem Sterling, a 20-year-old Liverpool player, has postponed contract negotiations until after the season, despite receiving a £100,000-a-week offer. PFA chief Gordon Taylor supports Sterling's decision, noting it is a player's right to consider options, especially with two years left on his contract. Sterling has been linked with moves to Arsenal and Spanish clubs.

La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, 38, of Youngstown, Ohio, discovered her birth mother, Francine Simmons, worked at the same call-center as her and lived just six minutes away after accessing birth records. They reunited after Simmons received a Facebook message from a mutual friend. Mitchell-Clark also learned she has three younger sisters.

Oscar 'Papoo' Hernandez Jr, a gun trafficker, pleaded guilty to weapons charges related to sending weapons to Aaron Hernandez, who was convicted of murdering Odin Lloyd. Hernandez, 25, was sentenced to life in prison for the murder, while 'Papoo' faces up to 30 months in prison. 'Papoo' expressed being awed by Hernandez's fame and unaware of the impending murder.

Joel Parker, 33, was arrested in St Johns County, Florida, for throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head after threatening and disrupting the ride, according to police. He posted $250 bond and was issued a trespass warning, barred from using the bus again.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has discussed pre-season plans with striker Saido Berahino, indicating the player will stay beyond the summer transfer window. Berahino, 21, has expressed a desire to play in Champions League football and was linked with a £20 million move in January. Pulis praised Berahino's attitude and performance, stating the club is "more than happy to have him here."

Giovanni Lo Porto, an Italian aid worker, was abducted and killed in a 2012 U.S. drone strike in Pakistan, where he worked on reconstruction efforts following flooding. Lo Porto, a project manager for Welthungerlife, was one of two hostages killed in the operation, which also targeted an al Qaeda leader. His work focused on providing clean water and sanitation in Pakistan.
