Two UK county councils, Essex and Gloucestershire, have created 'loneliness maps' to identify areas with high risk of social isolation among pensioners and others. The maps, which consider factors like age, living alone, mental illness, and low income, help councils target assistance. The Campaign to End Loneliness calls for more councils to adopt this approach to address loneliness.

Dedicated waitress Judy Eddingfield celebrated 50 years of working at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, where she started at age 15. Her mother had already been working there for 13 years when Eddingfield began. Eddingfield, who considers the restaurant her home away from home, has seen it through its early days and has worked alongside family members and friends.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not return to the national team immediately despite scoring runs for Surrey, as Gary Ballance, Ian Bell, and Joe Root are performing well. Gatting also expressed concerns about Alastair Cook's form and suggested his future as captain could be questioned if he fails to score runs against West Indies.

A 17-year-old Californian student, Caleb Benn, developed an app called 'Uploader for Instagram' that allows users to upload photos to Instagram from their computer, earning him $1,000 a day. Instagram sent Benn an email claiming the app violated their terms of service, but Benn argues it would make the app pointless to fix.

In South Korea, "hoesik" involves frequent group drinking sessions at work, often with multiple rounds of alcohol. This practice is deeply ingrained in Korean culture, seen as a way to build relationships, though foreign workers may initially find it challenging. Drinking etiquette, such as deferring to seniors and "one-shotting" glasses, is crucial to avoid offending colleagues. Traffic patterns in Seoul reflect this drinking culture, with rush hour traffic correlating with drinking nights.

The Duke of Kent, 79, was discharged from Aberdeen Royal Infirmary after being treated for a dislocated hip he suffered at Balmoral estate. He left the hospital with a walking stick. This comes two years after he had a mild stroke.

Local business leaders in Surfers Paradise, Queensland, have called for the end of the 50-year tradition of Meter Maids, young women in bikinis who enforce parking meters, due to outdated practices and anti-touting laws. The Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce president argues they no longer provide a public service and should move on, while Meter Maids' general manager defends their cultural significance.

Greece denied it would fail to pay a £330 million loan to the IMF, stating it would make the payment on time. Deputy finance minister Dimitris Mardas said Greece is prioritizing wages and pensions over loans. Sources suggested Greece might go into a 'silent arrears process' with the IMF, while Germany's finance minister warned of potential eurozone exit if the payment is missed.

A Turkish court blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after the social media platforms refused to remove pictures of a prosecutor held during an armed siege. Mehmet Selim Kiraz, a 46-year-old Turkish prosecutor, died after being taken hostage by the DHKP-C, a terrorist group. The court imposed the blocks because the images deeply upset the prosecutor's family.

Seven-year-old Colin Gilpatric wrote to George Lucas about the Star Wars Jedi rule against marriage, fearing it might lead to becoming a Sith. Lucas responded, affirming that true Jedi values like friendship and compassion would protect against the dark side, and sent Colin Star Wars merchandise.

Wisconsin beat Kentucky 71-64 in the NCAA Tournament semi-finals, advancing to the final for the first time since 1941. Duke defeated Michigan State 81-61, securing another final appearance. Both teams will compete in Indianapolis on Monday.

Vince Neil of Mötley Crüe performed a poor rendition of the American national anthem at a Las Vegas football game, joining a list of musicians who have botched the anthem, including Whitney Houston, Roseanne Barr, Jimi Hendrix, and Michael Bolton.

In January, Barry Lyttle from Belfast punched his brother Patrick outside a Sydney bar, causing Patrick to fall unconscious and nearly lose his life. Security footage shown at Downing Centre Local Court revealed the incident, with Barry pleading guilty to grievous bodily harm. He faces up to two years in jail, though a possible suspended sentence is under consideration.

The parents of conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, who died 19 days after birth, found their gravesite at Pinegrove Memorial Park in Sydney's west completely cleared of memorabilia, leaving them devastated. The family had built a shrine with flowers, toys, and statues, which was removed without notice, with only about 25 percent of the items recovered from nearby rubbish bins.

Lord Neuberger, President of Britain's Supreme Court, suggested Muslim women should be allowed to wear full-face veils in court to show respect for different customs. He called for judges to be sensitive to the 'subconscious bias' when dealing with poorer members of society. This comes after a 2003 case where a Muslim woman was sentenced for refusing to remove her veil during testimony.

Andre Cole, 52, was executed by lethal injection in Missouri on Tuesday for killing Anthony Curtis in 1998 over child support payments. Cole, who was black, was convicted by an all-white jury and declined a last meal request. Governor Jay Nixon refused a clemency petition.

Prince Harry will depart the UK tonight for Australia without seeing his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge remains overdue for the birth of her second child. Harry, now fifth in line to the throne, had hoped to meet the new royal baby but will return in mid-May. He spent time with Prince George at Kensington Palace while waiting for the birth.

Florida man Justin Jackson, accused of posing as celebrities including Oprah Winfrey and Reggie Love, defrauded businesses of $2.4 million worth of goods and services over eight years. Jackson, also named in lawsuits by Oprah's TV network and former Obama aide Love, sent forged letters recommending himself for jobs at hotels and requested free items from jewelry and clothing companies.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini has set a €50 million price tag on Paulo Dybala, attracting interest from Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus, and Paris Saint-Germain. Inter Milan's Roberto Mancini watched Dybala play, but PSG is seen as the strongest bidder. Zamparini wants €50 million for Dybala, comparing him to Lionel Messi.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians protested against President Dilma Rousseff, demanding her impeachment due to an economic downturn and a bribery scandal at state-run oil company Petrobras. Rousseff's supporters counter-protested, defending her and her right to clean up corruption. Rousseff's approval rating dropped to 13% after the protests, and the economy is expected to contract with high inflation and currency devaluation.

Former Manchester United player Eric Cantona refuted claims that he starred in a soft porn film, insisting "You and the Night" is a piece of art. At the Laureus Sports Awards in Shanghai, Cantona defended the film, saying it is not porn but a beautiful work of art. The film includes racy scenes, such as Cantona on his hands and knees in just his underwear, alongside actress Beatrice Dalle.

Psychologists found that listening to certain music can enhance food flavors. For instance, The Beatles' music is served with fish and chips at Ultraviolent restaurant in Shanghai. Researchers also discovered that paired music can increase wine enjoyment by up to 15%. Behavioral psychologist Charles Spence explained that while music cannot create flavors, it can draw attention to specific notes in food and wine.

Raheem Sterling, a 20-year-old Liverpool player, has postponed contract negotiations until after the season, despite receiving a £100,000-a-week offer. PFA chief Gordon Taylor supports Sterling's decision, noting it is within his rights to consider his options.

La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, 38, of Youngstown, Ohio, discovered her birth mother, Francine Simmons, worked at the same call-center company and lived just six minutes away after accessing her birth records. They reunited after Mitchell-Clark found Simmons on Facebook and they have three younger sisters in common.

Oscar 'Papoo' Hernandez Jr, a gun trafficker, pleaded guilty to weapons charges related to sending weapons to Aaron Hernandez, who was convicted of Odin Lloyd's murder. Hernandez, 25, was sentenced to life in prison. Papoo Hernandez, 24, said he was awed by Hernandez's fame and shipped three guns, including a rifle and two handguns, in April 2013, a month before Lloyd's killing.

Joel Parker, 33, was arrested in St Johns County, Florida, for throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head after threatening and disrupting the ride. He posted $250 bond and received a trespass warning, barred from using the bus again.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis discussed pre-season plans with striker Saido Berahino, indicating Berahino will stay beyond the summer transfer window. Berahino, 21, has expressed a desire to play in Champions League football and was linked to a £20 million move in January. Pulis praised Berahino's attitude and performance.

Giovanni Lo Porto, an Italian aid worker, was abducted and later killed in a U.S. drone strike in Pakistan in 2012 while working on reconstruction efforts following flooding. The strike also killed another hostage and an al Qaeda leader. Lo Porto, a Peace and Conflict Studies graduate, was working with the German aid organization Welthungerlife in Pakistan.

A photographer in Florida captured images of hundreds of sharks, believed to be Blacktips or Spinners, swarming just 100 feet from a beach on Thursday. The sharks were migrating north to breed in shallower waters. The photos, shared over 2,000 times, showed the intimidating sight along Sebastian Inlet.

An 11-year-old retired German Shepherd K-9 officer named Zeus was honored with a grand procession in Ridgefield, Connecticut, before being put down due to severe health issues. The tribute, attended by fellow officers and residents, included a parade through the town, with Zeus riding in a patrol car for the last time. Zeus served the Ridgefield Police Department for eight years, assisting in over 250 narcotics arrests and locating 50 missing or wanted individuals.

Reports of child sex abuse cases increased by over 60% since 2011, with nearly 9,000 reports filed in 2014, following investigations like Operation Yewtree and the Rotherham scandal. However, the number of arrests fell by nine percent, prompting criticism of the government's response to child abuse.

Iceland has become a popular filming location, with 17 production services companies now operating there. Notable locations include Thingvellir National Park for Game of Thrones, Svartalfheim for Thor: The Dark World, and the Svinafellsjokull glacier for Interstellar. Filmmakers also used Dettifoss for Prometheus and Reykjanes Peninsula for battle scenes in Letters from Iwo Jima and Flags of Our Fathers.

A 100-year-old bathing box in Melbourne sold for $276,000, breaking records for such historic structures. In Sydney, a 1917 fire station turned mechanic’s garage sold for $1.2 million to be converted into a home. Additionally, an 1850s maximum security prison in Kilmore, Victoria, listed for $2 million after being renovated into a residence.

Samantha Rawcliffe, 40, from Morecambe, lost control of her body and crashed her car in May 2022 due to a rare brain disorder, later diagnosed as functional neurological disorder. She now struggles with severe symptoms, including loss of bladder control and inability to walk, and relies on a mobility scooter and 32 daily medications.

Sculptor Dave Poulin, who created a controversial statue of Lucille Ball in Celoron, New York, admitted it was "unsettling" and offered to replace it for free. The statue, based on Ball's intoxicated pitch for a health tonic, was nicknamed 'Scary Lucy' and sparked a social media campaign to remove it. Poulin estimates the new statue would cost $8,000 to $10,000 to recast.

David Alaba, Bayern Munich's left-back, will miss the team's final games for about seven weeks after tearing his knee ligament while playing for Austria. The injury, which comes after a previous three-month absence this season, could affect Bayern's pursuit of a treble.

Beatrice Nokes, 21, daughter of two respected solicitors, appeared in court facing charges of inciting a prostitution ring in Central London. She is accused of working with Daniel Williams, a suspended police officer, to run the ring, while Williams also faced additional charges including voyeurism and hiding profits.

A firm called Sequester, linked to Alchemy Direct Media, offered NHS patient data, including details of eating disorder sufferers, for sale at 12p per person. The Information Commissioner’s Office, the Direct Marketing Commission, and the General Pharmaceutical Council launched investigations into the data breaches. The data included personal and financial information, raising concerns about privacy and potential fraud.

Jordan Spieth won the Masters tournament at Augusta, becoming the second-youngest champion and the fifth to lead from start to finish. He expressed his wish for his autistic sister Ellie to try on the green jacket and reflected on how she provides him perspective. Spieth, born in Dallas, achieved his childhood dream of wearing the green jacket after a dominant performance.

Dick Advocaat, taking charge of Sunderland for their first home game, learned from his past mistake of downplaying the Old Firm derby's significance in 1998, vowing not to repeat it. Sunderland, struggling in the relegation zone, face Newcastle in a crucial match, with Advocaat emphasizing the importance of three points.

A dispute erupted in Bondi when Belinda Bartholomew, girlfriend of rugby player Aidan Guerra, claimed she was racially abused by a butcher who refused to serve her. The butcher denies the claims, stating he was dealing with eftpos issues and that Bartholomew was being rude.

Cadbury has reduced the size of its Freddo Frogs by 20% from 15g to 12g while keeping the price the same, citing increased manufacturing costs. This follows a previous reduction in the size of their Dairy Milk family blocks. Customers have expressed anger and disappointment on Cadbury's Facebook page.

Hillary Clinton's campaign held a meeting in Brooklyn to outline its values and strategy for the 2016 presidential race, aiming to avoid past mistakes. The campaign will focus on economic prosperity and maintain humility and discipline. Clinton is set to announce her candidacy on Sunday via social media and will then visit Iowa and New Hampshire.

Kyli Wilfson, 29, battled chronic pancreatitis for a year and a half, unable to eat despite feeling perpetually hungry. Diagnosed at 26, she lost 30 pounds and postponed her wedding due to frequent hospitalizations. The rare condition, affecting less than 0.01% of people, left her dependent on a feeding tube.

Party leaders' debate memes featured Labour leader Ed Miliband superimposed over Plan B, challenging David Cameron to a debate, and Conservative leader David Cameron and deputy Nick Clegg shown on the Gogglebox sofa, with other leaders like Nicola Sturgeon and Nigel Farage included in various humorous images.

Amir Khan is set to potentially face Manny Pacquiao in a fight in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, after initially being close to challenging Floyd Mayweather. Khan, who recently received Pakistan's President's Award for Pride In Performance, is eager for the fight and sees it as a dream to box in the Middle East. Promoter Bob Arum is considering the match for November or December and sees Khan as a strong opponent for Pacquiao.

A tiny two-bedroom home in Islington, London, measuring only 5ft wide in some areas, sold for £750,000, nearly double its 2001 price. The property, described as a 'stylish two bedroom period house' with a 'pretty rear garden', has garnered significant interest despite its narrow dimensions.

Nicola Sturgeon unveiled an SNP manifesto with policies aimed at forming a power-sharing deal with Labour, including slashing English tuition fees, rolling back NHS competition, and halting benefit changes. The manifesto, which includes £180 billion in spending over five years, could give the SNP significant influence in a potential Labour minority government, potentially altering UK policy and constitutional dynamics.

Celtic U17 team beat Rangers 2-0 to win the Glasgow Cup at Hampden Park, with goals from Josh Kerr and Mark Hill. Rangers keeper Robby McCrorie made two mistakes that led to Celtic's goals. The match was played behind closed doors due to fan troubles in previous finals.

Tony Pulis led West Bromwich Albion to a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace, wearing his trademark cap, track suit, and white trainers. Pulis stated he will never change his pre-game attire, despite the team's improved performance in the Premier League. The win secured West Brom's safety in the league.

Jameela Jamil spent £3,000 to replace her amalgam fillings with white fillings after experiencing health issues linked to high mercury levels from the dental work. She had ten amalgam fillings removed and replaced, though dental experts say the amount of mercury released is minimal and there is no significant risk from amalgam fillings.

Suge Knight, co-founder of Death Row Records, laughed in court as he revealed hopes that Floyd Mayweather will bail him out after his next fight. Knight's bail was denied, remaining at $10 million, as he faces trial for murder and attempted murder. Knight's attorney believes Mayweather, a champion boxer and friend, will cover the cost after winning his upcoming match against Manny Pacquiao.

TV chef Gizzi Erskine, 35, featured in a cat magazine with her British shorthair Kimchi, who enjoys human food like poppadoms and taramasalata. The cat has a discerning palate and is on a diet due to her love for such delicacies. Erskine also introduced a new cat, Ponzu, who was found paw-deep in green curry at a Thai takeaway.

Martin Springall, a father from Tokyo, took a photo of his daughter in Japan in 2014, which went viral due to a mysterious pair of black boots appearing behind her. Springall, who initially did not notice the boots, insists the photo was not Photoshopped and that no one else was present. The image sparked debate on Reddit about whether it was a trick of the light or something more.

Home Secretary Theresa May announced plans to ban unemployed EU migrants from receiving welfare benefits for four years, requiring them to pay taxes and national insurance first. This includes a £22,600 tax burden for average-wage workers over four years. The measures aim to reduce migration from poorer EU countries and will be part of negotiations for a new deal with the EU.

Cody Neatis, an eight-year-old boy with Down's syndrome, epilepsy, and autism, was forced to sleep on the floor for seven nights in Royal Preston Hospital due to a lack of a suitable bed. His mother, Lynne Neatis, has slept with him to watch him and ensure his safety. Cody needs a high-sided cot to prevent him from injuring himself, but the hospital does not have one. Lynne has been advocating for such a bed for two years.

Rory McIlroy forgot his golf clubs while getting excited at Augusta National, Ian Poulter. Henrik Stenson is recovering from flu and may surprise with his performance. Tiger Woods will play with his children, Charlie and Sam, in a par-three tournament. Gene Sarazen's albatross on the 15th hole 80 years ago is remembered, and players attempt to skip balls into the 16th hole's water.

Juventus ruled out signing Manchester United's Radamel Falcao due to his high wages, despite initial interest. The club remains interested in Palermo's Paulo Dybala and Paris Saint-Germain's Edinson Cavani for their forward line.

David Cameron pledges to sell £4 billion worth of Lloyds Bank shares if re-elected, offering a discount and a loyalty bonus, aiming to pay down national debt and revive 1980s-style privatisation. This sale would be the largest since the Thatcher era.

Scientists found that living near congested roads with high air pollution increases the risk of silent strokes, which can lead to brain shrinkage and dementia. The study, involving over 900 people aged 60 and over, linked higher PM2.5 levels with a 46% higher risk of silent strokes. Researchers used MRI scans to measure brain matter and found that air pollution can cause insidious effects even in individuals without dementia or stroke history.

Jessica Ainscough, 30, died in late February from epithelioid sarcoma after undergoing radiation treatment in her final weeks, choosing this option over chemotherapy and Gerson Therapy. Her partner, Tallon Pamenter, revealed she integrated conventional and alternative medicine, showing courage and grace throughout her seven-year battle.

A multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway near Fernvale involved ten people, including four children, on Wednesday afternoon. Three vehicles collided, resulting in several injuries; a 40-year-old man and a five-year-old boy were flown to Princess Alexandra Hospital, while a 27-year-old woman and a six-year-old girl were taken to Ipswich Hospital. Six others, including an infant and two young girls, were treated for minor injuries at Ipswich Hospital. Emergency crews freed one trapped person using hydraulic cutting gear, and the highway was closed with diversions in place.

Jason McDonald, a 34-year-old gator farm volunteer from Colorado, walked a slackline over a pool containing over 50 alligators, some up to ten feet long, at the Colorado Gator Farm. McDonald, who has interacted with alligators for over a decade, aimed to create a new way of engaging with the creatures and plans to walk over larger alligators and albino gators.

Abdul Hadi Arwani, a Syrian imam and activist, was shot dead in North West London after visiting the area with his son days before. The man who called Arwani for a building quote is a prime suspect, as he postponed the meeting, possibly to avoid Arwani's son. Scotland Yard is investigating whether the man was a hired killer, considering Arwani's links to the Muslim Brotherhood and his opposition to Syrian President Bashar Al-Assad.

In Hong Kong, there is a surge in demand for Jenny's butter cookies, leading to long lines and a black market where knockoffs are sold. The original bakery warns against buying fakes, while others sell knockoff cookies at a higher price. This trend is part of a global phenomenon where foods like cronuts and ramen burgers have sparked similar frenzies.

Kira Hollis, a 27-year-old from Tamworth, Staffordshire, overcame anorexia and depression by becoming a bodybuilder after being diagnosed with borderline personality disorder. She weighed just 6st when diagnosed but is now 9.5st and a personal trainer. Her six-year-old daughter Olivia and medication from her doctor also helped in her recovery.

Jockey Lewis Ferguson, 18, survived a spectacular double somersault fall from Merrion Square during a race at Wincanton, an incident viewed by hundreds of thousands online. Ferguson returned to work at the stables the next day, showing a cut on his nose and expressing his determination to continue racing. The fall, deemed the worst by Wincanton clerk Barry Johnson, did not deter Ferguson from his ambitions, including competing at the Cheltenham Festival and Aintree.

Hillary Clinton launched her presidential campaign with a video and road trip aimed at rebranding herself and reframing her image as more empathetic and relatable. Critics, including Washington Post columnist Ruth Marcus and comedian Jon Stewart, were harsh, but the campaign may have successfully presented a more confident and forward-looking image. The new logo and road trip, particularly her unscripted stop at Chipotle, are key elements of this rebranding and reframing strategy.

More than 1,700 Chinese high school freshmen in Yichuan, Shaanxi province, took an exam in their school's playground due to insufficient indoor space. The students organized the outdoor exam themselves, taking measures to avoid sun dazzle, and said it helped broaden their horizons and reduce stress.

Sportsmail and Gillette are hosting a competition where one lucky reader can win a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Joe Hart, Manchester City and England goalkeeper, along with a Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor and shaving gel. The competition ends on April 19.

Kecil, a baby orangutan rejected by his natural and surrogate mothers, found a loving home with 53-year-old Maggie at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. After 10 months of care, Kecil and Maggie will make their first public appearance this weekend. The pair bonded when Kecil sought comfort from Maggie during a fire alarm scare.

Noelle Baynham, a 61-year-old from Winchester, Hampshire, died after an accidental overdose of medication and was partially eaten by her two dogs, a Jack Russell and a Staffordshire Bull Terrier, when her body lay undiscovered for days. Her friend Grant Donovan discovered her body on January 17, 2023, after she failed to answer the door. The pathologist could not determine the exact cause of death due to the dogs' consumption of her organs.

French handball star Nikola Karabatic, along with 15 others, is set to stand trial for fraud in an illegal betting case involving a match-fixing incident during his time with Montpellier. Karabatic, who now plays for Barcelona, denies the charges and faces up to five years in prison and a fine if found guilty.

A gang of six men, including Ahmed Hassan-Sule, were convicted and sentenced to a total of 31 years in jail for sexually abusing teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire, from 2009 to 2014. The abuse occurred at parties organized by the gang, which they lured victims to using social media. Sentencing judge Zoe Smith highlighted the defendants' use of charity events to raise their profile among young people.

Aaron Hernandez, convicted of Odin Lloyd's murder, faces three more trials, including a murder case for killing two men and wounding another near a Boston nightclub in 2012. The case involves multiple civil suits and asset freezes, and Hernandez's legal team is preparing for upcoming trials.

Emirates Airline is set to rebrand the FA Cup for £30 million over three years, expanding its portfolio of sporting sponsorships. The deal includes existing agreements with Arsenal worth £150 million, AC Milan worth £80 million, and Hamburg worth £17 million.

Michael Phelps announced his intention to compete in a fifth Olympics in Rio next year, despite not swimming in the upcoming world championships as punishment for his second DUI arrest. The 29-year-old swimmer, who has qualified in three events, is undergoing alcohol rehabilitation and has enrolled in Alcoholics Anonymous.

Gareth Bale is a major doubt for Real Madrid's Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid due to a calf injury. Real Madrid are also without Luka Modric, who suffered a knee ligament strain. Karim Benzema is hoped to be fit for the match. Real were drawn to a goalless first leg against Atletico.

A study by scientists at Texas Tech University found that older people sold their investments impulsively during the 2007-2008 financial crisis, leading to significant financial losses. The research, involving 1,204 retirees, showed that those with better cognitive abilities were less likely to make emotional investment decisions. This comes as new UK pension reforms allow individuals turning 55 to access their savings, potentially increasing the risk of emotional decision-making.

Stuart Pearce advocates for Manchester City to retain Manuel Pellegrini, citing the manager's experience and the need to refresh the squad. City's recent poor performance, including a defeat to Manchester United, has raised questions about Pellegrini's future, but Pearce believes the club should give him more time. Yaya Toure's decline is highlighted as a key factor in City's struggles.

Manchester United trained in preparation for their upcoming Premier League match against Manchester City, with key players like Wayne Rooney and Robin van Persie returning to action. The game, to be played at Old Trafford on Sunday, sees Manchester United leading the Premier League table for the first time since Sir Alex Ferguson's era, with victory potentially moving them four points ahead of City.

Fiorentina lost 1-0 to Verona in a match where Verona's Mounir Obbadi scored a late winner after Fiorentina's Alessandro Diamanti missed a penalty. The loss leaves Fiorentina nine points behind third-placed AS Roma in the league, with their hopes of Champions League qualification fading.

At the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Miley Cyrus went unshaven, displaying armpit hair, which sparked controversy and debate on social media. While some criticized her appearance, others defended her right to choose her own grooming habits.

Barcelona's Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez scored their 102nd combined goal of the season in a 6-0 victory over Getafe, taking them five points clear in La Liga. Messi leads with 49 goals, Neymar has 32, and Suarez has 21. Their goals are predominantly from inside the box, with Messi showing ambidextrous skill. Barcelona's win increases their goal difference to +78, putting pressure on Real Madrid.

A 44-year-old woman named Andrea McVeigh was knocked down by a cyclist on the pavement in Bermondsey, south London, on April 14, suffering significant facial injuries. The cyclist fled the scene, and police have issued CCTV footage for help in identifying him. McVeigh is scarred for life and off work due to her injuries.

Paul Gregory, 51, of Bedford, was fined £795 and ordered to do 150 hours of unpaid work after he misrepresented his physical abilities to obtain a blue badge, despite being a keen walker and mountaineer. Council officials discovered his fraud through a newspaper article detailing his 191-mile hike.

Apple has been awarded a patent for a facial recognition system that automatically unlocks iPhones when the device is moved into a specific position and the user's face is detected, potentially offering a more convenient alternative to current unlocking methods. The patent, filed in March 2011, was recently awarded and describes a system that uses the front-facing camera to scan a user's face and unlock the device if it matches a stored image.

Elizabeth Sedway, 51, was ejected from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California because she lacked a doctor's note, despite having multiple myeloma. Her family was also removed from the plane.

On Easter Sunday, a 1973 E-Type Jaguar worth over $120,000 collided with a Toyota Kluger on Warringah Road in Frenchs Forest, northern Sydney, resulting in the complete write-off of the vintage car. All three adults involved were taken to hospital as a precaution, though no one was injured. Police are investigating the circumstances.

Google has established a four-man team since 2012 to develop advanced battery technologies, including flexible, wearable, and subfreezing temperature batteries, for use in smartphones, electric cars, and other devices. The team, led by former Apple battery expert Dr. Ramesh Bhardwaj, works on projects like Google's Project Loon, which requires batteries that function in extreme temperatures.

The 223ft Explorer, a superyacht designed by Tony Castro, comes with features like a helipad, infinity pool, and space for a helicopter, submarine, and multiple water toys, costing around 40 million euros to build. It can accommodate 12 guests and 15 crew members, offering various amenities and luxury spaces.

Ed Miliband pressed on with plans to cap rents despite warnings from experts that the measure would reduce housing investment and potentially worsen tenant conditions. His proposal, which includes three-year tenancies and rent caps tied to inflation, faced criticism from business leaders and even some Labour figures. Critics argued the plan had loopholes that could incentivize evictions and fail to control long-term rent increases.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town supporter who hoped Arsenal would win was removed as a mascot for Reading in their FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal. The decision followed outrage from Reading fans after a video of him backing Arsenal was shared. The Football Association moved him to a mascot role for England instead.

Astronomers have proposed a giant supervoid 1.8 billion light-years across as an explanation for the 'Cold Spot' in the cosmic microwave background radiation, a region 20% less dense than other areas. The supervoid, discovered by the Institute for Astronomy at the University of Hawaii, is the largest structure ever found and could account for the Cold Spot's lower energy and temperature.

The chair where Abraham Lincoln was shot in 1865 will be displayed open to the public at The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, on April 15 for the 150th anniversary of his assassination. Historian Doris Kearns Goodwin will give a lecture about Lincoln the day before. The chair, part of the museum since 1932, will be removed from its enclosure for the first time in 85 years.

A 19-year-old man from East Sussex, Jake Boys, surprised his girlfriend Emily-Victoria Canham with One Direction concert tickets but booked flights to Dublin instead of Cardiff. The mix-up was discovered when Canham, a model from Northamptonshire, tweeted about the mistake. Boys, an Arsenal supporter and YouTube vlogger, plans to buy train tickets to correct the error.

Romanian company MB Telecom has developed the Roboscan 2M Aeria, a mobile X-ray scanner that can detect contraband, bombs, and weapons in planes. Costing €3 million, the device, already used to seize 76,000 packs of illegal cigarettes, can scan an entire plane in about 20 minutes and is aimed at plugging security gaps at small private airports.

Stephen Munden, a 54-year-old convicted paedophile with an obsession for young girls, went missing from a psychiatric unit in Hampshire, UK, after vanishing at 6:15 PM on Tuesday. Munden, described as having a "fanatical obsession" with small girls, was last seen leaving a hospital near Hook. Police are searching for him, believing he may have shaved off his beard.

Middlesbrough are leading the Championship with just four weeks left, having won seven points over second-place Bournemouth and third-place Norwich. Their advantage includes a favorable match timing and a strong defense led by captain Jonathan Woodgate, who has won five of his five appearances this season. The race for promotion remains volatile, with Watford and Norwich also in contention.

A global trend of embracing grey hair has emerged, with social media users sharing images under the hashtag #grannyhair. The trend, inspired by fashion shows and celebrity choices, reflects a defiant feminist statement and a move away from traditional hair dyeing. Models and influencers, including Jean Paul Gaultier's runway models and celebrities like Rihanna and Kelly Osborne, have showcased the look.

Randy and Jodi Speidel, from Bellefontaine, Ohio, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning in late April, less than two months after creating online fundraisers in February to seek financial help due to their chronic conditions and dire living conditions. The couple, who left behind two daughters, had been struggling to pay bills and had limited food and water.

Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg vowed to remain as party leader despite potential electoral losses, emphasizing the risk of Labour and Conservative parties vacating the center ground. Clegg expressed optimism about his party's prospects and his willingness to lead through the next Parliament. Business Secretary Vince Cable indicated a desire to become Chancellor if the Lib Dems form another coalition with the Conservatives.

A 79-year-old pensioner, Terry Cooper, was saved from a large badger by his Jack Russell dog, Sam, in Curry Rivel, Somerset. The badger, about the size of a pig with six-inch teeth, burst into Cooper's garden with cubs. Cooper covered the garden gap with metal and compost. The National Farmers' Union advised residents to protect their properties with badger-proof fencing and secure bins.
Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose 3-0 to Porto U21s at Motspur Park, while Real Madrid progressed to the Champions League semi-finals with a 1-0 win over Atletico Madrid.

Property developer Andreas Christopheros, 29, was severely injured in a December acid attack outside his Truro home, leaving him with life-changing injuries. Nicole Phillips, 45, and her husband David, 48, have been charged; David pleaded not guilty at Truro Crown Court.

In the Spanish town of Lastres, signs warning against defecating along the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route have been posted, though no one knows who put them up. The signs, which show a squatting figure defecating within a red circle with a diagonal line, have become an attraction for pilgrims, who now pose for photos with them. The pilgrimage, which attracts thousands of walkers, lacks public facilities for nature breaks, leading locals to complain.

A massive fire consumed a building that was once home to a Michigan strip club named The Body Shop in Flint, Michigan, on Wednesday afternoon. The blaze started around 1pm and affected only the building itself and nearby power lines. Local resident Terry Rauh reported a previous fire at the site. An investigation into the cause continues.

Shoshana Hebshi, a woman of Arab and Jewish descent, received $40,000 in compensation after being strip-searched at Detroit Metropolitan Airport on the 10th anniversary of 9/11. The federal government, Frontier Airlines, TSA, and Wayne County Airport Authority were named in her lawsuit.

An Asiana Airlines flight from Seoul to Hiroshima crash-landed and skidded off the runway, injuring 20 people. The Airbus A320 missed the landing point and spun 180 degrees, closing the airport. Emergency services are treating the injured and investigating the incident.

Mark-Francis Vandelli, 26, from the TV show Made In Chelsea, revealed his collection of 16 expensive watches, including a £32,000 Cartier white gold Moonphase and a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42, worth £6,500. He has been collecting watches since his teens and favors a Cartier Tortue Collection Privée that is no longer produced.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy, 89, is auctioning over 200 antiques, including a £4,000 diorama of the Battle of Agincourt, to downsize his home. The auction, set for Saturday in Gloucestershire, includes furniture, swords, and books dating back to the 17th century.

Brazilian commuter Nelson Felippe posted a photo on Facebook of two women hugging on a train platform, warning against public safety violations and inadvertently mocking homophobia, which went viral with over 100,000 shares.

Jonathan Stevenson, now a LiveWire Sport director, shared a letter from Richie Benaud, dated September 27, 1996, in tribute to the cricket legend. Benaud provided detailed advice on left-handed leg spin bowling, including various deliveries and techniques, to Stevenson when Stevenson was 16.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg envisions a future where virtual reality will replace long-haul flights, allowing users to explore the world through 3D scenes and VR headsets like Oculus Rift. Marriott hotels have also tested VR for travel experiences.

Guo Kai and Dong Hui, who met a year ago, had to postpone their wedding due to Dong's serious bone cancer. Instead, friends helped Dong dress in a wedding gown, and professional photographers took wedding photos at her bedside in Sichuan, China. Guo, now a firefighter, has been at Dong's bedside every hour to support her through her treatment.

A 34-year-old man, Blaine Boudreaux, killed two people and injured others in three separate drunk driving crashes in Houston, including the death of 6-year-old Joshua Medrano. Boudreaux, who has a history of DUIs, was charged with intoxication manslaughter and other offenses.

Microsoft has launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions at its Redmond campus, partnering with Specialisterne. The initiative, announced by Mary Ellen Smith, aims to expand opportunity and create a diverse workforce.

Two deputies involved in the fatal arrest of Eric Harris in Tulsa, Oklahoma, have been reassigned due to safety concerns after being criticized for pinning Harris to the ground. Reserve Deputy Robert Bates, who shot Harris, is charged with second-degree manslaughter. Sheriff Stanley Glanz has suspended the drug unit and is reviewing the deputies' actions, pending the Bates case outcome.

Katie Prager, 24, and her husband Dalton, 24, are seeking help for Katie to receive a lung transplant; her condition is worsening due to cystic fibrosis and an infection. Kentucky Medicaid will not cover the out-of-state treatment needed at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center, leaving the couple with limited options.

Using data from the Sleep Cycle app, researchers found that people wake up earliest on Mondays in South Africa, while the best sleep quality occurs on Wednesdays, particularly in China. Americans rise at 7am on Tuesdays and are the unhappiest on that day, but sleep in the latest and report the best wake-up mood on Fridays.

Mexican artist Frida Kahlo's 25 unpublished love letters to her lover Jose Bartoli, written between 1946 and 1949, are expected to sell for over $120,000 at auction in New York on April 15. The passionate correspondence, saved by Jose until his death in 1995, includes details of their secret romance and Frida's artistic inspirations.

Len McCluskey, leader of the Unite union, campaigned for Labour in South Wales, despite his controversial past as a militant socialist. His union's significant influence over Labour candidates and its push for 1970s-style socialism, including more strikes and expanded public sector, poses a potent threat to British politics.

Zookeeper Elad Hershkowitz in Tel Aviv captured unique animal drinking behaviors using a GoPro camera placed in water troughs for 30 hours, resulting in a 4-minute video showing various methods, from a rhino almost kissing the water to a lemur delicately licking it.

A poll shows that only 25% of voters think David Cameron is most eager to win the election, compared to 43% for Ed Miliband. Despite criticism of a dull campaign, Cameron insisted he was working "bloody hard." More voters believe Miliband is more enthusiastic about winning, with 43% of respondents saying so, compared to 25% for Cameron.

Zaur Dadaev, one of five Chechen men accused of murdering Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov, retracted his confession in court, claiming he was beaten and pressured into confessing. Human rights activists found signs of torture on Dadaev's body.

A photo of baby Sonit Awal being pulled from rubble became a defining image of the Nepal earthquake that killed over 5,000 people. Sonit, just four months old, was trapped for 22 hours after his home collapsed during the 7.8-magnitude quake on April 25. Rescuers found him by hearing faint cries and lifted him to safety on Sunday morning, finding him uninjured.

A Church of Scientology-backed organization, Narcocon, is trying to change the land designation of Trout Run, near Camp David, to build a drug rehab center using controversial methods like saunas and vitamin therapy. Opponents argue the move is a ploy to circumvent zoning laws and that the program is dangerous. Narcocon, which has faced lawsuits for wrongful deaths, claims its approach is non-religious and effective.

In Kabul, five Afghans who spoke English and worked for NATO have been fired and blacklisted, leaving them jobless and fearing for their safety. The city's population has grown significantly, with many fleeing violence in the provinces, while once bustling areas now appear deserted due to security warnings and the end of foreign presence.

Two US Navy SEALs died and one was critically injured while swimming in a pool at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story in Virginia on Friday. Both were assigned to Naval Special Warfare Group Two. An investigation into the incident is ongoing.

NBC, with Rebecca Lowe leading the coverage, has significantly increased US interest in the Premier League, with live viewers in the US now exceeding those in Britain. This weekend, NBC moved their entire production to England to enhance coverage, with Lowe and other experts attending key matches.

Boris Johnson verbally attacked Ed Miliband on the Andrew Marr Show, calling him "better than that" and saying he would do more damage to the country than to his brother David, who lost the Labour leadership to him in 2010. Miliband responded humorously, while the exchange turned into a shouting match.

Dustin Irons, a prisoner in Oregon, was sentenced to an extra 30 days in jail for flashing a judge during a court hearing, despite being in handcuffs. The incident occurred via video-link from the Umatilla County Jail.

Jenson Button believes McLaren has made significant progress ahead of the Chinese Grand Prix, having seen improvement in pace compared to midfield teams like Force India, Sauber, and Lotus during the Malaysian Grand Prix. Despite challenges, Button is optimistic about their chances in Shanghai.

The Fiona Stanley Hospital in Perth faced criticism after blood and bone fragments were found on supposedly sanitized medical instruments, despite a $60,000 fine and auditing of Serco, the previous medical service provider. The hospital's reputation and staff morale are further damaged by these findings, following other controversies including a patient death.
Becca Litchfield and Dale, from Nottingham, gave up their dream wedding to fund IVF, which led to them winning a wedding competition and eventually having twins, Darci-Mai and Stanley.

Scooter's Coffee in Omaha had its Facebook page hacked for 24 hours on March 29, 2015, when an employee clicked a malicious link, leading to the page being flooded with pornography. The company regained control only after contacting other businesses, not Facebook directly.

A Shibu Inu at an American Kennel Club centre attempted to bark but only made high-pitched squeaking and whining sounds, causing amusement among onlookers. The video shows the puppy trying to communicate with a husky, with both dogs making various vocalisations.

Liam Plunkett, a 29-year-old England seamer, aims to challenge West Indies' batsmen with his pace in the upcoming Test series. Recovered from an ankle injury, Plunkett seeks to prove himself, competing with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood for a spot. He emphasizes his adaptability and willingness to disrupt batters, despite likely competition from James Anderson and Stuart Broad.

Paul Smith is set to face reigning world super-middleweight champion Andre Ward in a non-title fight, potentially as a warm-up for a possible rematch with Carl Froch. The WBA has ordered Ward and Froch to unify their titles, but Ward prefers to fight in London rather than Nottingham. Meanwhile, Froch aims for his first Las Vegas fight against Julio Cesar Chavez Jr.

After Tyrus Byrd, the new black mayor of Parma, Missouri, was sworn in, five of the city's six police officers, the city attorney, clerk, and water treatment supervisor resigned, citing safety concerns, leaving the small town of 713 residents with a mayor who is unsure of the reasons behind the mass resignations.

Manchester City will make Yaya Toure available this summer but will not force him out, despite the club considering his future after a disappointing season. Toure, 31, remains committed to the team and is unlikely to move for less than his current £220,000-a-week salary. City will also resist Valencia's attempts to pull out of a £24m deal for Alvaro Negredo.

A new study found that more than two-thirds of people taking antidepressants in the U.S. did not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. Researchers analyzed selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), commonly prescribed for various psychiatric conditions. Official guidelines require five or more depressive symptoms over two weeks for a diagnosis of clinical depression.

Doris Fuller's daughter, Natalie, 28, with bipolar disorder and psychosis, killed herself in Baltimore last month. Fuller, who wrote about Natalie's struggles in the Washington Post, described how her daughter's condition worsened over years, despite treatment, and led to her suicide.

A 10-year-old boy named Koby Hodder suffered a cardiac arrest during a game of British Bulldog at school, collapsing for 12 minutes before being saved by CPR and a defibrillator. Teachers are calling for the game to be banned due to its perceived danger. Koby was diagnosed with the same heart condition as footballer Fabrice Muamba, who survived a similar cardiac arrest in 2012.

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain's most senior female judge, called for divorce laws in England and Wales to remove allegations of adultery and blame, aiming to reduce bitterness in matrimonial disputes and encourage couples to resolve child and financial arrangements before divorce.

Tottenham are considering a £400 million stadium with a retractable pitch for a potential NFL franchise, due to open in 2018. The new 65,000-capacity stadium could better suit American football than Wembley's 90,000 seats. The NFL is close to establishing a permanent London franchise.

U.S. senators, including Robert Menendez and Ron Johnson, wrote to FIFA, urging the organization to reconsider Russia's hosting of the 2018 World Cup due to Russia's involvement in the Ukraine crisis. England is considering bidding for the 2028 European Championship but not the 2026 World Cup while Sepp Blatter remains FIFA president.

Universal announced that the sequel to "Fifty Shades of Grey" will be released on February 10, 2017, and the third film on February 9, 2018. EL James's husband, Niall Leonard, will write the second film's script. The first film earned $568.8 million worldwide.

Tony Pulis, West Brom manager, faces another relegation battle despite his past successes in keeping teams in the Premier League. His worst record among long-serving managers, Pulis has never finished in the top half of the table in seven seasons. Upcoming tough fixtures against top teams could jeopardize his record of never being relegated.

Fenerbahce called for the suspension of the Turkish championship after their team bus was attacked by armed gunmen on Saturday, resulting in a wounded driver. The bus was returning from an away match when it was hit, with blood visible on the driver's seat and steering wheel. The club stated that solving the attack is vital for continuing the season.

A massive avalanche struck Everest Base Camp, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens more on Saturday. The earthquake triggered the snowslide, leaving climbers and local hires stranded and feared buried. Rescue efforts were hampered by aftershocks and impassable icefall routes, with helicopters evacuating some 200 people.

Gregory Margolin, an 87-year-old Jewish war veteran who fought in World War II, survived another war in Ukraine when a missile hit his house, killing his daughter. He and his family moved to Israel for safety. The International Fellowship of Christians and Jews has helped bring 600 Ukrainian Jews to Israel since the conflict began.

John Carver, assistant to former Newcastle manager Ruud Gullit, recalls Gullit's 1999 decision to bench Alan Shearer and Duncan Ferguson, leading to a 2-1 loss against Sunderland and Gullit's resignation. Carver, now fighting for the head coach position, knows the impact a derby win or loss could have on his future with the club.

Rev. Al Sharpton preached at Charity Missionary Baptist Church in North Charleston and addressed the Walter Scott case, meeting with local officials including Mayor Keith Summey and Police Chief Eddie Driggers. Sharpton is expected to attend a vigil near the shooting site.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers will speak to Raheem Sterling about his recent controversial behavior, including inhaling nitrous oxide and smoking a shisha pipe, after Sterling scored the opener in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United. Rodgers said Sterling, 20, will face internal club investigation.

Labour received over £1 million in union donations during the second week of the election campaign, more than twice the amount received by the Conservatives. Unions such as Unison and Unite contributed significantly, while the Liberal Democrats and UKIP received much less.

Passengers on a Qatar Airways flight from Birmingham to Doha revolted after being stranded for five hours on the tarmac due to severe winds. Police were called twice as passengers tried to disembark. The flight was later diverted to Manchester, where passengers faced further delays and frustration.

Justin Bieber will lead Floyd Mayweather's entourage into the ring for his $300 million fight against Manny Pacquiao on Saturday. The 21-year-old pop star has accompanied Mayweather to previous fights and will be there as long as Mayweather's daughter wants him.

Corinthian Colleges Inc., which once enrolled over 70,000 students, announced the closure of its 28 campuses, marking a significant step in holding for-profit colleges accountable. These colleges, which receive 86% of their funding from federal student loans, have high default rates and questionable educational value. The U.S. Department of Education has curtailed access to federal student aid for many such institutions, leading to calls for their closure and loan forgiveness for affected students.

Pep Guardiola denied a dispute with former Bayern Munich doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit after blaming the medical staff for the team's Champions League defeat by Porto. Guardiola took responsibility for the loss but said no rift existed between them.

Wladimir Klitschko, 39, prepares for his world title defense against Bryant Jennings at Madison Square Garden. Reflecting on his Olympic gold win in 1996, Klitschko credits sport for changing his life and motivating his career. He believes age is an advantage and looks forward to the fight.

Jeremy Clarkson, 54, admitted he would miss fronting Top Gear after being fired in March for attacking a producer. Former presenter Angela Rippon, 70, expressed interest in returning to the show. Clarkson was found to have launched an unprovoked attack on producer Oisin Tymon during filming.
In a La Liga match, Barcelona beat Celta Vigo 1-0. During the game, Celta Vigo's Fabian Orellana was shown a red card for throwing a lump of grass at Sergio Busquets, striking him in the neck.

In 2013, a bombing at the Boston Marathon killed three and injured over 200. In 2015, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was convicted of all 30 charges, including using weapons of mass destruction. The sentencing phase, set to begin April 21, will last four weeks.

Tens of millions of Chinese people marked the Tomb Sweeping Festival by visiting ancestral graves, burning paper money, and offering food. A grand ceremony honoring the Yellow Emperor Huangdi, considered the ancestor of the Chinese nation, was held in Shaanxi Province, with thousands attending. The festival, which falls in the first week of April, is one of 24 Chinese solar terms marking the start of spring.

Paul Simon, 73, topped the UK album chart with his "Ultimate Collection" for the first time in 25 years, outselling albums by younger artists like Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. His recent tour with Sting likely contributed to the success.

Iker Casillas, Real Madrid's goalkeeper, insists he will stay and fight for his position despite potential competition from Manchester United's David de Gea. Casillas, who has been at Real Madrid since 1996, hopes to fulfill his contract and continue his career with the team.

Britain's employment reached a record 31 million, with 557,000 more jobs in the three months to February compared to the same period last year. The International Monetary Fund and German finance minister praised Chancellor George Osborne's economic strategy, reducing the deficit from £153 billion to £90 billion. Prime Minister David Cameron hailed this as a 'jobs miracle,' with two million more people in work than in 2010.

SsangYong, known as 'two dragons', is launching the Tivoli SUV in the UK starting from £12,950, aiming to compete with the Nissan Juke. The Tivoli comes in three trim levels with features like seven airbags and a five-year warranty. SsangYong expects the Tivoli to double its UK sales to 4,000 annually.

Chef Sam Longhurst at Splendid Kitchen in Manchester created a 10-inch, 2,000-calorie burger called "The Whole Damn Farm" with six types of meat, priced at £13.50. The burger, containing two beef patties, bacon jam, ham, chicken, pulled pork, and bacon, weighs half a kilogram.

Yeo Valley's staff canteen, run by a Michelin-starred chef, offers high-quality, organic, and locally sourced meals to dairy workers for as little as £2. The menu changes daily and has been praised as the world's best staff canteen, now open to the public at higher prices.

B.B. King, 89, was hospitalized for dehydration caused by his Type II diabetes but has since returned home, thanking fans for their concern. He is known for his hits like "The Thrill Is Gone" and has been a Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inductee since 1987.

On Easter Sunday, New York's Fifth Avenue hosted an Easter parade featuring bizarre hats, with participants including Christians, Jews, Hindus, agnostics, and atheists. Highlights included a ship-shaped hat, a butterfly-topped headpiece, and a diorama inspired by Mayor Bill de Blasio.

The East of England ambulance service received 1,248 inappropriate calls in two years, including reports of a run-over squirrel, a bleeding burger, and a woman who ate too much takeaway. Front-line crews attended half of these calls, potentially affecting emergency response times.

Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake from Chelsea won a series of challenges against Loic Remy and Willian, including shooting balls into car boots and over a £127,000 Audi, but Willian accidentally broke a car's wing mirror during the long-range shooting.

Brendan Rodgers criticizes Raheem Sterling's advisor for potentially manipulating the player, stating Sterling would stay at Liverpool if left to decide. Rodgers revealed he spoke with Sterling about his contract and financial situation, advising him to stay despite interest from Arsenal. Sterling has rejected a £100,000-a-week contract and has two years left on his deal.

Rachel Riley was embarrassed on Countdown when contestants offered the word 'erection', which made Nick Hewer, the host, struggle to stifle his laughter. This is not the first time rude words have caused issues on the show, with previous incidents involving 'todgers', 'm*nges', and others.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, who tried to buy deadly poison on the dark web to commit suicide was spared jail after pleading guilty. He was arrested during a counter-terrorism operation and faced charges after officers tracked his online activity.

Lianne Hindle, 37, died of a cardiac arrest three hours after giving birth to her daughter Poppy at North Manchester General Hospital in December, prompting calls for action from her partner Chris Barnes. The hospital, along with Royal Oldham, is under investigation after 10 deaths in eight months. Ms Hindle's family is concerned about the care she received, alleging she was left alone with a student midwife.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after training while eight months pregnant. Pittman, a two-time world champion hurdler, continued training throughout her pregnancy and plans to compete in the Beijing World Championships and the 2016 Rio Olympics.

At least one person died when a powerful storm capsized several sailboats during the Dauphin Island regatta in Alabama on April 25, 2015. The Coast Guard searched for four missing individuals as crews rescued a man around 9 p.m. and reported scattered boats across Mobile Bay.

Roseanne Barr, 62, revealed she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma, which are worsening her vision. Her doctors have not provided a timeline, and there is no cure for these progressive eye diseases.

A 17-year-old named Chancey Allen Luna was convicted of first-degree murder in the 2013 shooting death of Australian college baseball player Christopher Lane in Duncan, Oklahoma. The jury recommended a life sentence without parole. Luna's defense argued he only meant to scare Lane.

Arsene Wenger insists his poor record against Jose Mourinho will not affect Arsenal's match against Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium. Wenger, who has lost 7 out of 12 games against Mourinho, says the result will depend on performance. Arsenal are 10 points behind Chelsea but are on a good run of form.

Manny Pacquiao, a Filipino boxer, is set to face Floyd Mayweather in a high-profile fight at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Pacquiao, who rose from poverty to become a global icon, has had a remarkable career, including victories over notable opponents like Oscar De La Hoya and Juan Manuel Marquez. The fight, dubbed the "Fight of the Century," is scheduled for Saturday and is expected to generate $300 million in revenue.

Jack Grealish, an outstanding Aston Villa player in their FA Cup win over Liverpool, was photographed inhaling nitrous oxide, a drug that can affect athletic performance. Arsenal's former manager Arsene Wenger emphasized the importance of professional athletes maintaining their health and avoiding substances that could harm their careers.

Sam Barton, who spent £55,000 on cosmetic surgery to resemble Joey Essex, was attacked on Easter Monday when a group of men pelted him with eggs after he checked into a pub on Facebook. Barton, 22, had already moved house due to online bullying.

Manchester University in Indiana was placed on lockdown late Friday night after receiving a 'likely prank call' about an armed person near the administration building. Police, a bomb squad, and Indiana State Police responded but decided it was a prank. Students were advised to barricade themselves in rooms and stay silent.

Edinson Cavani, known as "El Matador," faces Luis Suarez in a crucial Champions League quarter-final match between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona. Cavani, without key players Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Marco Veratti, must perform to help PSG advance, despite a recent goal drought.

Derry Mathews won the interim WBA lightweight title with a unanimous points decision over Tony Luis in Liverpool. Luis, drafted in at the last minute, could not overcome Mathews' control and was deducted points, while Mathews was also penalized for a low blow.

Hull recorded a surprising 28-20 victory over St Helens at Langtree Park, ending St Helens' three-game winning streak. Jamie Shaul's try proved decisive after Hull took an early lead and St Helens struggled with injuries and substitutions.

The U.S. immigrant population, including documented and undocumented, could reach 51 million by 2023, accounting for 14.8% of the population, and grow to 78 million by 2060, making up 82% of future population growth. This trend, driven by current policies, could lead to significant societal changes, as highlighted by the Center for Immigration Studies.

Jack Wilshere captained Arsenal Under 21s in a 1-0 loss to Reading, with Reading's Niall Keown scoring the only goal. Arsenal's other injured players, including Serge Gnabry and Abou Diaby, also featured in the match.

Justin Rose, who has been in the world's top five for the past three years, fell outside the top 10 after a poor performance in Florida. After two weeks of practice, Rose improved, scoring 69 in the first round of the Shell Houston Open, and is optimistic about his performance at the upcoming Masters.

A mansion in Mayfair, built on the site of a former milking parlour, is on the market for £25 million. The 8,139 square foot property, constructed in 2011, features modern amenities like an indoor pool, gym, and cinema room.

Bayern Munich, without several key players due to injuries, believes their unity is stronger and will help them in their Champions League quarter-final against Porto on April 15. Coach Pep Guardiola aims for a Treble and emphasizes focusing on the available players.

Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited Mercedes' Brackley base to strategize against Ferrari after Sebastian Vettel's victory in the Malaysian Grand Prix. Hamilton and Rosberg finished third and fourth, respectively, behind Vettel, who led by 8.5 seconds. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff acknowledged Ferrari's superior performance and the need for analysis to regain dominance.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to use nitrogen gas for executions if lethal injection becomes unavailable, aiming for a humane method. The bill, which has never been used in U.S. executions, was signed as Oklahoma's lethal injections are under review by the Supreme Court.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in Swansea's 3-1 win over Hull, topping this week's EA Sports Performance Index with a score of 52.9. Other top performers include Charlie Austin (52.2) and Eden Hazard (51.7).

A Russian freezer trawler called the Dalny Vostok sank in the Sea of Okhotsk, killing at least 56 of its 132 crew members. A massive rescue operation involving over 1,300 people is underway, with 63 survivors rescued and 13 still missing. The ship sank in 15 minutes after pulling in an 80-ton fishing net, and the investigation is considering various causes.

Clinical trials show that olaparib, a drug originally for women, can benefit men with advanced prostate cancer. Up to 30% of such men have DNA defects that respond well to olaparib, extending their disease control. The drug, known as Lynparza, works by blocking cancer cell repair mechanisms, reducing side effects from traditional treatments.

Rhiannon Taylor, a 29-year-old travel photographer from Australia, has turned her passion into a business by reviewing and photographing luxurious accommodations worldwide. With over 12,000 Instagram followers, she documents the best beds, pools, and room service, generating income from hotel reviews and product placements.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was killed after getting caught in a fight between two adult hippos in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park, South Africa. The calf's mother watched in horror as the baby was thrown into the air and dragged through the water. A tour operator described how the mother tried to protect her calf but was unable to save it.

During Chelsea's 1-0 victory over QPR at Loftus Road, QPR fans threw objects onto the pitch, hitting Branislav Ivanovic. The Football Association will contact both clubs and seek observations, while QPR is reviewing CCTV footage and appealing for witnesses to identify the culprits, who may face bans.

LaTasha Gosling, 27, and her three children, ages 4, 7, and 8, were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. The suspect, known to the victims, was found dead hours later but not from homicide. A GoFundMe page has been set up to raise money for funeral services.

Emily Thornberry, a Labour politician, faced criticism for opposing the right to buy policy while renting out a housing association property she bought for nearly £1 million. Her husband owns a £3 million Victorian townhouse. Critics accused her of hypocrisy, while housing association leaders were also criticized for living in mansions while opposing the policy.

Police dropped an investigation into a violent assault on Mike Lane, 40, a huntsman, despite having evidence and a video of the attack by masked protesters. Wiltshire Police cited insufficient evidence and plan to reopen the case only if new evidence emerges.
Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes, 21, insists he will stay at Valencia, despite links to Manchester United and Chelsea, saying he is happy with his current club and has not been contacted by Chelsea.

An Australian teenager, Audrey Pekin, was raped twice on Christmas Eve in Bali by a man named Henry Alafu, who lured her to his home and then followed her in a taxi. Indonesian police failed to prevent Alafu from escaping back to Nigeria.

Ashley James, a former Made In Chelsea star, has joined PETA in an anti-fur campaign against Harvey Nichols, which recently reintroduced fur products. The campaign features a fake skinned fox and aims to educate consumers about the fur industry's cruelty. Harvey Nichols claims to source fur responsibly but faces criticism from animal rights activists.

Chile's President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law recognizing same-sex civil unions, which will take effect in six months, benefiting an estimated 2 million people and providing legal rights in areas such as property, health care, and inheritance.

Chelsea have led the Premier League for 230 days, on course to break Manchester United's record of 262 days from 1993/94. They currently lead by seven points with a game in hand and could surpass the record by 12 days if they stay top until the end of the season.

Cape Verde, a country of 500,000 people, is leveraging its rich musical heritage to boost its economy, lacking conventional natural resources. The government, including Prime Minister Jose Maria Neves, supports this initiative, viewing music and culture as key to development. The Kriol Jazz Festival, celebrating its seventh edition, has attracted international artists and boosted tourism, highlighting music's potential economic impact.

A hoax video of a surfer in front of Sydney's Opera House resurfaced on social media, trending again after heavy storms. The video, originally posted in 2012, was debunked by wave experts who said it's impossible for waves to reach the Opera House.
Reading lost 1-0 to Birmingham in a Championship match at the Madejski Stadium, despite dominating much of the game. Clayton Donaldson scored Birmingham's winning goal with a late header.

David Luiz, a key defender for Paris Saint-Germain, injured his hamstring during a match against Marseille and will miss at least four weeks, including both legs of the Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona.

The return of Game of Thrones has led to a surge in internet piracy, with over 100,000 illegal downloads per day and seven million episodes illegally downloaded between February and April. Brazil was the top country for downloads, followed by France, the US, Canada, and the UK. HBO plans to air the new season globally simultaneously and launched a new streaming service to curb piracy.

Leicester City and West Ham United will face off at King Power Stadium in a Premier League match. Matt Upson is out for Leicester, while Winston Reid returns for West Ham. West Ham is favored with odds of 2/1, while Leicester is at 7/5. West Ham has not lost to Leicester in their last seven league meetings, while Leicester has won only one of their last ten home matches.

Residents of Celoron, N.Y., are unhappy with a statue of Lucile Ball unveiled in 2009, calling it unflattering and "monstrous." The statue, based on Ball's intoxicated pitch for a health tonic, has attracted over 600 likes on a Facebook page calling for its removal. It would cost $8,000 to $10,000 to recast.

Sharon Smith, 43, from Halesowen, lost nearly half her body weight, dropping from over 20st to 9st 9lb, after standing for 11 hours on a flight in 2012 due to concerns about crushing the passenger next to her. She credits her weight loss to joining a slimming club and taking up running.

Nicola Bonn, 34, from London, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences as a first-time mother of 14-month-old Poppy, addressing the overwhelming opinions and judgments she faced. Her viral blog post, "Why We Need to Stop Justifying Ourselves," highlights the challenges and self-doubt new mothers often encounter.

Two 17-year-old boys from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, named Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, are believed to have traveled to Syria, prompting their families' distress and police involvement. Hassan is related to Hammaad Munshi, who was previously convicted for a plot to murder non-Muslims in 2006. The boys boarded a Thomas Cook flight to Turkey on March 31 and have not been in contact since.

Stephanie Scott, a school teacher from Leeton, was murdered just days before her wedding, leaving her fiancé Aaron Leeson-Woolley devastated. Her body was found in bushland on Easter Friday after she went missing on Easter Sunday. The couple had planned a wedding at Eat Your Greens venue, with a guest list of 120 people. Mr Scott described his daughter as bubbly and thoughtful, with many wedding preparations left unfinished.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is interested in signing Feyenoord players Tonny Vilhena and Jordy Clasie, with Vilhena ready to leave Feyenoord after one year. Koeman aims to strengthen his squad for potential European qualification.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library at Ickworth House in Suffolk, sparking controversy among heritage experts. Similar experiments will be conducted at nine other National Trust venues. The Trust aims to encourage visitors to engage more deeply with the atmosphere, but critics argue it is patronizing.

Former Prime Minister John Howard was photographed changing a flat tyre with his driver in Sydney. A passerby, Felicity Waterford, offered assistance and took a selfie with Howard, who was described as a "complete gentleman." This incident occurred weeks after another Liberal MP, Christopher Pyne, faced a similar challenge on national television.

Tony Pulis acknowledges Joey Barton's criticism of West Brom's performance after they lost a 2-0 lead against QPR in December. Pulis, who has improved West Brom's performance, recalls his own experience of losing a match despite a two-goal lead. The teams face each other again at the Hawthorns.

In the Democratic Republic of Congo, researchers have captured the first-ever photograph of the Bouvier's red colobus monkey, proving it is not extinct after being thought lost for over 50 years. This discovery was made in Ntokou-Pikounda National Park. Additionally, a new species of white-cheeked macaque, Macaca leucogenys, has been identified in southeast Tibet through camera traps.

Kim Kardashian, her husband Kanye West, and their daughter North visited Armenia, the country of her father's birth, for an eight-day trip. They were welcomed with enthusiasm in Yerevan, staying at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan and visiting local landmarks like the Yerevan Opera House and Geghard Monastery.

Patrick and Valerie Jubb, British expats in Jimena de la Frontera, Spain, face losing their four-bedroom bed and breakfast due to illegal alterations made by a previous owner, despite obtaining a certificate stating no infractions. The town hall seeks to demolish the property, trapping the couple who wish to return to the UK.

Apple reported record iPhone sales of over 61 million units in the first quarter, generating $58 billion in revenue and $13.6 billion in profit, up 40% from the previous year. iPad sales fell 29%, while Mac revenue rose 2%. CEO Tim Cook highlighted strong growth in China and positive response to the new Apple Watch.

Natali Castellanos-Tyler, 30, died in a February SUV crash in Virginia, which police ruled a tragic accident. Her 3-year-old daughter Elisa has been having nightmares about a white van, leading her father to suspect foul play, as similar incidents involving white trucks have been reported in the area.

Researchers at New York University found that the brain can better remember 'neutral' events when they are tied to an emotion, such as the September 11 terrorist attacks. Emotion affects brain regions involved in emotional processing and memory consolidation, strengthening mundane memories over time.

Jahnae Jackson, girlfriend of 18-year-old Jackson Byrnes, has raised over $80,000 to fund life-saving surgery for his stage four brain tumour. The surgery, to be performed by Dr. Charlie Teo, aims to save Jackson's life but will leave him paralysed. Jahnae, who put her studies on hold, has been caring for Jackson since he was diagnosed four weeks ago.

Nedum Onuoha, a 28-year-old QPR centre-back, is wanted by Hull City, among others, as QPR considers squad streamlining if they are relegated. Onuoha played in QPR's recent 4-1 win against West Bromwich Albion. Hull is also interested in West Brom striker Victor Anichebe, who is likely to be sold.

Researchers at Yale University have mapped regional variations in English sentence structure across the US and UK, revealing phrases like "Here's you a water bottle" in the South and "This glass needs washed" in Idaho, highlighting how different regions use unique grammatical patterns.

A Canadian man, Kalman Kallai, travelled from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia for work by dragging a green rocking chair in a trailer, capturing the journey in a video that showed him rocking and making gestures while seeing various Canadian landscapes.

Manager Tim Sherwood revealed his 'win bonus' of a Twix multi-pack during a press conference, referencing a letter from six-year-old Aston Villa fan Charlie Pye, who had applied for the job and requested sweets and chocolate as a bonus.
Kell Brook received a hero's welcome at the Premier League Darts in Sheffield. Dave Chisnall won two matches to move to second place in the table with 17 points.

Marco Verratti praises Zlatan Ibrahimovic's off-field contributions for Paris Saint-Germain, where Ibrahimovic has scored 17 Ligue 1 goals. The Swedish striker was suspended for the first leg of PSG's Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona but will play in the return match.

The Ministry of Defence accidentally published a secret RAF base manual on their website, revealing vital GPS coordinates and technical details of the Falklands Islands' main base, potentially aiding Argentina in an invasion. The document, which included information on the runway and facilities, was uploaded unencrypted and could have been accessed by Argentine intelligence.

Huddersfield Giants coach Paul Anderson aims to improve his team's offensive play to boost their Super League standing after a poor start, while their strong defensive record remains intact. The Giants, currently ninth, face Catalans Dragons at home, with a win potentially moving them to fourth.

Planners in Windsor approved two Costa cafes less than 500 yards apart, with another Costa Express located in between. The new Costa will open on the site of a former bank, while another replaced a cycle shop nearby. Residents are divided, with one concerned about the proliferation of coffee shops, while another sees it as a sign of the area's growth.

The British Veterinary Association has withdrawn its support for shooting free-running badgers in controversial pilot culls, instead advocating for trapping and shooting. The Environment Secretary promised to expand culls if the Conservatives win the election, despite criticism from wildlife groups.
