In Somerset, 341 badgers were culled, leading to expected TB reductions in cattle, while in Gloucestershire, only 274 were culled, falling short of the target.

Geoff Barrow, Portishead's founder, criticized streaming services for low royalties, citing £1,700 for 34 million plays. He supports streaming but wants better payments for musicians, especially for young artists. Jay-Z launched Tidal, promising better deals for artists, while streaming companies defend their practices.

Before the premiere of Game of Thrones' fifth season, fans leaked the first four episodes online, with over 550,000 downloads by early Sunday morning. HBO stated they are investigating the breach from a group approved to receive the episodes.

Daniel Buccheri, a 25-year-old singer, composed an emotional song for his brother Adrian's wedding, which went viral with over 100,000 views. The speech, performed at Poet's Lane in Sherbrooke, Melbourne, included tributes to Adrian and his new wife Sarah, touching on their relationship and Daniel's childhood.

Zara Phillips, 33, regained her fitness after giving birth to Mia by exercising daily before her daughter woke up. She follows a strict diet and trains multiple times a day to prepare for the 2016 Olympics, where she hopes to compete in eventing.

Raheem Sterling's interview, where he said he was not ready to sign a new contract, upset Liverpool fans and could affect his future at the club. Sterling trains ahead of a match against Arsenal, with fans increasingly open to letting him go if he wants to leave.

In the 1996-97 season, Barcelona's squad included future managers like Jose Mourinho, Pep Guardiola, Laurent Blanc, and Julen Lopetegui, who are now coaching in the Champions League. This team, which won the Spanish Super Cup, is producing a significant number of current and former football managers.

Former Manchester United star Eric Cantona named Paris Saint-Germain's Javier Pastore the best player in the world, praising his creativity over Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. Pastore scored three goals and provided five assists this season.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murder after dismembering his tenant Michael Spalding and hiding the body parts in suitcases dumped in a canal. Simon's girlfriend, Michelle Bird, 35, was cleared of murder but admitted to assisting an offender. The crime occurred in Smethwick, Birmingham, in April 2022.

Health experts warn that social isolation can be as harmful as smoking 15 cigarettes a day. Two UK county councils, Essex and Gloucestershire, have created 'loneliness maps' to identify areas with high risk of social isolation among pensioners and others. The maps, which consider factors like age, living alone, mental illness, and low income, help councils target assistance to vulnerable areas. The Campaign to End Loneliness calls on other councils to adopt this approach.

Judy Eddingfield, 65, celebrated 50 years of working as a waitress at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, where she has been the only job she's ever had. She started in 1965 at age 15 and has seen the restaurant through its 80 years, meeting her husband there and serving celebrities like 'Leave It to Beaver' stars Jerry Mathers and Tony Dow.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not return to the national team immediately, even if he performs well for Surrey. Gatting suggests Pietersen needs to prove himself alongside players like Gary Ballance, Ian Bell, and Joe Root who have been performing well. England's Alastair Cook, who struggled in the recent Test series, faces more scrutiny if he fails to score runs against West Indies.

A 17-year-old Californian student, Caleb Benn, developed an app called 'Uploader for Instagram' that allows users to upload photos to Instagram from their computer, earning him $1,000 a day. Instagram has accused him of violating its terms of service, and an engineer has given him until Monday to fix the app, which Benn says would make it useless.

In South Korea, "hoesik" involves frequent group drinking events at work, where alcohol is consumed at multiple venues. This practice is seen as a way to get to know colleagues and is deeply ingrained in Korean culture, affecting traffic patterns in Seoul. Foreign business travelers must learn the drinking etiquette to avoid offending colleagues or superiors.

The Duke of Kent, 79, was discharged from Aberdeen Royal Infirmary after being treated for a dislocated hip suffered at Balmoral estate. He left the hospital with a walking stick. This comes two years after he had a mild stroke.

Local business leaders in Surfers Paradise, Queensland, are calling for the end of the 50-year tradition of Meter Maids, young women in bikinis who enforce parking meters, due to outdated practices and anti-touting laws. The Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce president argues they no longer provide a public service and should move on, while Meter Maids' general manager defends their cultural significance.

Greece denied it would fail to pay a £330 million loan to the IMF, stating it would make the payment on time. Deputy finance minister Dimitris Mardas said Greece is ready to pay on April 9. Sources suggested the government might prioritize paying wages and pensions over international loans.

A Turkish court blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after the social media platforms refused to remove pictures of a prosecutor killed during an armed siege. The court imposed the blocks because the images deeply upset the victim's family. Mehmet Selim Kiraz, a 46-year-old prosecutor, died in a six-hour stand-off with the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party-Front, a terrorist group.

Seven-year-old Colin Gilpatric wrote to George Lucas about Jedi Knights not being allowed to marry, fearing it might lead to becoming a Sith like Anakin Skywalker. Lucas responded, affirming that compassion and loyalty are values important in marriage and sent Colin Star Wars merchandise.

Wisconsin beat Kentucky 71-64 in the NCAA Tournament semi-finals, advancing to the final against Duke. Kentucky, with an undefeated season of 38-1, lost its chance to become the first undefeated team in nearly 40 years. Duke defeated Michigan State 81-61, securing their place in the final.

Vince Neil of Mötley Crüe performed a poor rendition of the American national anthem at a Las Vegas football game, joining a list of famous performers who have botched the anthem, including Whitney Houston, Roseanne Barr, Jimi Hendrix, and Michael Bolton.

In Sydney, Barry Lyttle, from Belfast, Ireland, punched his brother Patrick, causing him to fall unconscious and nearly lose his life. Security footage shown in court revealed the incident outside Hugo's Lounge. Barry, who pleaded guilty to grievous bodily harm, faces up to two years in jail.

The parents of conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, who died 19 days after birth, found their gravesite at Pinegrove Memorial Park in Sydney's west completely cleared of memorabilia, leaving them devastated. The family had built a shrine with flowers, toys, and statues, which was removed without notice, with only about 25 percent of the items recovered.

Lord Neuberger, President of the Supreme Court, suggested Muslim women should be allowed to wear full-face veils in court to show respect for different customs. He called for judges to be sensitive to the 'subconscious bias' when dealing with poorer members of society. This comes after a 2003 case where a Muslim woman was sentenced for refusing to remove her veil during testimony.

Andre Cole, 52, was executed by lethal injection in Missouri on Tuesday for killing a friend in 1998 after a dispute over child support payments. The execution was the third in Missouri this year. Cole, who was black, was convicted by an all-white jury.

Prince Harry will fly to Australia without seeing his new niece or nephew, who is expected to be born soon. Due to the baby's late arrival, Harry will miss the birth and return in mid-May to meet the new royal baby.

Florida man Justin Jackson, 38, has been accused of posing as celebrities including Oprah Winfrey, Reggie Love, and Madonna's manager to trick people into giving him free items and jobs, totaling $2.4 million in value. Jackson is being sued by Oprah's TV network and former Obama aide Reggie Love.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini has set a €50 million price tag on Paulo Dybala, attracting interest from Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus, and Paris Saint-Germain. Zamparini compares Dybala to Lionel Messi and is determined to maximize profits from his sale.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians are protesting against President Dilma Rousseff, calling for her impeachment due to an economic downturn and a bribery scandal at state-run oil company Petrobras. Rousseff's supporters counter-protest, defending her and her right to govern. Her approval rating has dropped sharply, and the economy is struggling with high inflation and currency devaluation.

Former Manchester United player Eric Cantona refuted claims that he starred in a soft porn film, insisting You and the Night is an artistic piece. At the Laureus Sports Awards in Shanghai, Cantona defended the film, saying it is not porn but "beautiful" and "a work of art."

Psychologists found that listening to certain music can enhance food flavors. For instance, The Beatles' music is served with fish and chips at Ultraviolent restaurant in Shanghai. Professor Charles Spence from Oxford University explained that while music cannot create flavors, it can draw attention to certain notes in food and wine, enhancing the dining experience.

Raheem Sterling, 20, has postponed contract talks with Liverpool until the summer, despite a £100,000-a-week offer, to focus on the season. PFA chief Gordon Taylor supports Sterling, saying he is entitled to consider his options.

La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, 38, discovered her birth mother, Francine Simmons, worked at the same call-center as her in Youngstown, Ohio, after receiving birth records. They live just six minutes apart and have three younger sisters.

Oscar 'Papoo' Hernandez Jr, a gun trafficker, pleaded guilty to weapons charges related to sending weapons to Aaron Hernandez, who was sentenced to life in prison for Odin Lloyd's murder. Hernandez said he was awed by Hernandez and grateful for the $15,000 payment, though he claims he did not foresee the murder. He faces up to 30 months in prison.

Joel Parker, 33, was arrested for throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head after threatening and disrupting the ride in St Johns County, Florida, on Wednesday. He posted $250 bond and was issued a trespass warning, barred from using the bus again.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has discussed pre-season plans with striker Saido Berahino, indicating Berahino will stay beyond the summer transfer window. Berahino, 21, has expressed a desire to play in the Champions League and was linked to Liverpool, but Pulis believes he is happy at the club.

Giovanni Lo Porto, an Italian aid worker, was abducted and later killed in a U.S. drone strike in Pakistan in 2012 while working on reconstruction efforts following flooding. The strike also killed another hostage and an al Qaeda leader. Lo Porto, a Peace and Conflict Studies graduate, was dedicated to humanitarian work and had been working with the German aid organization Welthungerlife.

A photographer in Florida captured images of hundreds of sharks, believed to be Blacktips or Spinners, swarming just 100 feet from a beach on Thursday. The sharks were migrating to breed in shallower waters, and the photos were shared over 2,000 times.

An 11-year-old retired K-9 officer named Zeus, a German Shepherd who served the Ridgefield Police Department for eight years, was honored with a grand procession before being put down due to severe health issues. The tribute, attended by fellow officers and residents, included a parade through the town and ended at the veterinary clinic where Zeus was euthanized.

Reports of child sex abuse cases have risen by over 60% since Operation Yewtree, with nearly 9,000 reports filed in 2014, but the number of arrests fell by nine percent, prompting criticism of the government's response.

Iceland has become a popular filming location, with 17 production services companies now operating there. Notable locations include Thingvellir National Park for Game of Thrones, Svartalfheim for Thor: The Dark World, and the Svinafellsjokull glacier for Interstellar. The Dettifoss waterfall was used in Prometheus.

A 100-year-old bathing box in Melbourne sold for $276,000, breaking records for such historic structures. In Sydney, a 1917 fire station turned mechanic’s garage sold for $1.2 million to be converted into a home. Also in Victoria, the 1850s Old Kilmore Gaol, now a renovated home, is on the market for $2 million.

Samantha Rawcliffe, 40, from Morecambe, lost control of her body and crashed her car in May after being diagnosed with functional neurological disorder, a rare condition causing unexplained neurological symptoms. She now struggles to walk, relies on a mobility scooter, and takes 32 daily medications.

Sculptor Dave Poulin, who created a controversial statue of Lucille Ball in Celoron, New York, admitted it was "unsettling" and offered to replace it for free. The statue, based on Ball's intoxicated pitch for a health tonic, has been nicknamed "Scary Lucy" and sparked a social media campaign for its removal.

David Alaba, Bayern Munich's left-back, will miss around seven weeks due to a torn knee ligament, ruling him out for the season's closing stages. He was injured while playing for Austria against Bosnia. Alaba expressed disappointment but aims to return for the season finale.

Beatrice Nokes, 21, and 37-year-old Daniel Williams, a suspended detective constable, appeared in court facing charges related to running a prostitution ring in London. Nokes, the daughter of respected solicitors, is accused of inciting prostitutes, while Williams faces additional charges including voyeurism and concealing profits.

A firm called Sequester, linked to Alchemy Direct Media, is offering NHS patient data, including details of eating disorder sufferers for 12p a head, prompting probes by the Information Commissioner’s Office, the Direct Marketing Commission, and the General Pharmaceutical Council into Pharmacy2U. The data includes personal and financial information, raising concerns about privacy and potential misuse.

Jordan Spieth won the Masters golf tournament at Augusta, becoming the second-youngest champion and the fifth to lead from start to finish. He expressed his wish for his autistic sister Ellie to try on the green jacket, highlighting her importance in his life and providing him with perspective.

Dick Advocaat, Sunderland's manager, will not downplay the significance of the Wear-Tyne Derby after his 1998 mistake against Celtic. Sunderland, one point above relegation, aims for three points against Newcastle. Advocaat considers fan support crucial, saying, "This must be a weapon."

A dispute erupted in Bondi when Belinda Bartholomew, girlfriend of Roosters player Aidan Guerra, claimed she was racially abused by a butcher who refused to serve her. The butcher denies the claims, saying he was just frustrated with his eftpos machine.

Cadbury has reduced the size of its Freddo Frogs by 20% from 15g to 12g, keeping the price the same, due to increased manufacturing costs. This follows a previous reduction in the size of their family blocks of Dairy Milk by 20g to 200g. Cadbury's profit rose 46% in 2013, but customers have expressed anger on social media about the size cuts.

Hillary Clinton's campaign held a meeting in Brooklyn to outline their values and strategy for the 2016 presidential race, emphasizing humility, discipline, and avoiding past mistakes that led to her 2008 defeat. The campaign will focus on electing Clinton to give Americans a path to prosperity and will launch with a social media announcement on Sunday.

Kyli Wilfson, 29, battled chronic pancreatitis for a year and a half, unable to eat despite feeling perpetually hungry. Diagnosed at 26, she lost 30 pounds and postponed her wedding due to frequent hospitalizations. The rare condition, affecting less than 0.01% of people, left her dependent on a feeding tube.

The leaders' debate was referenced in various memes, including Ed Miliband superimposed over Plan B calling to 'come at me bruv', and David Cameron and Nick Clegg shown on the Gogglebox sofa. Memes also featured Nicola Sturgeon with a sceptical face and the five leaders as the Mighty Morphin Power Rangers.

Amir Khan is set to potentially face Manny Pacquiao in a fight in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, after initially being close to challenging Floyd Mayweather. Khan, who recently received a presidential award in Pakistan, is eager for the fight and sees it as a dream to compete in the Middle East. Promoter Bob Arum views Khan as a strong contender for the fight, praising his speed and recent performances.

A tiny two-bedroom home in Islington, London, measuring only 5ft wide in some areas, sold for £750,000. Despite its narrow dimensions, the property, which includes a garden and two bedrooms, attracted buyers at almost double its 2001 price of £375,000.

Nicola Sturgeon, SNP leader, unveiled a manifesto with policies aimed at forming a power-sharing deal with Labour, including slashing English university tuition fees and rolling back NHS competition. The SNP seeks to build a 'progressive alliance' across the UK, with the potential to hold the balance of power at Westminster, where they are on track for a landslide victory in Scotland.

Celtic U17 team beat Rangers 2-0 to win the Glasgow Cup at Hampden Park, with goals from Josh Kerr and Mark Hill. Rangers keeper Robby McCrorie made two costly mistakes, allowing Kerr to score and doubling Celtic's lead.

Tony Pulis led West Bromwich Albion to a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace, maintaining his distinctive pre-game attire despite his former club's dominance. Pulis insists on wearing a cap, track suit, and white trainers for every match, stating he will never change.

Jameela Jamil spent £3,000 to replace her amalgam fillings with white fillings after experiencing health issues for seven years, which were linked to high mercury levels from the fillings. Dental experts say the mercury exposure from fillings is minimal and safe.

Suge Knight, co-creator of Death Row Records, laughed in court as he revealed hopes that Floyd Mayweather will bail him out after Mayweather's upcoming fight. Knight, facing murder and attempted murder charges, was denied a bail reduction and must await trial starting July 7. His attorney believes Mayweather, a champion boxer worth $420 million, will help.

TV chef Gizzi Erskine, 35, featured in a cat magazine with her British shorthair Kimchi, who loves human food like poppadoms and taramasalata. Gizzi insists Kimchi's taste is natural, not influenced by her foodie household, and she has put Kimchi on a diet due to its indulgence.

Martin Springall, a father from Tokyo, took a photo of his daughter in Japan in 2014, which went viral due to a mysterious pair of black boots appearing behind her. Springall, who insists no one else was present and the photo was not altered, remains unsure about the boots' origin.

Home Secretary Theresa May announced plans to ban unemployed EU migrants from claiming benefits for four years and to deport those without jobs within six months, with working migrants required to pay £22,600 in taxes over four years before accessing benefits. These changes aim to reduce EU migration, following a rise to 298,000 in the year ending September 2014.

Cody Neatis, an eight-year-old boy with Down's syndrome, epilepsy, and autism, slept on the floor for seven nights in Royal Preston Hospital due to a lack of a suitable bed. His mother, Lynne Neatis, has slept with him to watch for potential injuries or oxygen tube pulls. The hospital has faced criticism for not having a high-sided cot, despite previous promises to provide one.

Ian Poulter forgot his golf clubs after getting excited to start at Augusta. Henrik Stenson, recovering from flu, questions his ability to perform. Tiger Woods will play with his children, Charlie and Sam, in the traditional par-three tournament. Gene Sarazen's albatross on the 15th hole in 1935 is remembered as the most famous shot in Masters history.
Juventus have ruled out signing Manchester United's Radamel Falcao due to his high wages, while expressing interest in Paulo Dybala and Edinson Cavani for their forward line.
David Cameron pledges to sell £4 billion of Lloyds Bank shares if re-elected, offering a discount and a loyalty bonus, aiming to pay down national debt and revive 1980s-style privatisations.

A study found that living near congested roads with high air pollution increases the risk of silent strokes, which can lead to brain shrinkage and dementia. Researchers examined over 900 people and linked PM2.5 exposure to a 46% higher risk of silent strokes.

Jessica Ainscough, 30, died in late February from epithelioid sarcoma after undergoing radiation treatment in her final weeks, choosing unconventional Gerson Therapy over chemotherapy. Her partner, Tallon Pamenter, revealed she integrated natural healing with conventional medicine, showing courage and grace throughout her seven-year battle.

A multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway near Fernvale involved ten people, including four children, on Wednesday afternoon. Three vehicles collided, resulting in six people being airlifted to Princess Alexandra Hospital with serious injuries, while six others were taken to Ipswich Hospital with minor injuries. Emergency crews freed one trapped person using hydraulic cutting gear. The highway was closed for several hours with diversions in place.

Jason McDonald, a 34-year-old gator farm manager from Colorado, walked a slackline over a pool containing over 50 alligators, some up to ten feet long, as a new way to interact with the creatures. McDonald, who has been involved with alligators for over ten years, plans to walk over the farm's largest gators, Elvis and Morris, and even over albino gators.

Abdul Hadi Arwani, a Syrian imam and activist, was shot dead in North West London. Sources suggest he may have met his killer, a black man with an African accent, during a building quote visit days before his murder. The counter-terrorism unit is investigating whether the man was a hired killer who postponed the hit because Arwani was not alone at the time.

In Hong Kong, there is a surge in demand for Jenny's butter cookies, with people lining up for hours to buy them at $9 a tin. The popularity has led to knockoff bakeries and resellers marking up the cookies by 70%. Similar food crazes, like cronuts and ramen burgers, have also swept other parts of the world.

Kira Hollis, a 27-year-old from Tamworth, Staffordshire, overcame anorexia and depression by becoming a bodybuilder. Diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, she weighed just 6st but now stands at 9.5st and works as a personal trainer. Her six-year-old daughter Olivia and medication also contributed to her recovery.

Jockey Lewis Ferguson, 18, survived a spectacular fall from Merrion Square during a race at Wincanton, suffering only a cut on his nose. He returned to work at the stables the next day and remains undeterred from his racing career, aiming to compete at Cheltenham and Aintree.

Hillary Clinton launched her presidential campaign with a video and road trip aimed at rebranding herself and reframing her image as more empathetic and relatable. Critics, including Washington Post columnist Ruth Marcus and comedian Jon Stewart, were harsh, but the campaign may be successfully projecting a more confident and forward-looking image.
More than 1,700 Chinese high school students in Yichuan, Shaanxi province, took an exam in their school playground due to lack of indoor space, organizing the unusual outdoor test themselves.

Sportsmail and Gillette are offering a competition where one lucky reader can win a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Joe Hart, Manchester City and England goalkeeper, along with a Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor and shaving gel. The competition ends on April 19.

Kecil, a one-year-old baby orangutan, found a loving surrogate mother at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo after being rejected by his natural and another surrogate mother. Maggie, 53, has been raising Kecil for 10 months and the two have formed an inseparable bond. Kecil will make his first public appearance this weekend.

Noelle Baynham, 61, died after an accidental overdose and was partially eaten by her dogs over several days. Her friend Grant Donovan discovered her body when he entered her Winchester home, finding it covered in dog faeces. Pathologists could not determine the exact cause of death due to the dogs' consumption of her organs.

French handball star Nikola Karabatic, along with 15 others, will stand trial for fraud over an alleged match-fixing case involving a 2012 Montpellier match. Karabatic, a multiple gold medalist, denies the charges and faces up to five years in prison and a fine. His trial is expected to take place within months.

A gang of six men, including Ahmed Hassan-Sule, have been jailed for a total of 31 years for sexual offences against teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire. The offences, which included rape and inciting sexual activity with a child, occurred from 2009 to 2014. The victims, aged 13 to 16, were lured to parties organized on social media by the gang.

Aaron Hernandez, 25, faces three more trials after being convicted of murder, including another murder trial for allegedly killing two men and wounding another near a Boston nightclub in July 2012. His assets, including a $3.3 million signing bonus, are frozen pending the outcome of the double-murder trial.

Emirates Airline is set to rebrand the FA Cup for £30 million over three years, expanding its portfolio of sporting sponsorships. The deal includes existing agreements with Arsenal worth £150 million, AC Milan worth £80 million, and Hamburg worth £17 million.

18-time Olympic champion Michael Phelps aims to compete in his fifth Olympics next year in Rio, though he won't swim in the upcoming world championships as punishment for his second DUI arrest. Phelps, 29, is back in Arizona after completing alcohol rehabilitation and is focused on making amends.

Gareth Bale is a major doubt for Real Madrid's Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid due to a calf injury. He limped off after just a few minutes in a 3-1 win over Malaga. Real Madrid is also without Luka Modric, who suffered a knee ligament strain.

A study by scientists at Texas Tech University found that older people are more prone to emotional decision-making about retirement investments, leading to significant financial losses during the 2007-2008 financial crisis. The research, published in the Journal of Consumer Affairs, analyzed 1,204 retirees and warned that cognitive decline with age can impair emotional regulation in financial decisions. In related news, British pension reforms allow those turning 55 to access their pensions flexibly from April 5.

Stuart Pearce believes Manchester City should give Manuel Pellegrini more time to improve the team, despite their recent poor performance, including a loss to Manchester United. Pearce, who has experience with the club, attributes their struggles partly to Yaya Toure's declining form.

Manchester United trained in preparation for their upcoming Premier League match against Manchester City, with key players like Wayne Rooney and Robin van Persie returning to action. United leads the league for the first time since Sir Alex Ferguson's era, aiming to move four points ahead of City. City has won the last three visits to Old Trafford, making this match crucial for both teams.
Fiorentina lost 1-0 to Verona, conceding in the 90th minute, leaving them nine points behind third-place AS Roma in Serie A. Alessandro Diamanti missed a penalty, and Mounir Obbadi scored the winner.

Miley Cyrus displayed unshaven armpits at the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, sparking social media debate. Some criticized her appearance, while others defended her right to have body hair.

Barcelona's Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez scored 102 goals between them this season, with Barcelona defeating Getafe 6-0, taking them five points clear in La Liga. Messi leads with 49 goals, Neymar has 32, and Suarez has 21.

A cyclist knocked down 44-year-old Andrea McVeigh on a London pavement, leaving her scarred for life with facial and hand injuries. The cyclist fled, chased by McVeigh's husband. Police have released CCTV footage and are appealing for witnesses.

Paul Gregory, 51, of Bedford, was fined £795 and ordered to do 150 hours of unpaid work after admitting to dishonestly obtaining a blue badge by misrepresenting his physical abilities. Council officials discovered his fraud through a newspaper article detailing his 191-mile hike.

Apple has been awarded a patent for a facial recognition system that could automatically unlock iPhones by scanning a user's face with the front camera when the phone is moved into a specific position, potentially making the process more convenient than current methods.

Elizabeth Sedway, 51, was ejected from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California because she lacked a doctor's note, despite having multiple myeloma. Her family was also removed, and the incident was captured in a video posted on her Facebook page.

A 1973 E-Type Jaguar worth over $120,000 was completely written off in a head-on collision with a Toyota Kluger on Warringah Road in Frenchs Forest, northern Sydney, on Easter Sunday night. All three adults involved were taken to hospital as a precaution, though nobody was hurt.

Google has established a four-man team since 2012 to develop advanced battery technologies for various devices, including smartphones, electric cars, and wearable tech, aiming to improve battery life and functionality. The team, led by former Apple battery expert Dr. Ramesh Bhardwaj, has been working on projects like solid-state batteries and those functioning at subfreezing temperatures, crucial for Google's Project Loon.

The 223ft Explorer, a superyacht designed by Tony Castro, features a helipad, infinity pool, and space for 12 guests, along with storage for cars, jetskis, and a submarine, at a cost of approximately 40 million euros.

Ed Miliband pressed on with plans to cap rents despite warnings from experts that the measure would reduce housing investment and potentially worsen tenant conditions. His proposal, which includes three-year tenancies and rent caps tied to inflation, faced criticism from business leaders and even some Labour figures.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town supporter who hoped Arsenal would win was removed as a mascot for Reading in their FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal. The Football Association moved him to an England mascot spot instead, after 85% of Reading fans polled supported his removal.

Astronomers have proposed a giant supervoid 1.8 billion light-years across as an explanation for the 'Cold Spot' in the cosmic microwave background radiation, a region 20% less dense than other areas. The research, published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, suggests this supervoid, the largest structure ever found, could be responsible for the Cold Spot's lower temperature.

The chair where Abraham Lincoln was shot in 1865 will be displayed open to the public at The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, on April 15 to mark the 150th anniversary of his assassination. Historians at the museum say a dark stain on the chair is actually oil from other visitors, not blood.

Jake Boys, a 19-year-old vlogger from East Sussex, surprised his girlfriend Emily-Victoria Canham with One Direction concert tickets but booked flights to Dublin instead of Cardiff. Canham, a model from Northamptonshire, was dismayed and tweeted about the mistake. Boys plans to buy train tickets to Cardiff for the June concert.

Romanian company MB Telecom has developed the Roboscan 2M Aeria, a mobile X-ray scanner costing €3 million, to inspect planes for contraband and weapons. The device, which can scan an entire plane in about 20 minutes, is currently used to check trucks at borders in Eastern Europe, helping seize 76,000 packs of illegal cigarettes.

Stephen Munden, a 54-year-old convicted paedophile with an obsession for young girls, went missing from a psychiatric unit in Hampshire, prompting a manhunt. Munden, described as having a "fanatical obsession" with small girls, was last seen leaving a hospital near Hook. He was previously detained under the Mental Health Act after sexually touching a three-year-old girl on a bus.

Middlesbrough are leading the Championship with just four weeks left, having won their last four matches and holding a one-point lead over second-place Bournemouth. Watford, with Odion Ighalo aiming for promotion, face Norwich, while Bournemouth play Birmingham. Middlesbrough's lunchtime kick-off gives them an advantage.

The #grannyhair trend, featuring silver hair, is popular on social media, with many models and Instagrammers posting images of their grey locks. This trend, inspired by fashion shows and embraced by celebrities, represents a defiant feminist statement and a break from traditional views on women's grey hair.

Randy and Jodi Speidel, from Bellefontaine, Ohio, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning in late April, less than two months after creating online fundraisers in February to seek financial help due to their chronic conditions and dire living conditions.

Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg vowed to remain as party leader despite potential electoral losses, emphasizing the risk of Labour and Conservative parties vacating the center ground. He expressed optimism about the party's prospects and credited himself for forming the coalition government, while Business Secretary Vince Cable hoped to become Chancellor if the Lib Dems formed another coalition with the Conservatives.

Terry Cooper, 79, was saved from a large badger with six-inch teeth by his Jack Russell dog Sam in his Somerset garden. The badger, the size of a pig, burst through a hedge with cubs, but Sam dragged Cooper indoors. The National Farmers' Union advises protecting property with badger-proof fencing and securing bins.
Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose 3-0 to Porto U21s at Motspur Park, while Real Madrid progressed to the Champions League semi-finals with a 1-0 win over Atletico Madrid.

Property developer Andreas Christopheros, 29, was severely injured in a corrosive liquid attack outside his home in Truro, Cornwall, leaving him with life-changing injuries. David Phillips, 48, has been charged with grievous bodily harm with intent, while his wife Nicole, 45, faces charges of perverting the course of justice. The attack occurred in December and left Mr. Christopheros fighting for his life, with a loss of vision and facial scars.

In the Spanish town of Lastres, signs depicting a squatting figure defecating within a red circle with a diagonal line have been posted to warn pilgrims and visitors not to defecate along the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route. The signs, which have become an attraction, are in response to complaints from residents about pilgrims defecating outside their homes, despite the lack of public facilities along the route.

A massive fire consumed a building in Flint, Michigan, where a strip club named The Body Shop used to be located. The blaze started around 1pm and affected only the building and nearby power lines. Local resident Terry Rauh reported a previous fire at the site. An investigation into the cause of the fire is ongoing.

On the 10th anniversary of 9/11, Shoshana Hebshi, a woman of Arab and Jewish descent, was strip-searched and held for hours at Detroit Metropolitan Airport after being ethnically profiled. She has now settled a lawsuit with the federal government for $40,000, with Frontier Airlines and other entities also involved.

A plane made a crash landing and skidded off the runway at Hiroshima Airport, injuring 20 people. Asiana Airlines flight OZ162, en route from Seoul to Hiroshima, missed the landing point and spun 180 degrees after impact. The airport was closed, and emergency services were on the scene. Asiana Airlines, based in South Korea, operates two major airlines. Two years ago, an Asiana Airlines flight crashed in San Francisco, resulting in three deaths and 200 injuries.

Mark-Francis Vandelli, a 26-year-old reality TV star from Made In Chelsea, has a collection of 16 expensive watches, including a Cartier white gold Moonphase worth £32,000, a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42, and a Cartier Tortue Collection Privée. He buys a new watch each year, starting from his teens.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy, 89, is auctioning over 200 antiques, including a 3D diorama of the Battle of Agincourt and a medieval longbow, to downsize his home. The collection, valued at £100,000, includes furniture, paintings, and historical items from his career and interests. The auction will take place this Saturday at Dominic Winter auctioneers in Gloucestershire.

Brazilian commuter Nelson Felippe posted a photo on Facebook of two women hugging on a train platform in Rio de Janeiro, expressing his disapproval and concern about public behavior, which went viral. The post cleverly criticized public safety rather than homophobia, as the man in the photo was actually breaking safety regulations by standing on the yellow line.

A young English cricket fan named Jonathan Stevenson, now a director at LiveWire Sport, shared a letter he received from Richie Benaud in 1996, in tribute to the Australian cricket legend's death. The letter, dated September 27, 1996, included detailed advice on spin bowling for left-handers and was accompanied by a full sheet of notes. Benaud, a former Test player and commentator, advised Stevenson on various deliveries and encouraged him to enjoy his cricket.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg envisions a future where virtual reality will replace traditional travel, allowing users to experience global destinations through 3D environments and VR headsets like Oculus Rift. Facebook plans to integrate VR into its newsfeed and expects more immersive experiences in the future.

Guo Kai arranged for professional wedding photographs to be taken for his girlfriend Dong Hui, who is bedridden in hospital due to bone cancer. The couple, who met a year ago, planned to get married this month but had to postpone it. Despite her condition, Dong Hui wore a wedding dress and posed with Guo Kai, who has been by her side constantly.

A 34-year-old man, Blaine Boudreaux, got behind the wheel while intoxicated in Houston, causing three separate crashes within three hours that resulted in the deaths of a 6-year-old boy and a homeless man, and injuries to others. Boudreaux, with a history of DUIs, has been charged with intoxication manslaughter and other offenses.

Microsoft has launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions at its Redmond campus, partnering with Specialisterne. The initiative was announced by Mary Ellen Smith, who has a son with autism. This move follows Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella's previous controversial comments about women not needing to ask for raises.

Two deputies involved in the fatal arrest of Eric Harris in Tulsa, Oklahoma, have been reassigned due to safety threats after Harris' death. Reserve Deputy Robert Bates, who shot Harris, is charged with second-degree manslaughter. The sheriff's office has suspended the drug unit's operations pending a review of the shooting and is considering how to proceed with reviewing the deputies' actions.

Katie Prager, 24, and her husband Dalton, 24, are racing against time as Katie awaits a lung transplant for her cystic fibrosis and related infection, but Kentucky Medicaid will not cover the out-of-state treatment at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Dalton is pleading for help to save Katie, who was diagnosed with the infection in 2009 and given a year to live without a transplant.

Using data from the Sleep Cycle app, researchers found that the world wakes up earliest on Mondays in South Africa, while Americans are in the worst mood on Tuesdays, waking at 7am. The best sleep quality worldwide occurs on Wednesdays, with China having the highest quality sleep that night. Americans sleep the latest on Fridays, rising at 8:24am, and report the best mood upon waking.

Mexican artist Frida Kahlo's 25 unpublished love letters to her lover Jose Bartoli, written between 1946 and 1949, are expected to sell for up to $120,000 at auction in New York on April 15. The passionate correspondence, saved by Jose until his death in 1995, includes details about Kahlo's relationship with Diego Rivera and her artistic inspirations.

Len McCluskey, leader of the Unite union, is campaigning for Labour in South Wales with warm, popular appearances, but his union's influence on the Labour Party is described as potent and potentially sinister, with ties to Labour candidates and a desire to implement 1970s-style socialist policies. Unite, with 1.42 million claimed members, seeks to use its financial and organizational power to push Labour towards more radical left-wing policies, including expanding the public sector and increasing state spending.

Zookeeper Elad Hershkowitz at the Zoological Center in Tel Aviv captured unique perspectives of animals drinking from water troughs using a GoPro camera for 30 hours, resulting in a four-minute video showcasing various drinking styles, from a rhino almost kissing the water surface to a lemur delicately licking it.

A poll found that only 25% of voters think David Cameron is most eager to win the upcoming election, compared to 43% who believe Ed Miliband is more motivated. This comes as Cameron tries to revitalize his campaign, while Miliband is seen as more enthusiastic by voters.

Zaur Dadaev, one of five Chechen men accused of murdering Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov, retracted his confession in court, claiming he was beaten and pressured into confessing. Human rights activist Andrei Babushkin reported seeing signs of torture on Dadaev. Nemstov, an outspoken critic of Russian President Vladimir Putin, was shot four times on a bridge near the Kremlin in February.

A baby named Sonit Awal was rescued after being trapped for 22 hours under rubble in Nepal following a 7.8-magnitude earthquake on April 25, 2015. The earthquake killed over 5,000 people and injured thousands more, with Sonit's father Shyam Awal searching in vain before hearing his son's cries. Soldiers rescued Sonit at 10 a.m. on Sunday, and he was found uninjured at Bhaktapur Hospital.

A Church of Scientology-backed organization, Narcocon, is trying to change the land designation of Trout Run, a 40-acre plot near Camp David, to build a drug rehab center using controversial methods like saunas and vitamin therapy. Opponents argue the center could be dangerous and that the site has historic significance, while Narcocon denies any religious conversion and claims its program is non-medical and non-profit.

In Kabul, five men who spoke English for NATO are now jobless and blacklisted, living in market stalls and fearing for their safety after being fired from their jobs. The city's population has grown significantly, with many fleeing violence in the provinces, while once bustling areas are now deserted due to security warnings and the end of foreign presence.

Two US Navy SEALs died and one was critically injured while swimming in a pool at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story in Virginia on Friday. The incident occurred during regular training, not dive training, and both victims were assigned to Naval Special Warfare Group Two. An investigation is ongoing.

NBC, which holds the live rights to show Premier League matches in the USA, has significantly increased US viewership of the league, with over 32 million unique viewers last season, more than in Britain. To enhance coverage, NBC has brought their entire production team to England for the first time, including star anchor Rebecca Lowe, for recent matches. Lowe, a lifelong Crystal Palace fan, aims to improve American understanding of the league's drama and quality.

Boris Johnson verbally attacked Ed Miliband on live TV, claiming Miliband would do "more damage to the country than he did to his brother." The exchange turned into a heated argument on the BBC's Andrew Marr Show, with Miliband laughing off the attack. Johnson also accused Labour of needing SNP support to form a government, calling it "deeply alarming."

Dustin Irons, a prisoner in Oregon, was sentenced to an extra 30 days in jail for flashing a judge during a court hearing via video-link, despite being in handcuffs. The incident occurred while Irons, already serving time for hotel vandalism and assault, became disgruntled during his court appearance.

Jenson Button believes McLaren has made significant progress in Formula One, having raced competitively with midfield teams after struggling in Australia. Button hopes further improvements will allow McLaren to challenge Force Indias, Saubers, and Lotuses in the Chinese Grand Prix, despite acknowledging there is still work to be done on the car's power unit and downforce.

The Fiona Stanley Hospital in Perth, Australia, faced severe issues with improperly sanitized medical instruments containing blood and bone fragments, leading to the removal of its medical service provider Serco and a fine of $60,000. The hospital's reputation and staff morale are further damaged by these incidents, following other controversies like a patient's death.

Becca Litchfield and Dale, from Nottingham, sacrificed their dream wedding to fund one last round of IVF, which resulted in them giving birth to twins, Darci-Mai and Stanley. After two failed IVF attempts, they won a wedding competition, allowing them to finally get married.

A family-friendly coffee shop in Omaha, Scooter's Coffee, had its Facebook page hacked and used to post pornography for nearly 24 hours after an employee clicked a malicious link. The page was locked and taken over by an unknown third party, who posted adult content similar to breaches of other major brands. Scooter's managed to regain control with help from other businesses after struggling to contact Facebook.

A Shibu Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club center attempted to bark but only managed high-pitched squeaks and yaps, amusing onlookers and handlers who recorded the humorous interaction. The video shows the puppy trying to communicate with a husky, both dogs making various vocal sounds, while passers-by laughed and mimicked their actions. Canine vocalization typically develops from grunts and whines to barks by around seven to eight weeks, but some puppies, like this Shibu Inu, may take longer.

Liam Plunkett, a 29-year-old England seamer, aims to challenge West Indies' batsmen with his pace in the upcoming Test series. Recovered from an ankle injury, Plunkett seeks to prove himself, competing with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood for a spot. He emphasizes his adaptability and willingness to disrupt batters, despite facing strong competition.

Paul Smith is set to face reigning super-middleweight champion Andre Ward in a non-title fight, possibly as a warm-up for a potential rematch with Carl Froch. Trainer Virgil Hunter confirms the match is a "done deal," though it won't be for a title belt. Meanwhile, Froch aims for a Las Vegas Strip appearance against Julio Cesar Chavez Jr., while the WBA orders Ward and Froch to meet in a unification fight.

In Parma, Missouri, the election of the city's first black mayor, Tyrus Byrd, was overshadowed by the resignations of five of the six police officers, the city attorney, clerk, and water treatment supervisor, who cited safety concerns. The outgoing mayor, Randall Ramsey, and Byrd's father, Simon Wofford, have no explanation for the resignations, and residents question the need for such a large police force for a town of 713 people.

Manchester City will make Yaya Toure available for transfer this summer, despite his commitment to the club, as they look to reshape their squad. Toure, who has played a key role in City's recent successes, is unlikely to move due to his high wages, though Inter Milan is interested. Meanwhile, City will not allow Valencia to pull out of a £24 million deal for Alvaro Negredo, who has struggled at Valencia after scoring 23 goals for City last season.

A new study found that more than two-thirds of people taking antidepressants in the U.S. did not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder, with 38% not meeting criteria for other psychiatric conditions like OCD or anxiety. SSRIs, the most common type of antidepressant, are often prescribed without clear evidence-based indications.

Doris Fuller's daughter, Natalie, 28, with bipolar disorder and psychosis, killed herself in Baltimore last month. Fuller, writing in the Washington Post, described how her daughter's condition worsened over years, despite treatment, and led to her suicide. Fuller praised Natalie as the bravest person she knew, noting her struggles with terrifying voices that told her to hurt herself.

A 10-year-old boy named Koby Hodder suffered a cardiac arrest during a game of British Bulldog at school, collapsing for 12 minutes before being revived by CPR and defibrillation. The incident, similar to that of footballer Fabrice Muamba, has prompted teachers to call for the game's ban due to its perceived danger. Koby's father was notified and arrived to find Koby lifeless, but paramedics successfully resuscitated him.

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain's most senior female judge, proposed changes to divorce laws in England and Wales to remove the need for allegations of adultery or blame, aiming to reduce bitterness in matrimonial disputes. She suggested a one-year 'cooling off' period for couples to resolve child and financial arrangements before finalizing a divorce.

Tottenham Hotspur are considering a new £400 million stadium with a retractable pitch to accommodate a potential NFL franchise, due to be completed for the 2018-19 season. The stadium, with a capacity of 65,000, could include extra-large changing rooms and an NFL-style synthetic surface, providing an advantage over Wembley's 90,000 seats and logistical challenges.

U.S. senators have written to FIFA, urging the organization to remove Russia as the host of the 2018 World Cup due to its involvement in the Ukraine crisis. The letter, signed by 13 senators including Robert Menendez and Ron Johnson, calls for economic sanctions and condemnation of the Putin regime. England is considering a bid for Euro 2028 but is unlikely to bid for the 2026 World Cup while Sepp Blatter remains FIFA president.

Universal announced that the sequel to "Fifty Shades of Grey" will be released on February 10, 2017, and the third film on February 9, 2018. EL James's husband, Niall Leonard, will write the script for the second film. The first sequel earned $568.8 million worldwide, leading to negotiations for higher salaries for Dakota Johnson and Jamie Dornan.

Tony Pulis, manager of West Brom, faces another relegation battle despite his past successes in keeping teams in the Premier League. His record is one of the worst among long-serving managers, with never finishing in the top half of the table in seven seasons. West Brom's upcoming fixtures against top teams like Liverpool and Manchester United add to the pressure, while Pulis's expertise and past achievements are acknowledged but not reflected in his current poor standing.

Fenerbahce called for the suspension of the Turkish championship after their team bus was attacked by armed gunmen on its way from Rize to Trabzon, with the bus driver wounded and the vehicle damaged. The club stated that finding and punishing the culprits is vital, while players expressed relief and concern for the driver's well-being.

A massive avalanche struck Everest Base Camp, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens more after a strong earthquake in Nepal. The disaster stranded hundreds of climbers and local workers at higher camps, complicating rescue efforts due to dangerous aftershocks and the treacherous Khumbu Icefall. Helicopters rescued some climbers but many remain trapped.

Gregory Margolin, an 87-year-old Jewish war veteran who fought in World War II, survived another war in Ukraine when a missile hit his home, killing his daughter. He and his family moved to Israel for safety, joining 600 other Ukrainian Jews brought there by the International Fellowship of Christians and Jews since the conflict began.

John Carver, assistant manager at Newcastle, recalls how Ruud Gullit's decision to bench key players Alan Shearer and Duncan Ferguson during a 1999 Tyne-Wear derby led to Gullit's dismissal after a 2-1 loss to Sunderland. Carver, now fighting for the head coach position, knows the impact a victory or defeat in Sunday's derby could have on his future with the club.

Reverend Al Sharpton appeared in North Charleston to address a vigil for Walter Scott, a black driver fatally shot by a white police officer. During a sermon at Charity Missionary Baptist Church, Sharpton discussed the need for policing reform and credited Mayor Keith Summey for firing the officer involved. Sharpton is also expected to attend a vigil near the shooting site.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers will speak to Raheem Sterling about his recent controversial behavior, including inhaling nitrous oxide and smoking a shisha pipe, after Sterling scored the opening goal in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United. Rodgers emphasized the importance of being a top-class professional both on and off the field.

During the second week of the election campaign, Labour received over £1 every second from trades unions, totaling £1.1 million, compared to the Conservatives' £492,512. Key unions like Unison and Unite donated significantly, while the Liberal Democrats and UKIP received much less. Critics argue this union support indicates Labour's policies will cater to union demands.

Passengers on a Qatar Airways flight from Birmingham to Doha revolted after being stranded for five hours on the tarmac due to severe winds. Police were called twice to the aircraft in Birmingham and Manchester. The passengers were eventually bused to Manchester, where they faced further delays. Qatar Airways apologized for the delay, citing weather conditions and crew legal flying hours.

Justin Bieber will accompany Floyd Mayweather into the ring for his $300 million fight against Manny Pacquiao, following their long-standing friendship. Bieber confirmed his role in a video, leading Mayweather's entourage at the MGM Grand. The fight is considered the biggest in boxing history, with Mayweather aiming for a 47-0 record.

Corinthian Colleges Inc., a for-profit college chain, announced the closure of its 28 campuses, marking a significant step in holding such institutions accountable. Corinthian, which once enrolled over 70,000 students, faced curtailment of federal student aid and high student loan default rates. The U.S. Department of Education is considering loan forgiveness for Corinthian graduates and is pushing to close other for-profit colleges, aiming to address the issue of dubious degrees and high debt among students.

Pep Guardiola denied a dispute with former Bayern Munich doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit after blaming the medical staff for the 3-1 Champions League defeat by Porto. Guardiola took responsibility for the loss, stating it was his decision to field an injured squad. Muller-Wohlfahrt, a 72-year-old long-time club doctor, cited damage to the bond of trust as his reason for leaving.

Wladimir Klitschko, 39, reminisces about his Olympic gold win in 1996 that changed his life, and prepares for his world title defense against Bryant Jennings at Madison Square Garden. Klitschko, who became heavyweight champion in 2000, believes age is an advantage and is eager for the fight, noting his recent sparring partners are younger than him.

Jeremy Clarkson, 54, admitted he would miss fronting Top Gear after being fired in March for attacking a producer. Former presenter Angela Rippon, 70, expressed interest in returning to the show. Clarkson's sacking followed an internal investigation that found he had physically assaulted a producer and verbally abused him during a dispute over food. The future of the show remains uncertain as BBC attempts to retain co-presenters James May and Richard Hammond.

In a La Liga match, Barcelona defeated Celta Vigo 1-0, with Celta's Fabian Orellana receiving a red card for throwing a lump of grass at Sergio Busquets, who appeared to be struck on the neck. The incident occurred during the closing stages of the match, and Orellana was sent off as Barcelona secured a crucial victory.

In 2013, a bombing at the Boston Marathon killed three and injured over 200. In 2015, federal Judge George A. O'Toole warned the jury sentencing Dzhokhar Tsarnaev for the bombings not to attend the marathon or related events, as the trial's sentencing phase begins on April 21. Tsarnaev was convicted on all 30 charges, including using weapons of mass destruction, and faces the possibility of the death penalty.

Tens of millions of Chinese people marked the Tomb Sweeping Festival by traveling to ancestral villages to clean tombs, burn paper money, and offer food and drink. A grand ceremony honoring the Yellow Emperor Huangdi was held in Shaanxi Province, with thousands of people attending. The festival, also known as Qingming, celebrates the start of spring and involves outdoor celebrations and traditional dances.

Paul Simon, 73, topped the UK album charts with "The Ultimate Collection," outselling albums by younger artists like Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. This is his first UK chart-topping album since 1990. Simon's recent tour with Sting likely contributed to the album's success.

Iker Casillas, Real Madrid's goalkeeper, insists he will stay and fight for his position despite potential competition from Manchester United's David de Gea. Casillas, who has been with Real Madrid since 1996, hopes to fulfill his contract and remains committed to helping the team defend their Champions League title.

Britain's employment reached a record 31 million, with 557,000 more jobs in the three months to February compared to the same period last year. The International Monetary Fund and German finance minister praised Chancellor George Osborne's economic strategy, reducing the deficit from £153 billion to £90 billion and creating more jobs than the rest of the EU combined in the last five years.

SsangYong is launching the Tivoli SUV in the UK starting from £12,950, aiming to compete with the Nissan Juke. The vehicle comes in three trim levels with various features and options, and SsangYong expects it to boost the company's UK sales from 2,000 to 4,000 annually.

Chef Sam Longhurst at Splendid Kitchen in Manchester created a 10-inch, 2,000-calorie burger called "The Whole Damn Farm," featuring six forms of three different meats, for a customer's challenge. The burger, priced at £13.50, includes two beef patties, bacon jam, ham, a fried chicken thigh, barbecued pulled pork, and bacon, totaling the equivalent of six Big Macs.

Yeo Valley's staff canteen, located at the company's headquarters in Blagdon, North Somerset, offers high-quality, Michelin-starred meals made from organic and locally sourced ingredients for as little as £2. The canteen, praised as the world's best staff canteen, has now opened to the public at higher prices.

B.B. King, the legendary blues musician, was hospitalized for dehydration caused by his Type II diabetes but has since returned home, feeling much better, to spend time with his grandchildren. He is known for his hits like "The Thrill Is Gone" and has been inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

On Easter Sunday, New York's Fifth Avenue hosted an Easter parade featuring a wide array of bizarre and colorful hats, with participants ranging from churchgoers to those celebrating in more secular ways, all walking through the streets adorned with creative headgear like ship-shaped hats, butterfly headpieces, and elaborate dioramas.

The East of England ambulance service received 1,248 inappropriate calls in two years, with front-line crews responding to half of them, potentially affecting emergency response times. Notable calls included a squirrel being run over, a man reporting a bleeding burger, and a woman claiming to have eaten too much takeaway. Gary Morgan, Regional Head of Emergency Operations Centres, urged people to use common sense when calling 999.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake won a series of challenges against Loic Remy and Willian in Audi's football challenge, despite Willian accidentally breaking a car's wing mirror during the long-range shooting.

Brendan Rodgers criticizes Raheem Sterling's advisor for potentially manipulating the player, stating Sterling would stay at Liverpool if left to decide alone. Rodgers had a conversation with Sterling, advising him to stay despite rejecting a £100,000-a-week contract and having two years left on his deal. Rodgers emphasizes that Liverpool is the best place for Sterling's development both football-wise and financially.

On a recent episode of Countdown, co-presenter Rachel Riley was embarrassed when contestants used the word 'erection' in a word game, causing host Nick Hewer to struggle to suppress his laughter. This incident is part of a recurring pattern where rude words have caused hosts to react awkwardly, including previous instances with Carol Vorderman and other presenters.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, who tried to buy deadly poison on the dark web to commit suicide was spared jail after pleading guilty. He was arrested during a counter-terrorism operation and officers found he had expressed interest in buying the poison and suggested future purchases. He was sentenced to a 12-month referral order.

Lianne Hindle, 37, died of a cardiac arrest three hours after giving birth to her daughter Poppy at North Manchester General Hospital in December, just months after several other deaths at the same and another local hospital prompted an investigation. Her partner, Chris Barnes, is calling for action to prevent further tragedies, expressing concerns about the care she received, particularly noting she was left alone with a student midwife after the birth.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after being seen training while eight months pregnant. Pittman, a two-time world champion hurdler, continued training throughout her pregnancy and plans to compete in the Beijing World Championships and the 2016 Rio Olympics. Her coach praised her careful management of the training program.

A powerful storm capsized several sailboats during a regatta in Mobile Bay, Alabama, resulting in at least one death and multiple missing persons. The storm hit around 4 p.m., and the Coast Guard rescued one person by 9 p.m., vowing to continue searches through the night. Over 100 sailboats and about 200 people were participating in the Dauphin Island regatta.

Roseanne Barr revealed she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma, which are progressively worsening her vision. Her doctors have not provided a timeline, and there is no cure for these conditions, though treatments can delay progression.

A 17-year-old named Chancey Allen Luna was convicted of first-degree murder in the 2013 shooting death of Australian college baseball player Christopher Lane, who was jogging in Duncan, Oklahoma. The jury recommended a life sentence without parole. Luna's defense argued he only meant to scare Lane, but the jury found him guilty, with Luna remaining stoic during the verdict and later apologizing to reporters.

Arsene Wenger, Arsenal's manager, insists his poor record against Jose Mourinho will not affect the upcoming match between Arsenal and Chelsea. Wenger, who has lost 7 out of 12 games against Mourinho, says the result will depend on the performance on the day. The match, scheduled for 4pm, is part of the Barclays Premier League, with Chelsea currently leading by 10 points.

Manny Pacquiao, a Filipino boxer who rose from poverty to become a global sports icon, is set to face Floyd Mayweather in the "Fight of the Century" at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. These upcoming fights follow a career marked by significant victories against notable opponents like Oscar De La Hoya and Juan Manuel Marquez. Early photos show Pacquiao training in a Manila boxing gym at age 17, highlighting his journey to becoming one of the most recognizable names in boxing.

Jack Grealish, an outstanding Aston Villa player who starred in their FA Cup win over Liverpool, was photographed using nitrous oxide, a drug that can impair athletic performance. This incident highlights the ongoing challenge of maintaining discipline among top athletes, despite efforts by some clubs to promote a professional lifestyle focused on health and performance.

Sam Barton, who spent £55,000 on cosmetic surgery to resemble Joey Essex, was attacked on Easter Monday when a group of men pelted him with eggs after he checked into a pub on Facebook. Barton, who has also accumulated significant debts and debts from credit cards, believes the attackers targeted him based on his online presence and appearance.

Manchester University in Indiana was placed on lockdown late on Friday night after receiving a 'likely prank call' about an armed person near the administration building. Police, a bomb squad, and Indiana State Police responded but decided it was a prank. Students were advised to barricade themselves in rooms and stay silent. No injuries were reported, and the university had not given an all-clear by 2am.

Edinson Cavani, known as "El Matador," faces Luis Suarez in a crucial Champions League match between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona at Parc des Princes. Cavani, without key players Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Marco Veratti, must perform well to help PSG advance, though he has struggled with a goal drought recently.

Derry Mathews won the interim WBA lightweight title with a unanimous points decision over Tony Luis in Liverpool. Luis, drafted in at the last minute, showed aggression but Mathews controlled the fight, winning 114-112, 114-112, 115-112. Mathews faced challenges in the later rounds but ultimately secured the title.

Hull recorded a surprising 28-20 victory over St Helens at Langtree Park, ending St Helens' three-game winning streak. Hull took an early lead through Jamie Shaul's try, but St Helens responded with tries from Tommy Makinson and Louie McCarthy-Scarsbrook. Hull held on to secure the win, despite St Helens' efforts to regain the lead.

The U.S. immigrant population, including both documented and undocumented immigrants, could reach a record high of 51 million by 2023, accounting for 14.8% of the total population, according to a report from the Center for Immigration Studies. By 2060, immigrants could make up 82% of U.S. population growth and reach 78 million, or 18.8% of the total population. This growth is expected to accelerate, with immigrants accounting for three-quarters of U.S. population growth by 2050.

Jack Wilshere captained Arsenal Under 21s in a 1-0 loss to Reading's U21s at the Emirates Stadium. Martin Keown's son Niall scored the winning goal in the 8th minute, while Wilshere and Abou Diaby returned from injury without further issues.

Justin Rose, who has been in the world's top five for the past three years, fell outside the top 10 after a poor performance in Florida. After two weeks of practice, Rose improved, scoring 69 in the first round of the Shell Houston Open, showing signs of returning to form in time for the Masters.

A mansion in Mayfair, London, built on the site of a former 19th-century milking parlour, is on the market for £25 million. The four-bedroom property features modern luxuries like an indoor pool, gym, and cinema room. Originally used for agricultural trade, the site was a depot before being demolished in the 19th century and rebuilt as a lavish home in 2011.

Bayern Munich, without several key players due to injuries, believes their unity is stronger and will help them in their Champions League quarter-final against Porto, according to Thomas Muller. Bayern has performed well in recent matches despite the absences, and coach Pep Guardiola is optimistic about their chances in the tournament.

Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited Mercedes' Brackley base to strategize against Ferrari after Sebastian Vettel's victory in the Malaysian Grand Prix. Hamilton and Rosberg, who finished third, are determined to beat Vettel in the upcoming Chinese Grand Prix. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff expressed concern over Ferrari's performance and acknowledged the need to analyze their strategy.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to use nitrogen gas for executions if lethal injection becomes unavailable, stating it would be humane and quick. The bill was passed in response to issues with lethal injections and while the state's executions are on hold pending Supreme Court review.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in Swansea's 3-1 win over Hull, topping this week's EA Sports' Performance Index with a score of 52.9. Other top performers include Charlie Austin (52.2) and Eden Hazard (51.7) after notable contributions in their respective matches.

A Russian freezer trawler called the Dalny Vostok sank in the Sea of Okhotsk, killing at least 56 of its 132 crew members. A massive rescue operation involving over 1,300 people is underway, with 63 survivors rescued and 13 still missing. The ship sank in 15 minutes after pulling in an 80-ton fishing net, flooding its engine compartment. Temperatures in the water can dip to -2 degrees Celsius, complicating rescue efforts.

Clinical trials show that olaparib, a drug originally for women with breast cancer, can benefit men with advanced prostate cancer, particularly those with DNA defects in their tumors. Out of 49 men tested, 16 responded positively, with the drug delaying disease progression and improving scan responses. This makes olaparib the first cancer drug to target inherited genetic mutations in prostate cancer.

Rhiannon Taylor, a 29-year-old travel photographer from Australia, turned her passion into a business by reviewing and photographing the world's most luxurious accommodations. With over 12,000 Instagram followers, she documents her travels, stays, and experiences on her website 'In Bed With', generating income from hotel reviews, professional photos, and partnerships with travel product companies.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was killed after getting caught in a fight between two adult hippos in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park, South Africa. The calf's mother watched helplessly as the baby was thrown into the air and dragged along the water's surface, dying hours later from its injuries. A tour operator described how the mother initially kept her distance from the fight, believing it safer for her calf, but was unable to save it when one of the adult hippos grabbed and injured the baby.

The Football Association contacted QPR and Chelsea after a fan threw a cigarette lighter at Branislav Ivanovic during Chelsea's 1-0 victory at Loftus Road. QPR is reviewing CCTV footage and appealing for witnesses to identify the culprit, who could face a stadium ban.

A young mother, LaTasha Gosling, and her three children were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. The suspect, known to the family, was found dead hours later; his six-month-old baby was unharmed. The family has started a GoFundMe page to raise money for funeral services, having already exceeded their initial goal.

Emily Thornberry, a Labour politician, faced criticism for opposing the right to buy policy while renting out a property she bought from a housing association for nearly £1 million. Her tweet of a house with English flags and a white van sparked controversy, and she lost her frontbench job. Thornberry lives in a £3 million Victorian townhouse in London.

Police have dropped an investigation into a violent assault on Mike Lane, the joint master of the Tedworth Hunt, despite having a video and other evidence. The attack, which left Lane with concussion and broken teeth, was carried out by balaclava-clad protesters armed with iron bars. Wiltshire Police have stopped the inquiry pending further information, angering hunt supporters and Lane himself, who feels let down by the police response.
Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes insists he will stay at the club this summer, despite links to Manchester United and Chelsea, saying he is happy with his current form and position in La Liga.

An Australian teenager, Audrey Pekin, was raped twice on Christmas Eve in Bali by a man named Henry Alafu, who lured her to his home and then followed her in a taxi. Indonesian police allowed Alafu to escape back to Nigeria.

Ashley James, a former Made In Chelsea star, has joined PETA in an anti-fur campaign against Harvey Nichols, which recently reintroduced fur products after a decade-long ban. The campaign features a fake skinned fox and aims to raise awareness about the cruelty of the fur industry. Harvey Nichols claims to source fur responsibly, but PETA's undercover investigation suggests otherwise.

Chile's President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law allowing civil unions for same-sex couples, which will take effect in six months. The law aims to provide legal rights in areas such as property, health care, pensions, and inheritance, benefiting an estimated 2 million people. This move aligns Chile with several South American countries that have recently recognized same-sex civil unions, though marriage equality is only legal in Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay.

Chelsea have led the Premier League table for 230 days, on course to break Manchester United's record of 262 days set in 1993/94. Chelsea currently lead by seven points with a game in hand, and could surpass the record by 12 days if they remain top until the end of the season.

Cape Verde, a country of 500,000 people, is leveraging its rich musical heritage to boost its economy, which lacks conventional natural resources. The government, including Prime Minister Jose Maria Neves, recognizes the potential of the music and arts sector. The Kriol Jazz Festival, now in its seventh year, has attracted international artists and boosted tourism, indicating the growing importance of music in the country's economic development.

A hoax video of a wave rider surfing in front of Sydney's Opera House resurfaced on social media, going viral again after heavy storms. The video, originally posted in 2012, was shared by radio hosts Fitzy and Wippa and quickly spread. Wave experts dismissed the video as impossible, citing the physical impossibility of waves breaking that far inside the harbor.

Reading lost to Birmingham 1-0 in a Championship match at the Madejski Stadium, despite dominating much of the game. Clayton Donaldson scored the winning goal for Birmingham in the 89th minute. Reading had previously lost in the FA Cup semi-finals to Arsenal.

David Luiz, a key defender for Paris Saint-Germain, injured his hamstring during a match against Marseille and will miss at least four weeks, including both legs of the Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona.

The return of Game of Thrones has led to a significant surge in internet piracy, with over 100,000 illegal downloads per day and seven million episodes illegally downloaded between February and April. This represents a 45% increase year-on-year. Brazil was the top country for illegal downloads, followed by France, the US, Canada, and the UK. HBO has responded by launching a new streaming service, HBO Now, in an attempt to curb piracy and protect its business model.

Leicester City and West Ham United will face off in a Premier League match at King Power Stadium on Saturday at 3pm. Key team news includes Matt Upson's absence for Leicester and Winston Reid's return for West Ham. Betting odds favor West Ham, and key stats show West Ham's recent strong performance against Leicester, while Leicester struggles at home.

In Celoron, New York, a statue of Lucile Ball unveiled in 2009 has been met with widespread criticism, with a Facebook page garnering over 600 likes calling for its removal. The statue, based on Ball's intoxicated pitch for a health tonic, is described as unflattering and monstrous. Estimated to cost $8,000 to $10,000 to recast, the artist, Dave Poulin, has declined to comment on the controversy.

Sharon Smith, a 43-year-old from Halesowen, lost nearly half her body weight, dropping from over 20 stone to 9st 9lb, after being forced to stand for an 11-hour flight due to concerns about crushing the passenger next to her. This experience, combined with joining a slimming club and taking up running, led to her significant weight loss and improved health, allowing her to run a 10k race.

Nicola Bonn, a 34-year-old London mother, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences and advice as a new mother to help other mothers feel less clueless. Her viral post, "Why We Need to Stop Justifying Ourselves," addresses the overwhelming opinions and judgments new mothers face, highlighting common criticisms about feeding, sleeping, and parenting choices for her baby Poppy.

The families of two 17-year-old British boys, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, are worried about their sons who are believed to have traveled to Syria to join ISIS. Both families are in shock and are trying to locate their sons, who have not been in contact for several days. Hassan is related to Hammaad Munshi, who was previously convicted for a plot to murder non-Muslims in 2006. British authorities are investigating and urging the public to provide any information.

Stephanie Scott, a school teacher from Leeton, was murdered just days before her wedding, leaving her fiancé Aaron Leeson-Woolley devastated. Her body was found in bushland on Easter Friday, days after she went missing on Easter Sunday. The couple had planned a wedding at Eat Your Greens venue, with a guest list of 120 people. Her father, Robert Scott, expressed the pain of losing her at a time when she had so much to look forward to, including her wedding.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is interested in signing Feyenoord players Tonny Vilhena and Jordy Clasie, both Dutch internationals, as the club aims to qualify for European competition. Vilhena, 20, has one year left on his contract and is eager to leave Feyenoord for the Premier League. Clasie, valued at £10 million, has also been monitored by Southampton.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library at Ickworth House in Suffolk, sparking controversy among heritage experts. The move, part of an experiment at nine other sites, aims to encourage visitors to engage more deeply with the space but has been criticized as patronizing. The National Trust says the experiment is short-term and part of efforts to enhance visitor experience.
